sec01-card-f01.front: What credential must a Nebraska resident hold to drive a motor vehicle on state streets or highways?
sec01-card-f01.expected_back: A Nebraska resident needs a license to drive a motor vehicle on the state’s streets or highways.

sec01-card-f02.front: How soon must a new resident holding a valid license from another state get Nebraska licensing?
sec01-card-f02.expected_back: A newly arrived resident who holds a valid license from another state must obtain Nebraska licensing within thirty days.

sec01-card-f03.front: Why does Nebraska phase in teen driving privileges in stages through its graduated licensing system?
sec01-card-f03.expected_back: Nebraska’s graduated licensing system introduces driving privileges in stages to limit high-risk situations while teenagers gain experience.

sec01-card-f04.front: When do graduated-license restrictions forbid using an interactive wireless device?
sec01-card-f04.expected_back: Graduated-license restrictions prohibit using an interactive wireless device while the vehicle is moving.

sec01-card-f05.front: Who must wear a seat belt inside a vehicle operated by a permit holder?
sec01-card-f05.expected_back: Everyone in a vehicle driven by a permit holder must use a seat belt.

sec01-card-f06.front: Which passengers may a school-permit holder carry to the school that driver attends?
sec01-card-f06.expected_back: A school-permit holder may transport only household family members to the school that the holder attends.

sec01-card-f07.front: During the first six months, how many non-immediate-family passengers under nineteen may a provisional-permit driver carry?
sec01-card-f07.expected_back: For the first six months, a provisional-permit driver may carry at most one non-immediate-family passenger who is younger than nineteen.

sec01-card-f08.front: Which two travel purposes are exempt from the midnight-to-six-in-the-morning limit for provisional-permit drivers?
sec01-card-f08.expected_back: The graduated restrictions list school-activity and work travel as exceptions to the midnight-to-six-a.m. limit for provisional-permit drivers.

sec01-card-f09.front: What can happen to your license if you break a driving restriction?
sec01-card-f09.expected_back: Breaking a driving restriction can lead to license suspension or revocation.

sec01-card-f10.front: What must a driver under twenty-one do after earning six or more points within one year?
sec01-card-f10.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one who earns at least six points in a year must complete driver improvement within three months.

sec01-card-f11.front: What driving goal does the school learner permit allow an eligible student to practice toward?
sec01-card-f11.expected_back: The school learner permit lets an eligible student practice driving toward a school permit.

sec01-card-f12.front: What is the minimum age for a school learner permit, and can an applicant apply early?
sec01-card-f12.expected_back: A school learner permit applicant must be at least fourteen and cannot apply before that birthday.

sec01-card-f13.front: Who must sit beside a school learner driving a passenger car?
sec01-card-f13.expected_back: A passenger-car school learner must have an adjacent supervising driver aged at least twenty-one who is licensed in Nebraska or another state.

sec01-card-f14.front: Which two tests are required to get a school learner permit?
sec01-card-f14.expected_back: The school learner permit requires vision and written testing.

sec01-card-f15.front: How long does a school learner permit stay valid after it is issued?
sec01-card-f15.expected_back: A school learner permit lasts for six months after issuance.

sec01-card-f16.front: How does a school-permit applicant meet the city-population geographic requirement?
sec01-card-f16.expected_back: A school-permit applicant satisfies the geographic condition by living outside a city of five thousand or more people or attending school outside such a city.

sec01-card-f17.front: Where and how may a school-permit driver travel without a supervising adult?
sec01-card-f17.expected_back: A school-permit driver may travel unsupervised by the nearest direct accessible route between home and the attended school or its activity property for scheduled school purposes.

sec01-card-f18.front: When may a school-permit holder drive outside solo school routes?
sec01-card-f18.expected_back: A school-permit holder may drive at any time when accompanied by a licensed driver who is at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-f19.front: What is the exact minimum age to apply for a Nebraska school permit?
sec01-card-f19.expected_back: A school-permit applicant must be at least fourteen years and two months old.

sec01-card-f20.front: How long must an applicant hold a school learner permit or learner permit before applying for a school permit?
sec01-card-f20.expected_back: Before applying for a school permit, an applicant must have held a school learner permit or learner permit for at least two months.

sec01-card-f21.front: Besides logging fifty practice hours, what course option qualifies an applicant for a school permit?
sec01-card-f21.expected_back: One route to a school permit is successful completion of a Nebraska driver-safety course approved by the DMV.

sec01-card-f22.front: How many certified driving hours and whose signature are needed on the supervised-practice route to a school permit?
sec01-card-f22.expected_back: The supervised-practice route to a school permit requires certification of fifty driving hours, signed by a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-f23.front: How many of the certified school-permit practice hours must take place between sunset and sunrise?
sec01-card-f23.expected_back: The school-permit practice certification must include at least ten hours driven between sunset and sunrise.

sec01-card-f24.front: Which tests are waived for a school-permit applicant who finishes a Nebraska DMV-approved driver-safety course?
sec01-card-f24.expected_back: For a school-permit applicant, completing a Nebraska DMV-approved driver-safety course waives the written and drive tests.

sec01-card-f25.front: Which two tests must a school-permit applicant still take when qualifying through the fifty-hour practice certification?
sec01-card-f25.expected_back: School-permit applicants using the practice certification still need vision and drive testing.

sec01-card-f26.front: When is the written test waived for a school-permit applicant using the fifty-hour practice certification?
sec01-card-f26.expected_back: For a school-permit applicant using practice certification, a valid school learner or learner permit, or one expired no longer than a year, waives the written test.

sec01-card-f27.front: What safety restraint rule applies to every occupant riding with a school-permit driver?
sec01-card-f27.expected_back: Every occupant riding with a school-permit driver must be secured by an occupant-protection system.

sec01-card-f28.front: At what exact age does a Nebraska school permit expire?
sec01-card-f28.expected_back: A school permit expires when its holder reaches sixteen years and three months.

sec01-card-f29.front: Which future credentials does a standard learner permit allow you to practice driving toward?
sec01-card-f29.expected_back: The learner permit permits legal driving practice toward a provisional permit or operator license.

sec01-card-f30.front: How early may you apply for a learner permit, and what is the minimum age for issuance?
sec01-card-f30.expected_back: A learner permit may be applied for sixty days before the fifteenth birthday, but cannot be issued until age fifteen.

sec01-card-f31.front: What penalties apply to a first wireless-device violation under graduated-license restrictions?
sec01-card-f31.expected_back: A first graduated-license wireless-device violation carries a two-hundred-dollar fine and license points.

sec01-card-f32.front: What dollar fine applies to a seat-belt violation under Nebraska graduated-license restrictions?
sec01-card-f32.expected_back: A seat-belt violation under the graduated restrictions carries a twenty-five-dollar fine.

sec01-card-f33.front: How many driving-record points come from breaking a graduated-permit passenger restriction?
sec01-card-f33.expected_back: A graduated-permit passenger restriction violation carries one point on the driving record.

sec01-card-f34.front: How many points are added to your driving record for a provisional-permit nighttime-driving violation?
sec01-card-f34.expected_back: A provisional-permit nighttime-driving violation carries one point on the driving record.

sec01-card-f35.front: What happens to the permit or license on a first under-twenty-one zero-tolerance offense?
sec01-card-f35.expected_back: A first under-twenty-one zero-tolerance offense results in the court holding the permit or license for thirty days.

sec01-card-f36.front: What law applies when a driver younger than twenty-one has a BAC of zero point zero eight or higher?
sec01-card-f36.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one with a BAC of at least zero point zero eight is subject to the same DWI laws as an adult driver.

sec01-card-f37.front: What underlying permit standards must every school learner permit applicant already satisfy?
sec01-card-f37.expected_back: A school learner permit applicant must be eligible for a school permit and satisfy all school-permit criteria.

sec01-card-f38.front: What must an applicant bring if they finished the safety course before being old enough for a school learner permit?
sec01-card-f38.expected_back: An applicant who was not old enough for a school learner permit when completing the safety course must present the school’s paper waiver when applying for the school permit.

sec01-card-r01.front: Who must occupy the seat next to a passenger-car learner-permit driver?
sec01-card-r01.expected_back: A passenger-car learner-permit holder needs a licensed driver aged at least twenty-one in the adjacent seat.

sec01-card-r02.front: Which prior permits waive the learner-permit written test if valid or expired no more than one year?
sec01-card-r02.expected_back: The learner-permit written test is waived after issuance of a school learner, school or learner permit that is valid or expired no longer than a year.

sec01-card-r03.front: How long after issuance does a standard Nebraska learner permit expire?
sec01-card-r03.expected_back: The learner permit expires a year after it is issued.

sec01-card-r04.front: During which daily hours may a provisional-permit holder drive unsupervised for any purpose?
sec01-card-r04.expected_back: A provisional-permit holder may drive without supervision from six a.m. until midnight.

sec01-card-r05.front: Which unsupervised trips are allowed on a provisional permit between midnight and six in the morning?
sec01-card-r05.expected_back: Unsupervised provisional driving between midnight and six a.m. is limited to trips between home and work or a school activity.

sec01-card-r06.front: Who must accompany a provisional driver to allow driving at any hour of the day or night?
sec01-card-r06.expected_back: A provisional driver may drive at any time with an accompanying parent, guardian or licensed driver who is at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-r07.front: When can you start applying for a provisional permit, and when can it be issued?
sec01-card-r07.expected_back: A provisional permit cannot be issued before the sixteenth birthday, although application may start sixty days earlier.

sec01-card-r08.front: How long must an applicant hold a qualifying permit before applying for a provisional permit?
sec01-card-r08.expected_back: Before a provisional-permit application, a school learner, school or learner permit must have been held for at least six months.

sec01-card-r09.front: What point-record standard must a provisional-permit applicant meet over the six months right before applying?
sec01-card-r09.expected_back: A provisional applicant must have fewer than three points accumulated during the six months immediately before applying.

sec01-card-r10.front: What certified driving hours and signature are required on the practice route to a provisional permit?
sec01-card-r10.expected_back: The provisional-permit practice route requires certification of fifty driving hours, including ten between sunset and sunrise, signed by a parent, guardian or licensed driver aged at least twenty-one.

sec01-card-r11.front: Which provisional-permit tests are waived by completing a DMV-approved Nebraska driver-safety course?
sec01-card-r11.expected_back: A DMV-approved Nebraska driver-safety course waives the provisional written and drive tests.

sec01-card-r12.front: Which tests apply to a provisional applicant using practice certification, and what waives the written test?
sec01-card-r12.expected_back: A provisional applicant using practice certification needs vision and drive tests, with the written test waived for a learner permit valid or expired no longer than a year.

sec01-card-r13.front: What restraint requirement applies to every person riding with a provisional-permit driver?
sec01-card-r13.expected_back: Every person riding with a provisional-permit driver must use an occupant-protection system.

sec01-card-r14.front: On which birthday does a Nebraska provisional permit expire?
sec01-card-r14.expected_back: A provisional permit expires on the holder’s eighteenth birthday.

sec01-card-r15.front: Which vehicles does a Class O license cover, and which two categories does it exclude?
sec01-card-r15.expected_back: A Class O license authorizes noncommercial motor vehicles, including mopeds, autocycles, all-terrain vehicles and utility-terrain vehicles, but excludes motorcycles and commercial motor vehicles.

sec01-card-r16.front: Can an applicant use an autocycle to take the Class O drive test?
sec01-card-r16.expected_back: An autocycle cannot be used for the Class O drive test.

sec01-card-r17.front: What is the earliest age a driver can qualify for a Nebraska operator license?
sec01-card-r17.expected_back: The minimum age for an operator license is seventeen.

sec01-card-r18.front: How does an applicant under eighteen qualify for an operator license?
sec01-card-r18.expected_back: An applicant below age eighteen qualifies for an operator license after holding a provisional permit for at least twelve months with fewer than three points during the previous twelve months.

sec01-card-r19.front: Which tests are waived when an applicant under eighteen qualifies for an operator license through a clean twelve-month provisional record?
sec01-card-r19.expected_back: An operator applicant younger than eighteen receives written- and drive-test waivers after holding a provisional permit for at least twelve months and accumulating fewer than three points during the previous twelve months.

sec01-card-r20.front: Which tests are waived when a provisional holder upgrades to an operator license at ages eighteen through twenty-one?
sec01-card-r20.expected_back: A provisional-permit holder applying for an operator license between ages eighteen and twenty-one receives a waiver of the written and drive tests.

sec01-card-r21.front: Which tests apply to an adult eighteen or older seeking a first operator license without prior provisional status?
sec01-card-r21.expected_back: A first-time operator applicant aged eighteen or older who never held a provisional permit needs vision, written and drive tests, with the written test waived for a learner permit that is valid or expired no more than a year.

sec01-card-r22.front: When does a learner permit waive the written test for a first-time operator applicant aged eighteen or older?
sec01-card-r22.expected_back: For a first-time operator applicant aged at least eighteen, a learner permit valid or expired no longer than a year waives the written test.

sec01-card-r23.front: Which requirements apply to an applicant under eighteen who surrenders a valid out-of-state permit or license?
sec01-card-r23.expected_back: Applicants below age eighteen who surrender a valid out-of-state permit or license must meet provisional-permit requirements.

sec01-card-r24.front: What testing applies when a new resident aged eighteen or older surrenders a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-r24.expected_back: A new resident aged at least eighteen who surrenders a valid out-of-state license needs a vision test, with drive testing left to licensing staff discretion.

sec01-card-r25.front: When must a new Nebraska resident aged eighteen or older take the written test?
sec01-card-r25.expected_back: A new Nebraska resident aged eighteen or older must take the written test if unable to surrender the out-of-state license or if that license has expired.

sec03-card-f01.front: Can one person simultaneously carry a State ID Card alongside a Nebraska driving permit or license?
sec03-card-f01.expected_back: A person cannot simultaneously hold a Nebraska driving permit or license and a state identification card.

sec03-card-f02.front: How long is a Nebraska license or State ID valid for a holder with lawful immigration status?
sec03-card-f02.expected_back: A Nebraska license or State ID Card issued to a person with lawful status is limited to the authorized U.S. stay, or to one year if that stay has no definite end.

sec03-card-f03.front: Will Nebraska issue a license while your driving privileges are suspended or revoked somewhere else?
sec03-card-f03.expected_back: Nebraska will not issue a license while driving privileges are suspended or revoked in any state or jurisdiction.

sec03-card-f04.front: What does a license suspension do to your card and driving privilege?
sec03-card-f04.expected_back: Suspension temporarily removes a person’s valid license and driving privilege.

sec03-card-f05.front: How does license revocation affect your driving privilege and physical card?
sec03-card-f05.expected_back: Revocation removes the driving privilege and takes the license for a specified period.

sec03-card-f06.front: When does a Nebraska license suspension or revocation actually end?
sec03-card-f06.expected_back: A suspension or revocation continues until the driver satisfies reinstatement requirements and pays required fees.

sec03-card-f07.front: What happens to your license and driving privilege during court impoundment?
sec03-card-f07.expected_back: Impoundment means a court holds the license and prohibits driving for the ordered period.

sec03-card-f08.front: What does license confiscation mean during an impaired-driving investigation?
sec03-card-f08.expected_back: Confiscation means an officer seizes the license after an alcohol-test failure or refusal.

sec03-card-f09.front: How many days does the temporary license last after an officer confiscates your plastic card?
sec03-card-f09.expected_back: After confiscation, the issued temporary license lasts fifteen days.

sec03-card-f10.front: What happens when the fifteen-day temporary license ends after an alcohol-test failure or refusal?
sec03-card-f10.expected_back: At the end of the fifteen-day temporary license after alcohol-test failure or refusal, the license is revoked unless a departmental hearing dismisses the violation.

sec03-card-f11.front: How can a motor-vehicle homicide affect your Nebraska driver license?
sec03-card-f11.expected_back: A motor-vehicle homicide can cause loss of a license.

sec03-card-f12.front: What can repeated traffic violations in Nebraska or other states do to your driving privileges?
sec03-card-f12.expected_back: Repeated traffic violations in any state can cause loss of driving privileges.

sec03-card-f13.front: What licensing consequence can follow from using a motor vehicle to commit a crime?
sec03-card-f13.expected_back: Using a vehicle to commit a crime can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f14.front: How can an arrest or conviction for impaired driving under drugs or alcohol impact your license?
sec03-card-f14.expected_back: A drug- or alcohol-impaired-driving arrest or conviction can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f15.front: What can happen if you falsify or hide information on a licensing application?
sec03-card-f15.expected_back: Falsifying or concealing application information can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f16.front: What licensing penalty can hit a driver who leaves a crash without giving a name and address?
sec03-card-f16.expected_back: Leaving a crash without providing a name and address can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f17.front: What can happen to your license if you ignore a court judgment or citation in Nebraska or elsewhere?
sec03-card-f17.expected_back: Ignoring a citation or court judgment in Nebraska or another state can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f18.front: How can alcoholism or drug addiction affect a person's Nebraska driving privileges?
sec03-card-f18.expected_back: Alcoholism or drug addiction can lead to loss of driving privileges.

sec03-card-f19.front: What licensing consequence can result from fleeing an officer to avoid arrest?
sec03-card-f19.expected_back: Flight from an officer to avoid arrest can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f20.front: What can happen to your license if you refuse a chemical test?
sec03-card-f20.expected_back: Refusing a chemical test can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f21.front: Can reckless driving cost you your Nebraska driver license?
sec03-card-f21.expected_back: Reckless driving can lead to loss of the license.

sec03-card-f22.front: What can happen if you lend your driver license to someone else?
sec03-card-f22.expected_back: Lending a driver license to another person can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f23.front: What licensing penalty can follow from having someone else take your licensing test?
sec03-card-f23.expected_back: Having another person take the licensing test can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f24.front: How can a conviction for failing to show proof of insurance affect your license?
sec03-card-f24.expected_back: A conviction for failing to show insurance proof can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f25.front: What non-driving court noncompliance can lead to losing a Nebraska driver license?
sec03-card-f25.expected_back: Failure to comply with a child-support or alimony order can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f26.front: When can a driver under twenty-one lose driving privileges over driver-improvement training?
sec03-card-f26.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one can lose driving privileges for failing to complete required improvement training after accumulating six points in a year.

sec03-card-f27.front: What licensing consequence can strike a driver who transports a child while intoxicated?
sec03-card-f27.expected_back: Transporting a child while intoxicated can lead to license loss.

sec03-card-f28.front: Until what age is a teen barred from getting another permit after violating school learner, school, or learner permit terms?
sec03-card-f28.expected_back: Violating school learner, school or learner permit terms also bars eligibility for another permit until age sixteen.

sec03-card-f29.front: What happens automatically if a driver accumulates twelve points within two years?
sec03-card-f29.expected_back: Accumulating twelve points within two years automatically revokes the operator license for six months.

sec03-card-f30.front: What action does the DMV's point-revocation letter direct the driver to take?
sec03-card-f30.expected_back: The DMV’s point-revocation letter directs the driver to surrender the license.

sec03-card-f31.front: What maximum fine and jail sentence can follow from failing to surrender a revoked license?
sec03-card-f31.expected_back: Failure to surrender the revoked license can bring a fine up to five hundred dollars, up to thirty days in county jail, or both.

sec03-card-f32.front: What training course must a driver pay for and finish to reinstate after point revocation?
sec03-card-f32.expected_back: Point-based reinstatement requires successful completion, at the driver’s expense, of a DMV-approved driver-education and training course with at least four hours of instruction.

sec03-card-f33.front: How long must financial-responsibility proof stay active after a point revocation ends?
sec03-card-f33.expected_back: After point revocation, financial-responsibility proof must remain in force for three years after the original revocation ends.

sec03-card-f34.front: How long are driving privileges removed for a second Nebraska point revocation within five years?
sec03-card-f34.expected_back: A second Nebraska point revocation within five years removes driving privileges for three years.

sec03-card-f35.front: How many points does a motor-vehicle-homicide conviction add to a Nebraska record?
sec03-card-f35.expected_back: A motor-vehicle-homicide conviction carries twelve points.

sec03-card-f36.front: How many points does a third drunk-driving offense carry?
sec03-card-f36.expected_back: A third drunk-driving offense carries twelve points.

sec03-card-f37.front: How many points come from failing to report a crash to law enforcement?
sec03-card-f37.expected_back: Failure to report a crash to law enforcement carries six points.

sec03-card-f38.front: How many points are assessed for failing to help after a crash involving the driver?
sec03-card-f38.expected_back: Failure to help after a crash involving the driver carries six points.

sec03-card-f39.front: How many points does driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs carry?
sec03-card-f39.expected_back: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs carries six points.

sec03-card-f40.front: How many points does willful reckless driving carry in Nebraska?
sec03-card-f40.expected_back: Willful reckless driving carries six points.

sec03-card-f41.front: How many points does leaving a crash scene carry?
sec03-card-f41.expected_back: Leaving a crash scene carries six points.

sec03-card-f42.front: How many points does standard reckless driving carry?

sec03-card-f43.front: How many points are added for careless driving?

sec03-card-f44.front: How many points come from failing to yield when a pedestrian is injured?
sec03-card-f44.expected_back: Failure to yield that injures a pedestrian carries four points.

sec03-card-f45.front: How many points come from reading, typing, or sending written messages on a handheld phone while driving?
sec03-card-f45.expected_back: Using a handheld wireless device to read, type or send written messages while driving carries three points.

sec03-card-f46.front: How many points does negligent driving carry?

sec03-card-f47.front: How many points come from passing a school bus with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing?
sec03-card-f47.expected_back: Passing a school bus with its stop arm out and red lights flashing carries three points.

sec03-card-f48.front: How many points come from failing to yield to a pedestrian when no injury occurs?
sec03-card-f48.expected_back: Failure to yield to a pedestrian without injury carries two points.

sec03-card-f49.front: How many points does unlawfully blocking the driver's view carry?
sec03-card-f49.expected_back: Unlawfully blocking the driver’s view carries one point.

sec03-card-f50.front: How many driving-record points are assigned for refusing an alcohol-content test?
sec03-card-f50.expected_back: Refusal of an alcohol-content test carries one point.

sec03-card-f51.front: How many points does a child-restraint violation add to your driving record?
sec03-card-f51.expected_back: A child-restraint violation carries one point.

sec03-card-f52.front: Which insurer form usually satisfies financial-responsibility proof after a point revocation?
sec03-card-f52.expected_back: Financial-responsibility proof after point revocation is usually an insurer’s written certification identified as Form SR-twenty-two.

sec03-card-f53.front: What usually serves as financial-responsibility proof after a court-ordered license revocation?
sec03-card-f53.expected_back: For court-ordered revocation, financial-responsibility proof is usually an insurer’s written Form SR-twenty-two certification.

sec03-card-f54.front: Which three violations does the handbook list as carrying zero points?
sec03-card-f54.expected_back: The handbook assigns no points for parking violations, muffler violations or failure to carry a valid operator license on the person.

sec03-card-f55.front: How long is a sobriety program permit valid when issued after the subsequent-offense or refusal waiting period?
sec03-card-f55.expected_back: A sobriety program permit issued during the subsequent-offense or refusal waiting-period pathway is valid only for the remaining portion of the one-year administrative revocation.

sec03-card-f56.front: How long does a later-offense interlock permit last during administrative revocation?
sec03-card-f56.expected_back: A later-offense interlock permit during administrative revocation lasts for the remaining portion of that one-year revocation.

sec03-card-f57.front: Once the chemical-test refusal waiting period ends, how long does the interlock permit remain valid?
sec03-card-f57.expected_back: After the refusal waiting period, the interlock permit lasts only for the remaining portion of the one-year administrative revocation.

sec03-card-f58.front: What offense level and license penalty apply to fleeing an officer over a misdemeanor, traffic infraction, or moving local ordinance?
sec03-card-f58.expected_back: Fleeing an officer to avoid arrest or citation for a Nebraska misdemeanor or traffic infraction, or a city or village ordinance violation other than a nonmoving traffic violation, is a Class I misdemeanor and may also revoke the operator license.

sec03-card-f59.front: Under the general juvenile-court offense rule for age seventeen and younger, how long is an unlicensed youth barred from getting a permit or license?
sec03-card-f59.expected_back: For the handbook’s age-seventeen-and-younger juvenile-court offense rule, an individual without a permit or license is prohibited from obtaining one for thirty days.

sec03-card-r01.front: For citations dated November fourteen, two thousand twenty or later, how many points come from driving one through five miles per hour over the limit?
sec03-card-r01.expected_back: For a citation dated November fourteen, two thousand twenty or later, driving one through five miles per hour above the limit adds no points inside or outside city limits.

sec03-card-r02.front: Inside city limits, how many points come from speeding more than five up to ten miles per hour over the limit?
sec03-card-r02.expected_back: Inside city limits, speeding more than five but no more than ten miles per hour above the limit carries two points.

sec03-card-r03.front: Inside city limits, how many points come from going over ten up through thirty-five miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r03.expected_back: Inside city limits, speeding more than ten through thirty-five miles per hour above the limit carries three points.

sec03-card-r04.front: How many points come from going over thirty-five miles per hour past the speed limit anywhere in Nebraska?
sec03-card-r04.expected_back: Speeding more than thirty-five miles per hour above the limit carries four points inside or outside city limits.

sec03-card-r05.front: Outside city limits, how many points come from going over five up through ten miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r05.expected_back: Outside city limits, speeding more than five through ten miles per hour above the limit carries one point.

sec03-card-r06.front: Outside city limits, how many points come from going over ten up through fifteen miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r06.expected_back: Outside city limits, speeding more than ten through fifteen miles per hour above the limit carries two points.

sec03-card-r07.front: Outside city limits, how many points come from going over fifteen up through thirty-five miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r07.expected_back: Outside city limits, speeding more than fifteen through thirty-five miles per hour above the limit carries three points.

sec03-card-r08.front: How many points come from driving on an expired license or without ever having been licensed?
sec03-card-r08.expected_back: Driving with an expired license or without ever having received a license carries one point.

sec03-card-r09.front: How many points come from a passenger violation on a provisional or school permit?
sec03-card-r09.expected_back: A provisional or school permit passenger violation carries one point.

sec03-card-r10.front: How many points come from breaking wireless-device restrictions on a school learner, learner, school, or provisional permit?
sec03-card-r10.expected_back: A wireless-device violation under provisional, learner, school or school learner permit restrictions carries one point.

sec03-card-r11.front: Which date determines when points from a traffic conviction are counted on your record?
sec03-card-r11.expected_back: A traffic conviction adds points using the violation date rather than the conviction date.

sec03-card-r12.front: How long do traffic convictions remain on your Nebraska driving record?
sec03-card-r12.expected_back: Traffic convictions stay on the driving record for five years.

sec03-card-r13.front: When do active points stop counting toward revocation?
sec03-card-r13.expected_back: Points stop counting two years after the violation date.

sec03-card-r14.front: How does Nebraska score an out-of-state traffic conviction on your point record?
sec03-card-r14.expected_back: An out-of-state traffic conviction receives Nebraska points as though the violation happened in Nebraska.

sec03-card-r15.front: How can a non-CDL, non-CLP driver earn a two-point credit on their record?
sec03-card-r15.expected_back: A driver without a CDL or CLP may receive a two-point credit after successfully completing a DMV-approved improvement course before the violation that would bring the total to twelve points.

sec03-card-r16.front: How often can an eligible driver use the driver-improvement course two-point credit?
sec03-card-r16.expected_back: The improvement-course point credit can be used only once every five years.

sec03-card-r17.front: What can a court order upon a serious traffic conviction?
sec03-card-r17.expected_back: A serious traffic conviction can result in a court-ordered license revocation for the period the court specifies.

sec03-card-r18.front: After a court-ordered revocation ends, how long must financial-responsibility proof stay in place?
sec03-card-r18.expected_back: Court-ordered revocation requires financial-responsibility proof for three years after the original revocation’s ending date.

sec03-card-r19.front: Who returns an impounded license once the ordered impoundment period finishes?
sec03-card-r19.expected_back: The court returns an impounded license when the impoundment period ends.

sec03-card-r20.front: Compare the revocation penalties for driving during general court impoundment versus underage drinking or refusal impoundment?
sec03-card-r20.expected_back: Driving during general court-ordered impoundment brings a one-year revocation upon conviction, while driving during the separately stated underage drinking or refusal impoundment brings six months.

sec03-card-r21.front: For a driver aged twenty or younger, how long does a conviction under the zero point zero two percent alcohol rule impound the license?
sec03-card-r21.expected_back: For a driver aged twenty or younger, a conviction under the alcohol-content rule of zero point zero two percent leads to thirty days of court impoundment.

sec03-card-r22.front: How long does a zero point zero two percent underage alcohol conviction stay on the record before deletion?
sec03-card-r22.expected_back: For a driver aged twenty or younger, the conviction under the zero point zero two-percent alcohol rule remains on the record for ninety days and is then deleted.

sec03-card-r23.front: How many days of court impoundment result from an underage chemical-test refusal conviction?
sec03-card-r23.expected_back: An underage refusal conviction leads to ninety days of court impoundment.

sec03-card-r24.front: How long does an underage refusal conviction stay on the driving record before deletion?
sec03-card-r24.expected_back: An underage refusal conviction remains on the record for one hundred twenty days and is then deleted.

sec03-card-r25.front: What penalty hits a driver convicted of driving during underage drinking or refusal impoundment?
sec03-card-r25.expected_back: A driver convicted of driving during impoundment under the underage drinking or refusal procedure receives a six-month court-ordered license revocation.

sec03-card-r26.front: What roadside events allow immediate license confiscation under administrative revocation?
sec03-card-r26.expected_back: Administrative revocation permits immediate license confiscation after an alcohol-test failure or refusal of an alcohol-or-drug chemical test.

sec03-card-r27.front: How long is the administrative revocation for a first alcohol-test failure?
sec03-card-r27.expected_back: A first alcohol-test failure brings a one hundred eighty-day administrative revocation.

sec03-card-r28.front: How long is the administrative revocation for a later alcohol-test failure?
sec03-card-r28.expected_back: A later alcohol-test failure brings a year of administrative revocation.

sec03-card-r29.front: How long is the administrative revocation for refusing a chemical alcohol-or-drug test?
sec03-card-r29.expected_back: Refusing a chemical alcohol-or-drug test brings a year of administrative revocation.

sec03-card-r30.front: How can a driver contest an administrative license revocation?
sec03-card-r30.expected_back: A driver subject to administrative revocation may request a hearing to challenge it.

sec03-card-r31.front: How does requesting an administrative-revocation hearing affect interlock or sobriety permit access?
sec03-card-r31.expected_back: A driver who requests an administrative-revocation hearing cannot drive with an interlock or sobriety permit until the court orders it as part of sentencing.

sec03-card-r32.front: What driving option can open up if an eligible driver waives the administrative-revocation hearing?
sec03-card-r32.expected_back: Waiving the administrative hearing can allow eligible driving with an ignition-interlock permit during some or all of the revocation.

sec03-card-r33.front: What credential must a twenty-four over seven sobriety program participant with a court-certified order obtain?
sec03-card-r33.expected_back: A participant in the twenty-four over seven sobriety program who has a court-certified order must obtain a Sobriety Program Permit.

sec03-card-r34.front: When does a sobriety program permit actually allow driving during administrative revocation?
sec03-card-r34.expected_back: A sobriety program permit permits driving during administrative revocation only when the driving record otherwise allows it.

sec03-card-r35.front: For a subsequent offense, when does sobriety-permit eligibility begin?
sec03-card-r35.expected_back: For a subsequent offense, sobriety-permit eligibility begins forty-five days after the temporary license expires.

sec03-card-r36.front: After a chemical-test refusal, when does sobriety-permit eligibility start?
sec03-card-r36.expected_back: After chemical-test refusal, sobriety-permit eligibility begins ninety days after the temporary license expires.

sec03-card-r37.front: Which two events revoke a sobriety program permit?
sec03-card-r37.expected_back: A sobriety program permit is revoked when the DMV receives a conviction abstract revoking driving privileges or a court order revoking that permit.

sec03-card-r38.front: What age and licensing history must a sobriety-permit participant have?
sec03-card-r38.expected_back: A sobriety-permit participant must be at least eighteen and have held or tested for a Class O or Class M license.

sec03-card-r39.front: Does a Nebraska sobriety program permit allow operating a commercial motor vehicle?
sec03-card-r39.expected_back: A sobriety program permit does not authorize commercial vehicle operation.

sec03-card-r40.front: What travel is permitted under an employment drive permit issued after a point or child-support revocation?
sec03-card-r40.expected_back: An employment drive permit after qualifying point or child-support revocation allows only direct home-and-work travel under its employment terms.

sec03-card-r41.front: Can an employment drive permit authorize commercial motor vehicle operation?
sec03-card-r41.expected_back: An employment drive permit does not authorize commercial vehicle operation.

sec03-card-r42.front: When may an eligible first-time administrative-revocation offender apply for an interlock permit?
sec03-card-r42.expected_back: An eligible first-time administrative-revocation offender may apply for an interlock permit after the temporary license’s fifteen days expire.

sec03-card-r43.front: For a first-time administrative-revocation offender, how long does the interlock permit last and what vehicle may be driven?
sec03-card-r43.expected_back: For a first-time offender subject to administrative license revocation, the interlock permit lasts six months and allows driving a vehicle equipped with the interlock system.

sec03-card-r44.front: For a later administrative-revocation offense, when does interlock-permit eligibility start?
sec03-card-r44.expected_back: For a later administrative-revocation offense, interlock-permit eligibility begins forty-five days after temporary-license expiration.

sec03-card-r45.front: After a chemical-test refusal, when does interlock-permit eligibility start?
sec03-card-r45.expected_back: After chemical-test refusal, interlock-permit eligibility begins ninety days after temporary-license expiration.

sec03-card-r46.front: Up to how many years may a court or the Board of Pardons order ignition-interlock use?
sec03-card-r46.expected_back: A court or the Board of Pardons may order interlock use for as long as fifteen years, depending on the record and prior convictions.

sec03-card-r47.front: What is the base criminal classification for tampering with, circumventing, or driving without a required interlock device?
sec03-card-r47.expected_back: The base offense for a driver’s interlock tampering, circumvention or driving without the required device is a Class I misdemeanor.

sec03-card-r48.front: How does the handbook describe the alcohol-related felony enhancement for interlock tampering, circumvention, or driving unequipped?
sec03-card-r48.expected_back: The handbook describes an alcohol-related Class IV felony enhancement for a driver’s interlock tampering, circumvention or driving without the required device, but does not specify the alcohol-threshold unit.

sec03-card-r49.front: Which prior license classes qualify a driver for interlock-permit eligibility?
sec03-card-r49.expected_back: Interlock-permit eligibility requires having held a Class O or Class M license.

sec03-card-r50.front: Where may a driver travel on a medical-hardship permit issued after point revocation?
sec03-card-r50.expected_back: After point revocation, a medical-hardship permit limits travel to trips from home or work to the specified treatment location and back.

sec03-card-r51.front: What offense classification and license consequence apply to fleeing to avoid arrest for a felony?
sec03-card-r51.expected_back: Fleeing to avoid arrest for a felony is a Class IV felony and can also cause license revocation.

sec03-card-r52.front: Up to how long can your driver license be revoked upon conviction for fleeing a motor-vehicle crash scene?
sec03-card-r52.expected_back: A conviction for leaving a motor-vehicle crash scene can revoke the driver license for as long as a year.

sec03-card-r53.front: For a driver aged twenty or younger, how long does a first minor-in-possession conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r53.expected_back: For a driver aged twenty or younger, a first minor-in-possession conviction impounds the permit or license for thirty days.

sec03-card-r54.front: For someone aged twenty or younger, how long does a second minor-in-possession conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r54.expected_back: For a person aged twenty or younger, a second minor-in-possession conviction impounds the permit or license for ninety days.

sec03-card-r55.front: For someone aged twenty or younger, how long does a third or later minor-in-possession conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r55.expected_back: For a person aged twenty or younger, a third or later minor-in-possession conviction impounds the permit or license for twelve months.

sec03-card-r56.front: How long is an unlicensed person aged twenty or younger barred from getting a permit or license after first, second, or third minor-in-possession convictions?
sec03-card-r56.expected_back: An unlicensed person aged twenty or younger cannot obtain a permit or license for thirty days after a first minor-in-possession conviction, ninety days after a second, or twelve months after a third or later conviction.

sec03-card-r57.front: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, how long does a first juvenile-court drug conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r57.expected_back: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, a first juvenile-court drug conviction impounds the permit or license for thirty days.

sec03-card-r58.front: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, how long does a second juvenile-court drug conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r58.expected_back: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, a second juvenile-court drug conviction impounds the permit or license for ninety days.

sec03-card-r59.front: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, how long does a third or later juvenile-court drug conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r59.expected_back: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, a third or later juvenile-court drug conviction impounds the permit or license for twelve months.

sec03-card-r60.front: How long is an unlicensed juvenile aged seventeen or younger barred from getting a permit or license after first, second, or third drug convictions?
sec03-card-r60.expected_back: An unlicensed juvenile aged seventeen or younger cannot obtain a permit or license for thirty days after a first juvenile-court drug conviction, ninety days after a second, or twelve months after a third or later conviction.

sec03-card-r61.front: For any juvenile-court offense involving someone aged seventeen or younger, how long may the court impound driving documents?
sec03-card-r61.expected_back: For any juvenile-court offense involving a person aged seventeen or younger, the court may impound driving documents for thirty days.

sec03-card-r62.front: What must a driver finish before a new license can be issued after suspension, revocation, cancellation, or disqualification?
sec03-card-r62.expected_back: A driver whose license was suspended, revoked, cancelled or disqualified must complete reinstatement before a new license can be issued.

sec04-card-f01.front: How does Nebraska law treat driving while impaired by alcohol or another drug?
sec04-card-f01.expected_back: Driving while impaired by alcohol or another drug is unlawful.

sec04-card-f02.front: Who is barred from drinking alcohol or holding an open alcoholic container inside a vehicle on Nebraska public roads or public parking areas?
sec04-card-f02.expected_back: On Nebraska public roadways or public parking areas, neither a driver nor a passenger may consume alcohol or possess an open alcoholic-beverage container inside a vehicle.

sec04-card-f03.front: Which two core driving essentials can alcohol and other drugs impair?
sec04-card-f03.expected_back: Alcohol and other drugs can impair safe vehicle control and sound driving decisions.

sec04-card-f04.front: Which age group falls under Nebraska's zero-tolerance alcohol rule?
sec04-card-f04.expected_back: Nebraska’s zero-tolerance alcohol rule applies to drivers younger than twenty-one.

sec04-card-f05.front: What are the legal consequences of providing alcohol to a minor in Nebraska?
sec04-card-f05.expected_back: Providing alcohol to a minor is unlawful and can create liability for resulting damage.

sec04-card-f06.front: At what minimum blood alcohol concentration does driving become unlawful for someone younger than twenty-one?
sec04-card-f06.expected_back: For a driver younger than twenty-one, a blood alcohol concentration of at least zero point zero two percent makes driving unlawful.

sec04-card-f07.front: What blood alcohol concentration makes driving unlawful for any driver regardless of age or vehicle type?
sec04-card-f07.expected_back: Driving with a blood alcohol concentration of at least zero point zero eight percent is unlawful regardless of age or vehicle type.

sec04-card-f08.front: What two types of consequences can follow a violation of Nebraska's alcohol-driving provisions?
sec04-card-f08.expected_back: Violating the alcohol-driving provisions can lead to criminal penalties or administrative license revocation.

sec04-card-f09.front: What agreement do you automatically make regarding chemical alcohol-or-drug testing simply by driving on Nebraska roads?
sec04-card-f09.expected_back: Driving on Nebraska roads constitutes agreement to chemical alcohol-or-drug testing when an officer requests it.

sec04-card-f10.front: Under Nebraska's implied-consent rule, how is refusing an officer's request for a blood, breath, or urine test classified?
sec04-card-f10.expected_back: Refusing an officer’s request for an alcohol-or-drug test of blood, breath or urine under Nebraska’s implied-consent rule is a separate crime.

sec04-card-f11.front: What happens if, in the officer's judgment, a driver fails to complete a requested blood, breath, or urine test?
sec04-card-f11.expected_back: Failing, in the officer’s judgment, to complete a requested blood, breath or urine test for alcohol or drugs violates Nebraska’s implied-consent law.

sec04-card-f12.front: How long is the administrative license revocation for refusing a requested chemical test under Nebraska's implied-consent law?
sec04-card-f12.expected_back: Refusing a requested alcohol-or-drug chemical test under Nebraska’s implied-consent law brings a one-year administrative license revocation.

sec04-card-f13.front: Criminal test-refusal penalties match an impaired-driving conviction at what minimum blood alcohol concentration?
sec04-card-f13.expected_back: Criminal refusal penalties match the penalties for a DUI conviction involving blood alcohol concentration of at least zero point one five percent.

sec04-card-f14.front: Depending on prior convictions, for how many years can a criminal refusal conviction revoke your license alongside fines and jail?
sec04-card-f14.expected_back: Depending on prior convictions, a criminal refusal conviction may revoke the license for two through fifteen years in addition to fines and jail.

sec04-card-f15.front: Can significant driving impairment happen before a motorist reaches zero point zero eight percent alcohol concentration?
sec04-card-f15.expected_back: Significant impairment can appear well below the general unlawful alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent.

sec04-card-f16.front: How does a person's body weight relate to alcohol in the bloodstream?
sec04-card-f16.expected_back: Body weight is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption.

sec04-card-f17.front: Why can biological sex influence how quickly alcohol is absorbed?
sec04-card-f17.expected_back: Body composition associated with sex is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption.

sec04-card-f18.front: What role does food in the digestive tract play when someone consumes alcohol?
sec04-card-f18.expected_back: Food in the digestive tract is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption.

sec04-card-f19.front: How does the amount of time spent drinking connect to alcohol absorption?
sec04-card-f19.expected_back: The amount of time spent drinking is among the factors affecting alcohol absorption.

sec04-card-f20.front: If a drinker appears calm and in control socially, what can still be true behind the wheel?
sec04-card-f20.expected_back: A drinker who seems in control may still have seriously impaired driving ability.

sec04-card-f21.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does simple reaction time become impaired?
sec04-card-f21.expected_back: Simple reaction time is impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero four percent.

sec04-card-f22.front: Beginning at what blood alcohol concentration does choosing between possible driving responses become impaired?
sec04-card-f22.expected_back: Choosing between possible responses becomes impaired beginning at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero three percent.

sec04-card-f23.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does tracking a single object become impaired?
sec04-card-f23.expected_back: Tracking a single object becomes impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent.

sec04-card-f24.front: How does the alcohol concentration that impairs tracking several objects compare with tracking just one object?
sec04-card-f24.expected_back: Tracking several objects can be impaired at an alcohol concentration lower than that needed to impair tracking one object.

sec04-card-f25.front: Below what blood alcohol concentration can dividing attention across multiple driving tasks already be impaired?
sec04-card-f25.expected_back: Dividing attention across tasks can be impaired below a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent.

sec04-card-f26.front: What happens to understanding sights and sounds once blood alcohol concentration reaches zero point zero five percent?
sec04-card-f26.expected_back: At a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent, understanding what was seen or heard takes longer.

sec04-card-f27.front: Which visual mechanics decline at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent?
sec04-card-f27.expected_back: At a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent, eye-movement control and combining visual images decline.

sec04-card-f28.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does seeing detail in a moving object decline?
sec04-card-f28.expected_back: Seeing detail in a moving object declines at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent.

sec04-card-f29.front: At what blood alcohol concentration are hand-and-foot coordination and precise muscular tasks impaired?
sec04-card-f29.expected_back: Hand-and-foot coordination and other precise muscular tasks are impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent.

sec04-card-f30.front: Which six vehicle-handling and judgment skills are impaired at zero point zero eight percent blood alcohol concentration?
sec04-card-f30.memory_hook: Steering braking speed lanes gears distance
sec04-card-f30.expected_back: A blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero eight percent impairs steering, braking, speed control, lane tracking, gear changes and distance judgments.

sec04-card-f31.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does emergency response become impaired?
sec04-card-f31.expected_back: Emergency response is impaired at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero four percent.

sec04-card-f32.front: What transportation step should you take ahead of time whenever drinking is planned?
sec04-card-f32.expected_back: If drinking is planned, arrange a designated driver or another form of transportation.

sec04-card-f33.front: What is the only thing that actually lowers alcohol concentration in the body and clears its effects?
sec04-card-f33.expected_back: Only elapsed time reduces the body’s alcohol level and its effects.

sec04-card-f34.front: How does Nebraska's handbook contrast single-task focus up to zero point zero eight percent alcohol concentration against divided attention?
sec04-card-f34.expected_back: The handbook contrasts concentration on one task at a BAC as high as zero point zero eight percent with impaired divided attention below zero point zero five percent.

sec04-card-f35.front: What fine, fee, and license-record penalty come with a Nebraska child-restraint violation?
sec04-card-f35.expected_back: A child-restraint violation carries a twenty-five-dollar fine plus court costs and one point on the operator’s record.

sec04-card-f36.front: What monetary penalty applies to a general occupant-protection violation in Nebraska?
sec04-card-f36.expected_back: A general occupant-protection violation carries a twenty-five-dollar fine plus court costs.

sec04-card-r01.front: What authority does a primary-law violation give a police officer?
sec04-card-r01.expected_back: A primary-law violation alone allows an officer to stop and ticket a driver.

sec04-card-r02.front: When can an officer issue a citation for a secondary-law violation?
sec04-card-r02.expected_back: A secondary-law citation requires the driver to have been stopped and ticketed for another violation.

sec04-card-r03.front: Do vehicle airbags replace the need to buckle your seat belt?
sec04-card-r03.expected_back: Airbags add protection but do not replace seat-belt use.

sec04-card-r04.front: What happens to crash protection when occupants wear seat belts together with airbags?
sec04-card-r04.expected_back: Combining seat belts with airbags improves crash protection.

sec04-card-r05.front: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel in a vehicle equipped with a steering-wheel airbag?
sec04-card-r05.expected_back: In a vehicle with a steering-wheel airbag, the recommended hand positions are nine o’clock and three o’clock.

sec04-card-r06.front: Which passengers face injury risk from an airbag deployment even during a low-speed crash?
sec04-card-r06.expected_back: An airbag deployment can injure children, older occupants or short adults even in a low-speed crash.

sec04-card-r07.front: Up through what age should children ride in a rear seat for greatest crash safety?
sec04-card-r07.expected_back: For greatest safety, children aged twelve or younger should ride in a rear seat.

sec04-card-r08.front: Where must you never place a rear-facing infant seat in an airbag-equipped vehicle?
sec04-card-r08.expected_back: Never put a rear-facing infant seat in the front passenger position of an airbag-equipped vehicle.

sec04-card-r09.front: At least how many inches should a driver keep between their body and the steering wheel in an airbag-equipped vehicle?
sec04-card-r09.expected_back: A driver in an airbag-equipped vehicle should leave at least ten inches between the body and steering wheel.

sec04-card-r10.front: Until what age or manufacturer limit must a young child ride rear-facing?
sec04-card-r10.expected_back: A child must ride rear-facing up to age two or until the child reaches the seat manufacturer’s upper height or weight limit.

sec04-card-r11.front: Which children must be properly secured in a federally approved child safety seat in Nebraska?
sec04-card-r11.expected_back: Children younger than eight must be properly secured in a federally approved child safety seat.

sec04-card-r12.front: When must a child younger than eight ride in a nonfront seat?
sec04-card-r12.expected_back: A child younger than eight must occupy a nonfront seat when that seat has a passenger-restraint system and is not already occupied by another child younger than eight.

sec04-card-r13.front: Is Nebraska's child-safety-seat and nonfront-seating requirement for children younger than eight enforced as a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r13.expected_back: The under-eight child-safety-seat rule, including use of a restraint-equipped nonfront seat not already occupied by another child younger than eight, is a primary law.

sec04-card-r14.front: What restraint rule applies to passengers from age eight until age eighteen?
sec04-card-r14.expected_back: Children from age eight until age eighteen must use a seat belt or child safety seat.

sec04-card-r15.front: Is Nebraska's restraint requirement for children aged eight through seventeen a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r15.expected_back: The restraint requirement for children aged eight through seventeen is a secondary law.

sec04-card-r16.front: Who is prohibited from riding in vehicle cargo areas in Nebraska?
sec04-card-r16.expected_back: Children younger than eighteen may not ride in vehicle cargo areas.

sec04-card-r17.front: Is the ban on children younger than eighteen riding in cargo areas enforced as a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r17.expected_back: The prohibition on children riding in cargo areas is a primary law.

sec04-card-r18.front: Who must be buckled when the driver holds a provisional operator permit or a school permit?
sec04-card-r18.expected_back: All passengers must be buckled when the driver holds a provisional operator permit or a school permit.

sec04-card-r19.front: Is the all-passenger buckle rule for provisional or school permit drivers a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r19.expected_back: The passenger-restraint rule for provisional or school permit drivers is a secondary law.

sec04-card-r20.front: Which seating positions inside a vehicle are covered by child-restraint requirements?
sec04-card-r20.expected_back: Child-restraint requirements apply throughout the vehicle’s seating positions.

sec04-card-r21.front: What restraint rule must childcare providers follow when transporting children?
sec04-card-r21.expected_back: Childcare providers must secure every child in an appropriate safety seat or seat belt.

sec04-card-r22.front: What professional consequence can hit a childcare provider who fails to secure children properly?
sec04-card-r22.expected_back: A childcare provider’s failure to secure children can result in revocation of the childcare license.

sec04-card-r23.front: Is the child-restraint requirement for childcare providers enforced as a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r23.expected_back: The child-restraint requirement for childcare providers is a primary law.

sec04-card-r24.front: What occupant protection must drivers and front-seat passengers use?
sec04-card-r24.expected_back: Drivers and front-seat passengers must wear a seat belt or use a child safety seat.

sec04-card-r25.front: Does Nebraska's front-seat occupant-protection requirement also apply inside autocycles?
sec04-card-r25.expected_back: The front-seat occupant-protection requirement also applies in autocycles.

sec04-card-r26.front: Is the general seat-belt requirement for drivers and front-seat passengers a primary or secondary law in Nebraska?
sec04-card-r26.expected_back: The general driver-and-front-passenger belt requirement is a secondary law.

sec04-card-r27.front: May you ever leave a child alone or unsupervised inside a vehicle?
sec04-card-r27.expected_back: Never leave a child alone or unsupervised in a vehicle.

sec04-card-r28.front: How quickly can a pet left inside a parked vehicle suffer fatal heatstroke, even in mild weather?
sec04-card-r28.expected_back: A pet left in a vehicle can suffer fatal heatstroke in minutes even when outdoor temperatures seem mild.

sec04-card-r29.front: What is the handbook's direct rule about leaving pets inside a motor vehicle?
sec04-card-r29.expected_back: Do not leave pets inside a motor vehicle.

sec04-card-r30.front: In a passenger vehicle, how does swerving to avoid a deer affect your risk of death or injury?
sec04-card-r30.expected_back: In a passenger vehicle, swerving to avoid a deer increases the risk of death or injury.

sec04-card-r31.front: What three actions should you take when hitting a deer is unavoidable?
sec04-card-r31.expected_back: When a deer impact is imminent, brake firmly, keep steering control and stop as safely as possible.

sec04-card-r32.front: What three dangerous maneuvers must you avoid when a deer enters your path?
sec04-card-r32.expected_back: Do not veer off the road, lose control or enter oncoming traffic to avoid a deer.

sec04-card-r33.front: Which three driving habits lower your chance of colliding with a deer?
sec04-card-r33.expected_back: Reduce deer-crash risk by improving your view, slowing in deer-warning zones and keeping speed within headlight range.

sec04-card-r34.front: During which daily hours, seasons, and roadside settings should you watch closely for deer?
sec04-card-r34.expected_back: Be alert for deer during dusk-to-dawn periods, in spring or fall, and near water or wooded areas.

sec04-card-r35.front: Why must you keep scanning for more deer right after spotting one near the road?
sec04-card-r35.expected_back: After seeing a deer, look for additional deer because they travel in groups and behave unpredictably.

sec05-card-f01.front: Which two personal states can influence your driving performance?
sec05-card-f01.expected_back: A person's physical condition and emotional state can influence driving performance.

sec05-card-f02.front: Which two mental habits does the handbook connect directly with safe driving?
sec05-card-f02.expected_back: The handbook connects safe driving with full attention and control of emotions.

sec05-card-f03.front: How does clear forward vision help a motorist while driving?
sec05-card-f03.expected_back: Forward vision helps a driver recognize important objects and respond to them.

sec05-card-f04.front: What traffic awareness benefit comes from peripheral vision?
sec05-card-f04.expected_back: Peripheral vision helps a driver notice objects approaching from either side.

sec05-card-f05.front: Why is judging distance an essential visual skill behind the wheel?
sec05-card-f05.expected_back: Judging distance is one of the visual abilities needed for sound driving decisions.

sec05-card-f06.front: How do horns, sirens, and nearby vehicle sounds help you drive?
sec05-card-f06.expected_back: Sounds such as horns, sirens and nearby vehicles can help a driver make safer decisions.

sec05-card-f07.front: What two ways does the handbook advise drivers with hearing loss to stay safe?
sec05-card-f07.expected_back: The handbook advises drivers with hearing loss to use hearing aids when possible or compensate through stronger visual observation.

sec05-card-f08.front: Who should you consult when an illness or disability might affect your ability to drive safely?
sec05-card-f08.expected_back: The handbook advises consulting a physician when illness or disability may affect the ability to drive safely.

sec05-card-f09.front: Reporting a seizure or loss of consciousness within what lookback window before licensing or renewal triggers a physician's safe-driving certification?
sec05-card-f09.expected_back: An applicant reporting a seizure or loss of consciousness during the three months before obtaining or renewing an operator license is asked for a physician's safe-driving certification.

sec05-card-f10.front: What routine checkup does the handbook recommend for drivers who have diabetes?
sec05-card-f10.expected_back: The handbook recommends regular vision examinations for people with diabetes.

sec05-card-f11.front: What step should people with heart disease, high blood pressure, or circulation problems take before driving?
sec05-card-f11.expected_back: The handbook advises physician consultation before driving for people with heart disease, high blood pressure or circulation problems.

sec05-card-f12.front: When does diabetes, a heart condition, or another medical issue require a physician's safe-driving certification for license issuance or renewal?
sec05-card-f12.expected_back: Diabetes, a heart condition or another medical condition causing loss of consciousness in the three months before operator-license issuance or renewal triggers a physician's safe-driving certification requirement.

sec05-card-f13.front: Whom should you ask about how a prescription medicine might affect your driving?
sec05-card-f13.expected_back: The handbook advises asking a physician or pharmacist how a prescription medicine could affect driving.

sec05-card-f14.front: What should you inspect before driving after taking nonprescription medicine?
sec05-card-f14.expected_back: Review nonprescription medicine packaging for side effects that could impair driving.

sec05-card-f15.front: What does the handbook state about nitrous oxide use inside a vehicle operating on a Nebraska public roadway?
sec05-card-f15.expected_back: The handbook prohibits nitrous oxide use in a motor vehicle being operated on a Nebraska public roadway.

sec05-card-f16.front: What legal basis does the handbook describe for a police officer conducting a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f16.expected_back: The handbook describes reasonable suspicion of a traffic or criminal violation as the basis for an officer's traffic stop.

sec05-card-f17.front: How should both the driver and passengers act when emergency lights appear behind the vehicle?
sec05-card-f17.expected_back: When emergency lights appear behind the vehicle, the driver and passengers are advised to remain calm and cooperate.

sec05-card-f18.front: How and where should you pull over when an officer signals a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f18.expected_back: Signal and move off the road or to its side at the first safe opportunity when being stopped.

sec05-card-f19.front: Which two vehicle systems should you switch off once stopped by an officer?
sec05-card-f19.expected_back: During the stop, switch off the engine and audio equipment.

sec05-card-f20.front: When should you step out of your vehicle during a police stop?
sec05-card-f20.expected_back: Remain inside the vehicle unless the officer directs you to get out.

sec05-card-f21.front: What lighting step should you take if an officer pulls you over at night?
sec05-card-f21.expected_back: If stopped at night, illuminate the vehicle's interior so the officer can see inside.

sec05-card-f22.front: Why might an officer shine a bright spotlight on your vehicle during a stop?
sec05-card-f22.expected_back: An officer may use a spotlight to improve visibility during a stop.

sec05-card-f23.front: Where should you keep your hands while waiting during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f23.expected_back: Keep your hands on the wheel or another place where the officer can readily see them.

sec05-card-f24.front: Whose instructions must both you and your passengers follow during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f24.expected_back: Follow the instructions the officer gives to you and your passengers.

sec05-card-r01.front: From which side of your vehicle might an officer approach during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-r01.expected_back: An officer conducting a stop may approach the vehicle from either side.

sec05-card-r02.front: Which window should you roll down so you and the officer can speak easily?
sec05-card-r02.expected_back: Lower the window on the approaching officer's side to make conversation easier.

sec05-card-r03.front: When must you inform the officer if there is a weapon inside the vehicle?
sec05-card-r03.expected_back: Tell the officer at the first contact if there is a weapon in the vehicle.

sec05-card-r04.front: When should you reach for your driver license or vehicle paperwork during a stop?
sec05-card-r04.expected_back: Wait for directions before reaching for a license or vehicle paperwork.

sec05-card-r05.front: What may you do if a nonuniformed officer conducts a stop without showing official credentials?
sec05-card-r05.expected_back: A nonuniformed officer will ordinarily show credentials; you may ask to see credentials if none are shown.

sec05-card-r06.front: What does an officer ordinarily explain and ask during a routine traffic stop?
sec05-card-r06.expected_back: The officer ordinarily explains the stop and may ask about the trip.

sec05-card-r07.front: Which three documents does an officer ordinarily request during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-r07.expected_back: A stopping officer ordinarily requests the driver's license, insurance evidence and vehicle registration.

sec05-card-r08.front: What should you do before retrieving requested paperwork stored out of easy reach?
sec05-card-r08.expected_back: If requested paperwork is out of reach, explain its location and wait for the officer's acknowledgement before retrieving it.

sec05-card-r09.front: How should you behave if the officer directs you to exit the vehicle?
sec05-card-r09.expected_back: When instructed to exit, keep your hands visible and stand where the officer directs.

sec05-card-r10.front: What three enforcement outcomes can result from a police traffic stop?
sec05-card-r10.expected_back: A stop may result in a warning, a traffic citation that can include a fine, or an arrest.

sec05-card-r11.front: What may you do if an officer does not explain the enforcement action being taken?
sec05-card-r11.expected_back: The officer usually explains the action being taken; you may request an explanation if one is not given.

sec05-card-r12.front: How should you ask if you need an officer to clarify an instruction or action?
sec05-card-r12.expected_back: Ask respectfully when you need an officer to clarify an instruction or action.

sec05-card-r13.front: Where should you challenge an officer's decision instead of arguing on the roadside?
sec05-card-r13.expected_back: The handbook advises using established court procedures to contest a decision instead of extending the stop by arguing.

sec05-card-r14.front: Does signing and accepting a traffic ticket admit that you are guilty?
sec05-card-r14.expected_back: Accepting and signing a traffic ticket does not itself admit guilt.

sec05-card-r15.front: What serious consequence can happen if you refuse to sign a traffic ticket?
sec05-card-r15.expected_back: Refusing to sign a traffic ticket can result in arrest.

sec05-card-r16.front: Whom may you ask to speak with regarding an officer's conduct, and when is best?
sec05-card-r16.expected_back: You may ask to speak with a supervisor about an officer's conduct, preferably soon after the stop.

sec05-card-r17.front: What coverage obligation applies to motor vehicles operated on Nebraska public roadways?
sec05-card-r17.expected_back: The handbook requires financial responsibility for motor vehicles operated on public roadways.

sec05-card-r18.front: What minimum liability dollar amount covers injury to or death of one person in a single crash?
sec05-card-r18.expected_back: The printed insurance requirement includes twenty-five thousand dollars for injury to or death of one person in a single crash.

sec05-card-r19.front: What minimum liability dollar amount covers injury to or death of two or more people in one crash?
sec05-card-r19.expected_back: For injury to or death of at least two people in one crash, the printed amount is fifty thousand dollars, subject to the separate one-person limit.

sec05-card-r20.front: What minimum liability dollar amount covers damage to other people's property in a single crash?
sec05-card-r20.expected_back: The printed property-damage amount is twenty-five thousand dollars for damage to other people's property in a single crash.

sec06-card-f01.front: What reports does the federal highway safety agency collect regarding vehicles, tires, and child safety seats?
sec06-card-f01.expected_back: NHTSA collects reports about possible safety problems in vehicles and equipment, including tires and child safety seats.

sec06-card-f02.front: What safety outcome can reporting a vehicle problem help trigger?
sec06-card-f02.expected_back: Reporting a vehicle safety problem may help identify a defect that leads to a recall.

sec06-card-f03.front: Which four lighting components are included in the handbook's required equipment list?
sec06-card-f03.expected_back: The handbook's required lighting equipment includes headlights, tail lamps, brake lamps and turn indicators.

sec06-card-f04.front: Alongside lighting and brakes, which three sound, visibility, and exhaust items sit on the required-equipment list?
sec06-card-f04.expected_back: A horn, windshield wipers and a muffler are included in the required-equipment list.

sec06-card-f05.front: What vehicle detail determines which seat-belt equipment is legally required?
sec06-card-f05.expected_back: The required seat-belt equipment depends on the vehicle's manufacturing year.

sec06-card-f06.front: Which two separate braking systems does the handbook require on a motor vehicle?
sec06-card-f06.expected_back: The handbook requires both a service-brake system and a parking-brake system.

sec06-card-f07.front: What material must every window on a motor vehicle use?
sec06-card-f07.expected_back: Every vehicle window is required to use safety glass.

sec06-card-f08.front: What tire type and minimum tread depth appear on Nebraska's required-equipment list?
sec06-card-f08.expected_back: The equipment list specifies pneumatic tires with tread measuring at least two thirty-seconds of an inch.

sec06-card-f09.front: What rule governs items hung from mirrors or posted on vehicle windows?
sec06-card-f09.expected_back: Objects hung or posted in a window may not obstruct the driver's view.

sec06-card-f10.front: Which unique code should vehicle owners look up when checking for manufacturer safety recalls?
sec06-card-f10.expected_back: The handbook directs owners to use their vehicle identification number when checking for manufacturer safety recalls.

sec06-card-f11.front: Where on the vehicle is the vehicle identification number usually located?
sec06-card-f11.expected_back: The VIN is usually found near the lower corner below the windshield.

sec06-card-f12.front: What happens in many vehicles when the ignition key is turned to the lock position?
sec06-card-f12.expected_back: Many vehicles have a spring-loaded device that locks the steering wheel when the ignition key reaches the lock position.

sec06-card-f13.front: Why must you never turn the ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is still moving?
sec06-card-f13.expected_back: Do not move the ignition to its lock position while the vehicle is moving, because steering control can be lost.

sec06-card-f14.front: When does the handbook recommend having the steering-wheel lock inspected?
sec06-card-f14.expected_back: The handbook recommends inspecting the steering-wheel lock during routine maintenance.

sec06-card-f15.front: When is sunscreen material allowed below the upper windshield mark in Nebraska?
sec06-card-f15.expected_back: The handbook forbids windshield sunscreen material below the AS-one line unless that material is clear and transparent.

sec06-card-f16.front: What is the maximum luminous reflectance allowed on front side windows?
sec06-card-f16.expected_back: The printed front-side-window rule does not allow luminous reflectance above thirty-five percent.

sec06-card-f17.front: Below what light-transmission percentage is tint prohibited on front side windows?
sec06-card-f17.expected_back: The printed front-side-window rule does not allow light transmission below thirty-five percent.

sec06-card-f18.front: What is the maximum luminous reflectance allowed under the printed rear-window rule?
sec06-card-f18.expected_back: The printed rear-window rule does not allow luminous reflectance above thirty-five percent.

sec06-card-f19.front: Below what light-transmission percentage is tint prohibited on the rear window?
sec06-card-f19.expected_back: The printed rear-window rule does not allow light transmission below twenty percent.

sec06-card-f20.front: How does the handbook classify owning or operating a vehicle that violates Nebraska's window-tint restrictions?
