sec02-card-f03.front: What status must every new Nebraska applicant establish when applying?
sec02-card-f03.expected_back: New Nebraska applicants must establish U.S. citizenship or, for applicants who are not U.S. citizens, lawful status.

sec02-card-f04.front: Once U.S. citizenship proof has been presented, is it needed again at future licensing visits?
sec02-card-f04.expected_back: After citizenship proof has been presented, it is not required again at later licensing-office visits.

sec02-card-f05.front: How often must a noncitizen applicant bring lawful-status proof to the licensing office?
sec02-card-f05.expected_back: An applicant who is not a U.S. citizen must present lawful-status proof on every licensing-office visit.

sec02-card-f06.front: What authentication features must required application documents carry?
sec02-card-f06.expected_back: Required documents must be certified and bear a raised seal or stamp.

sec02-card-f07.front: Are faxed documents or photocopies accepted for a Nebraska licensing application?
sec02-card-f07.expected_back: A faxed document or photocopy is not accepted for the application.

sec02-card-f08.front: What can happen if your application paperwork needs deeper document review?
sec02-card-f08.expected_back: Document review may require more information and a later office visit rather than same-day approval.

sec02-card-f09.front: Can a document stamped or marked as unsuitable for identification proof establish your identity?
sec02-card-f09.expected_back: A document marked as unsuitable for identification proof cannot establish identity.

sec02-card-f10.front: What may the Nebraska DMV do with documents you submit alongside an application?
sec02-card-f10.expected_back: The DMV may keep copies of documents submitted with an application.

sec02-card-f11.front: Which documents link a changed name to your existing permit, license, or ID?
sec02-card-f11.expected_back: To link a changed name to the existing permit, license or ID, present certified marriage licenses, certified divorce decrees or a court order; lawful-status applicants may use a name-change petition.

sec02-card-f12.front: Which type of birth certificate is accepted to prove both citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f12.expected_back: A state-government-certified birth certificate is an accepted citizenship-and-identity document.

sec02-card-f13.front: Does Nebraska accept a hospital-issued birth certificate for licensing?
sec02-card-f13.expected_back: A birth certificate from a hospital is not accepted.

sec02-card-f14.front: Which Puerto Rico birth certificates are rejected for a Nebraska application?
sec02-card-f14.expected_back: A Puerto Rico birth certificate issued before September thirty, two thousand ten is not accepted.

sec02-card-f15.front: When can a U.S. passport or passport card establish both citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f15.expected_back: An unexpired U.S. passport or passport card can establish citizenship and identity.

sec02-card-f16.front: What companion documents apply when presenting a valid I-ninety-four or A-variant arrival record for status and identity?
sec02-card-f16.expected_back: An unexpired I-ninety-four or I-ninety-four A is accepted for lawful status and identity with a valid foreign passport, except the passport is unnecessary for a Refugee stamp or Canadian place of origin; F one, F two, J one, J two, M one and M two applicants also need an I-twenty and or or DS-two thousand nineteen, and a Refugee stamp may require an I-seven hundred ninety-seven.

sec02-card-f17.front: What extra SEVIS paperwork must student or exchange applicants in F, J, or M categories provide?
sec02-card-f17.expected_back: Applicants with F one, F two, J one, J two, M one or M two status must also supply an I-twenty and or or DS-two thousand nineteen for SEVIS information.

sec02-card-f18.front: In which two cases is a foreign passport unnecessary alongside an arrival-and-departure record?
sec02-card-f18.expected_back: For an I-ninety-four or I-ninety-four A arrival record, the foreign passport is unnecessary when the record is stamped Refugee or the place of origin is Canada.

sec02-card-f19.front: Can a visa by itself satisfy Nebraska's accepted lawful-status and identity document list?
sec02-card-f19.expected_back: A visa alone is not one of the accepted lawful-status and identity documents listed here.

sec02-card-f20.front: When does a permanent-resident card count as accepted lawful-status and identity proof?
sec02-card-f20.expected_back: An unexpired permanent-resident card is an accepted lawful-status and identity document.

sec02-card-f21.front: When is an employment-authorization card accepted for lawful status and identity?
sec02-card-f21.expected_back: An unexpired employment-authorization card is an accepted lawful-status and identity document.

sec02-card-f22.front: Which Certificate of Naturalization form numbers establish citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f22.expected_back: A Certificate of Naturalization on Form N-five hundred fifty or N-five hundred seventy is an accepted citizenship and identity document.

sec02-card-f23.front: Which Certificate of Citizenship form numbers does the handbook accept for citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f23.expected_back: The handbook lists a Certificate of Citizenship on Form N-five hundred sixty or N-four hundred fifty-one as citizenship and identity evidence.

sec02-card-f24.front: Which State Department Consular Report of Birth Abroad forms prove citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f24.expected_back: A State Department Consular Report of Birth Abroad on Form FS-two hundred forty, DS-one thousand three hundred fifty or FS-five hundred forty-five is accepted as citizenship and identity evidence.

sec02-card-f25.front: What two conditions must your principal-address documents satisfy together?
sec02-card-f25.expected_back: Principal-address evidence must show the Nebraska address and come from two different issuing sources.

sec02-card-f26.front: Does a post-office box qualify as your principal residence address?
sec02-card-f26.expected_back: A post-office box does not establish the principal residence address.

sec02-card-f27.front: How can an applicant younger than twenty-one prove residence without personal bills or statements?
sec02-card-f27.expected_back: An applicant younger than twenty-one who cannot supply personal residence proof may use the parent’s or guardian’s address documents.

sec02-card-f28.front: How recent must a bank or financial-institution statement be to prove residence?
sec02-card-f28.expected_back: A bank or other financial-institution statement used for residence proof must have been issued within ninety days.

sec02-card-f29.front: What date window and employer details must appear on a pay stub used for residence proof?
sec02-card-f29.expected_back: A pay stub used for residence proof must be from the preceding ninety days and show the employer’s name and address.

sec02-card-f30.front: How recent must a government document be when used under the recent-document residence category?
sec02-card-f30.expected_back: A government document used under the handbook’s recent-document category must have been issued within ninety days.

sec02-card-f31.front: How recent must a magazine issue be if you bring it as residence proof?
sec02-card-f31.expected_back: A magazine used for residence proof must be from the preceding ninety days.

sec02-card-f32.front: What date mark must appear on a mailed envelope, box, or postcard used for address proof?
sec02-card-f32.expected_back: A mailed envelope, box or postcard used as address proof must show a postmark or stamped date within ninety days.

sec02-card-f33.front: What date limit applies to correspondence, receipts, or invoices in the recent-address category?
sec02-card-f33.expected_back: Correspondence, a receipt or an invoice used in the recent-address-document category must be dated within ninety days.

sec02-card-f34.front: Can a Nebraska vehicle registration serve as one of your residence documents?
sec02-card-f34.expected_back: A valid Nebraska vehicle registration is one accepted residence document.

sec02-card-f35.front: Which four types of valid insurance policies or cards are accepted as residence documents?
sec02-card-f35.expected_back: A valid insurance policy or card for life, health, auto or home coverage is one accepted residence document.

sec02-card-f36.front: Does Nebraska accept a valid property tax statement or receipt as a residence document?
sec02-card-f36.expected_back: A valid real-estate tax statement or receipt is one accepted residence document.

sec02-card-f37.front: Can a valid license count as one of the documents establishing Nebraska residence?
sec02-card-f37.expected_back: A valid license is among the documents accepted to establish residence.

sec02-card-f38.front: Is a Nebraska voter-registration card accepted to help prove principal residence?
sec02-card-f38.expected_back: A Nebraska voter-registration card is one accepted residence document.

sec02-card-f39.front: What landlord details must appear on a residential lease or rental agreement submitted for address proof?
sec02-card-f39.expected_back: A lease or rental agreement used for residence proof must give the landlord’s name and contact information.

sec02-card-f40.front: Does a mortgage agreement qualify as an accepted principal-address document?
sec02-card-f40.expected_back: A mortgage agreement is among the accepted principal-address documents.

sec02-card-f41.front: Can you use your Nebraska DMV renewal notice as one principal-address document?
sec02-card-f41.expected_back: A Nebraska DMV renewal notice is among the accepted principal-address documents.

sec02-card-f42.front: Can a blank check or deposit slip serve as a principal-address document?
sec02-card-f42.expected_back: A blank check or deposit slip is among the accepted principal-address documents.

sec02-card-f43.front: If staff ask for Social Security proof, how much of the number must appear on the document?
sec02-card-f43.expected_back: If Social Security proof is requested, it must show the complete number.

sec02-card-f44.front: Which numbers and federal immigration documents does the Nebraska DMV verify?
sec02-card-f44.expected_back: The DMV verifies Social Security numbers and documents from U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services.

sec02-card-f45.front: Does a Social Security card qualify as accepted Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-f45.expected_back: A Social Security card is an accepted form of Social Security proof.

sec02-card-f46.front: Can an employer Form W-two serve as Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-f46.expected_back: Form W-two is among the documents accepted as Social Security number proof.

sec02-card-f47.front: Is Form SSA-one thousand ninety-nine accepted as Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-f47.expected_back: Form SSA-one thousand ninety-nine is among the documents accepted as Social Security number proof.

sec02-card-f48.front: How many documents from the accepted list are needed to prove U.S. citizenship or lawful status and identity?
sec02-card-f48.expected_back: Present one document from the handbook’s accepted list to establish U.S. citizenship or lawful status and identity.

sec02-card-f49.front: What extra requirement can apply if you bring a city- or county-issued birth certificate?
sec02-card-f49.expected_back: A city- or county-issued birth certificate may require additional identification documents.

sec02-card-f50.front: What additional form may be required alongside a Refugee-stamped arrival-and-departure record?
sec02-card-f50.expected_back: A Refugee-stamped I-ninety-four or I-ninety-four A may require an I-seven hundred ninety-seven.

sec02-card-f51.front: Which three immigration forms does the handbook explicitly exclude from this identity and lawful-status pathway?
sec02-card-f51.expected_back: Forms I-one hundred fifty-one, I-ninety-four W and I-ninety-four Border Crosser are not accepted for this identity and lawful-status documentation pathway.

sec02-card-f52.front: When is an ADIT temporary permanent-residence stamp accepted for licensing?
sec02-card-f52.expected_back: An unexpired ADIT stamp documenting temporary lawful admission for permanent residence until a stated date is accepted in a valid foreign passport.

sec02-card-f53.front: What must a valid foreign passport show under the temporary-resident endorsement wording used after June twenty-eight, two thousand four?
sec02-card-f53.expected_back: For the temporary-resident endorsement wording specified after June twenty-eight, two thousand four, the valid foreign passport must show the one-year temporary I-five hundred fifty-one permanent-resident statement with the properly placed admission stamp.

sec02-card-f54.front: Which two personal details must appear on citizenship or lawful-status documents for a noncommercial application?
sec02-card-f54.expected_back: Citizenship or lawful-status documents required for a Nebraska noncommercial permit, license or state ID application must include the applicant’s name and birth date.

sec02-card-r01.front: When can a pay stub serve as Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-r01.expected_back: A pay stub showing the applicant’s name and Social Security number can serve as Social Security number proof.

sec02-card-r02.front: How is a Nebraska credential marked when issued to an applicant with parolee immigration status?
sec02-card-r02.expected_back: A Nebraska document issued to an applicant with parolee immigration status is marked as unsuitable for federal identification.

sec02-card-r03.front: Which identification, verification, and testing rules apply to a parolee applicant?
sec02-card-r03.expected_back: A parolee applicant still must meet the ordinary identification, verification and testing requirements.

sec02-card-r04.front: Who receives a vision test when applying for a noncommercial permit or operator license?
sec02-card-r04.expected_back: All noncommercial permit and operator-license applicants receive a vision test.

sec02-card-r05.front: Which two aspects of eyesight does the Nebraska DMV vision screening check?
sec02-card-r05.expected_back: The DMV’s vision screening checks both visual acuity and peripheral vision.

sec02-card-r06.front: If you need corrective lenses to pass the vision standard, when must you wear them?
sec02-card-r06.expected_back: When corrective lenses are necessary to meet the vision standard, the driver must wear them whenever driving.

sec02-card-r07.front: Who must check the findings if you do not meet the DMV vision standards at the counter?
sec02-card-r07.expected_back: If the DMV vision standards are not met, an ophthalmologist or optometrist must check the findings.

sec02-card-r08.front: What happens if an applicant cannot meet Nebraska's minimum vision standard even after specialist evaluation?
sec02-card-r08.expected_back: A person who cannot meet the minimum vision standard cannot receive a license.

sec02-card-r09.front: How are Nebraska written knowledge tests organized across different license classes?
sec02-card-r09.expected_back: Each license class has a separate written test.

sec02-card-r10.front: Which permit and license applicants get their written-test study material from this driver manual?
sec02-card-r10.expected_back: The manual supplies written-test material for school learner, learner, school, provisional and Class O operator applicants.

sec02-card-r11.front: What does the Nebraska drive test evaluate?
sec02-card-r11.expected_back: The drive test checks the applicant’s operation of the requested vehicle class in ordinary driving conditions.

sec02-card-r12.front: Can licensing staff require a drive test from any license applicant?
sec02-card-r12.expected_back: Licensing staff may require a drive test from any license applicant at their discretion.

sec02-card-r13.front: Who supplies the vehicle for the drive test, and what kind of vehicle must it be?
sec02-card-r13.expected_back: The applicant must provide a drive-test vehicle representative of the requested license class.

sec02-card-r14.front: What mechanical condition and lighting feature must your drive-test vehicle have?
sec02-card-r14.expected_back: The drive-test vehicle must be mechanically sound and have functioning brake lights.

sec02-card-r15.front: Which drive-test vehicles must provide a clean working passenger seat belt for licensing staff?
sec02-card-r15.expected_back: A drive-test vehicle from model year nineteen sixty-four or later must have a clean working passenger belt for licensing staff.

sec02-card-r16.front: Which drive-test vehicles must have clean working seat belts for both licensing staff and the driver?
sec02-card-r16.expected_back: A drive-test vehicle from model year nineteen seventy-three or later needs clean working belts for both staff and driver.

sec02-card-r17.front: Which dashboard instrument must work properly inside your drive-test vehicle?
sec02-card-r17.expected_back: The drive-test vehicle needs a working speedometer.

sec02-card-r18.front: What interior condition is required for a Nebraska drive-test vehicle?
sec02-card-r18.expected_back: The drive-test vehicle’s interior must be clean.

sec02-card-r19.front: Which nine driving skills and maneuvers can the Nebraska drive test assess?
sec02-card-r19.expected_back: The drive test may assess starting, stopping, turning, lane position, traffic controls, speed, right of way, parking and backing.

sec02-card-r20.front: What must you prove before reapplying after failing the Class O drive test three times in a row?
sec02-card-r20.expected_back: After three consecutive Class O drive-test failures, reapplication requires proof of successful completion of a DMV-approved driver-training course or at least ninety days holding a learner permit.

sec02-card-r21.front: What form do you receive explaining why a requested licensing document was denied?
sec02-card-r21.expected_back: An applicant denied the requested document receives a Return for Services form explaining the denial.

sec02-card-r22.front: What should you do with a Return for Services form when you come back to the licensing office?
sec02-card-r22.expected_back: Bring the Return for Services form on the next licensing-office visit.

sec02-card-r23.front: If you fail a licensing test, can you retake it later that same day?
sec02-card-r23.expected_back: A failed test cannot be repeated that same day.

sec02-card-r24.front: Within how many days and where must you present your issuance certificate for payment?
sec02-card-r24.expected_back: Present the issuance certificate within ninety days to a county treasurer outside Douglas, Lancaster and Sarpy Counties, or to a state driver-licensing office in one of those three counties.

sec02-card-r25.front: What happens if you miss the ninety-day issuance-certificate payment deadline?
sec02-card-r25.expected_back: Missing the issuance-certificate deadline requires a return to the licensing office.

sec02-card-r26.front: How long is the temporary receipt valid after you pay for your credential?
sec02-card-r26.expected_back: The temporary receipt issued after payment is valid for thirty days.

sec02-card-r27.front: Does the TSA accept Nebraska's temporary paper receipt for boarding flights or entering federal buildings?
sec02-card-r27.expected_back: The temporary receipt is not accepted by the TSA as identification for boarding an aircraft or entering certain federal facilities.

sec02-card-r28.front: How is your permanent credential delivered, and will the postal service forward it?
sec02-card-r28.expected_back: The permanent document is mailed to the address supplied to licensing staff and is not forwarded by the postal service.

sec02-card-r29.front: When and whom should applicants contact if they need disability testing accommodations?
sec02-card-r29.expected_back: Applicants needing disability accommodations should contact the local licensing office or state DMV before testing.

sec02-card-r30.front: To whom may an applicant appeal a Nebraska license or State ID refusal?
sec02-card-r30.expected_back: An applicant may appeal a licensing or identification-card refusal to the DMV Director.

sec02-card-r31.front: Whose safety report can prompt the DMV to recall a licensed driver for reexamination?
sec02-card-r31.expected_back: A safety concern reported by police, a physician or another person can lead the DMV to recall a driver for reexamination.

sec02-card-r32.front: What details appear in the letter sent to a driver recalled for reexamination?
sec02-card-r32.expected_back: A driver recalled for reexamination receives a letter identifying the office, date and time for written and drive tests.

sec02-card-r33.front: Which two professional statements must a recalled driver supply?
sec02-card-r33.expected_back: A recalled driver must supply a licensed physician’s driving-related medical statement and a vision statement from an optometrist or ophthalmologist.

sec02-card-r34.front: What happens if a recalled driver skips reexamination, omits required statements, or fails required tests?
sec02-card-r34.expected_back: Failure to attend reexamination, provide required statements or pass required tests results in license cancellation.

sec02-card-r35.front: When does a Nebraska license expire for a U.S. citizen issued the card below age twenty-one?
sec02-card-r35.expected_back: A Nebraska license issued to a U.S. citizen younger than twenty-one expires on the holder’s twenty-first birthday.

sec02-card-r36.front: When does a Nebraska license expire for a U.S. citizen aged twenty-one or older at issuance?
sec02-card-r36.expected_back: A Nebraska license issued to a U.S. citizen aged at least twenty-one expires on the holder’s birthday in the fifth year after issuance.

sec02-card-r37.front: Within how many days must you report a changed name or address through a document change?
sec02-card-r37.expected_back: A changed name or address must be reported through the required document change within sixty days.

sec02-card-r38.front: What happens to your previous license's validity once a replacement license is issued?
sec02-card-r38.expected_back: Issuing a replacement license invalidates the previous document for identification use.

sec02-card-r39.front: What does Restriction B mean on a Nebraska license?
sec02-card-r39.expected_back: Restriction B means corrective lenses are required.

sec02-card-r40.front: What does Restriction C identify on a Nebraska driver license?
sec02-card-r40.expected_back: Restriction C identifies mechanical aids on the vehicle.

sec02-card-r41.front: How does Restriction E limit your driving privileges?
sec02-card-r41.expected_back: Restriction E limits the license to an automatic-transmission vehicle.

sec02-card-r42.front: What vehicle equipment does Restriction F require?

sec02-card-r43.front: What time-of-day limit does Restriction G place on a driver?
sec02-card-r43.expected_back: Restriction G limits driving to daylight.

sec02-card-r44.front: Which roadways are off-limits under Restriction Q?

sec02-card-r45.front: What signaling equipment does Restriction U require on the vehicle?
sec02-card-r45.expected_back: Restriction U requires automatic turn signals.

sec02-card-r46.front: How does Restriction V limit where a person may drive?
sec02-card-r46.expected_back: Restriction V limits driving to the stated geographical area.

sec02-card-r47.front: Which type of road does Restriction W exclude?

sec02-card-r48.front: What driving limit does Restriction X specify?
sec02-card-r48.expected_back: Restriction X specifies a maximum driving speed.

sec02-card-r49.front: Which roads are allowed under Restriction Y?
sec02-card-r49.expected_back: Restriction Y limits travel to two-lane roads carrying traffic in both directions.

sec02-card-r50.front: What does Restriction Z stand for on a Nebraska license?
sec02-card-r50.expected_back: Restriction Z represents a special DMV-specified condition.

sec02-card-r51.front: Outside a renewal window, how can you remove a restriction placed from a medical or vision statement?
sec02-card-r51.expected_back: Outside a renewal period, removing a restriction imposed from a medical or vision statement requires the applicable new physician or vision statement.

sec02-card-r52.front: How must an applicant qualify for a veteran designation on a Nebraska credential?
sec02-card-r52.expected_back: A veteran designation requires eligibility certification through the Nebraska Department of Veterans’ Affairs.

sec02-card-r53.front: When is voter registration offered through the Nebraska DMV?
sec02-card-r53.expected_back: Voter registration is offered when applying for a Nebraska license or State ID Card.

sec02-card-r54.front: At what minimum age may a permit, license, or State ID holder declare organ and tissue donation through the DMV?
sec02-card-r54.expected_back: A permit, license or State ID holder aged sixteen or older may make an organ-and-tissue donation declaration through the DMV.

sec02-card-r55.front: When does the heart donor symbol appear on a Nebraska credential?
sec02-card-r55.expected_back: A heart donor symbol appears on the document only when the holder chooses organ or tissue donation.

sec02-card-r56.front: For a donor between ages sixteen and eighteen, who may amend the minor's donation decision?
sec02-card-r56.expected_back: For a donor between sixteen and eighteen, available parents or legal adult guardians may amend the minor’s donation decision.

sec02-card-r57.front: What happens to your organ-donor status if your driving or identification card expires?
sec02-card-r57.expected_back: Donor status remains in place when the driving or identification document expires.

sec02-card-r58.front: Can an organ donation declared on a credential, donor card, or registry be revoked after the donor's death?
sec02-card-r58.expected_back: A donation declared through a permit, license, State ID, donor card or donor registry cannot be rescinded after the donor’s death.

sec02-card-r59.front: What role does a deceased registered donor's family play in the donation process?
sec02-card-r59.expected_back: A deceased donor’s family is included in the donation process but does not need to authorize the donation.

sec02-card-r60.front: When can you get a replacement Nebraska driving or identification document?
sec02-card-r60.expected_back: A replacement document is available when the prior card has been lost or destroyed.

sec02-card-r61.front: Besides losing a card, which two life changes are reasons to obtain a replacement document?
sec02-card-r61.expected_back: A changed name or a move is a reason to obtain a replacement document.

sec10-card-f01.front: Where on the roadway should you travel when moving slower than normal traffic for current conditions?
sec10-card-f01.expected_back: Traffic moving below the normal speed for the time, location and conditions should use the available right lane or stay as far right as practicable.

sec10-card-f02.front: Which two maneuvers allow a driver to leave the right lane under Nebraska's keep-right rule?
sec10-card-f02.expected_back: The keep-right rule allows overtaking same-direction traffic and preparing for a left turn at an intersection, private road or driveway.

sec10-card-f03.front: Who yields when vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at roughly the same moment?
sec10-card-f03.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection, vehicles arriving at about the same time yield to traffic on their right.

sec10-card-f04.front: Why must you still drive defensively at an intersection when traffic rules give you priority?
sec10-card-f04.expected_back: Drive defensively even when you appear entitled to proceed, because another driver might not stop.

sec10-card-f05.front: What should you scan for ahead of reaching an intersection controlled by a yield sign?
sec10-card-f05.expected_back: Before reaching a yield-controlled intersection, look for crossing traffic.

sec10-card-f06.front: Which crossing vehicles must you let pass at a yield sign or when turning onto a roadway?
sec10-card-f06.expected_back: Yield to crossing traffic close enough to create a conflict, including when turning onto a road.

sec10-card-f07.front: Once a safe opening appears at a yield point, how should you enter the roadway?
sec10-card-f07.expected_back: After finding a safe traffic gap, merge and adjust travelling speed.

sec10-card-f08.front: What must you do before entering a crossroad from the stop-sign side of a two-way stop?
sec10-card-f08.expected_back: A driver approaching the stop-controlled side of a two-way-stop intersection must stop fully before entering.

sec10-card-f09.front: After halting at a two-way stop, what must you check and wait for before pulling out?
sec10-card-f09.expected_back: At a two-way stop, look in every direction and wait for conflicting vehicles and pedestrians to clear before proceeding.

sec10-card-f10.front: What two obligations apply to every driver crossing a four-way stop intersection?
sec10-card-f10.expected_back: At a four-way stop, every driver must stop and exercise ordinary care while crossing.

sec10-card-f11.front: How does Nebraska treat first-to-stop order at a four-way stop, and what resolves uncertainty?
sec10-card-f11.expected_back: First-stop-first-go is described as common courtesy at a four-way stop; when uncertain, yield to the driver on the right.

sec10-card-f12.front: What should you do whenever insisting on intersection priority could cause a collision?
sec10-card-f12.expected_back: Do not insist on priority if doing so risks a crash.

sec10-card-f13.front: In which direction does all traffic circulate around a roundabout's central island?
sec10-card-f13.expected_back: Roundabout traffic circulates one way counterclockwise around the central island.

sec10-card-f14.front: Why do roundabouts include a raised truck apron around the central island?
sec10-card-f14.expected_back: A roundabout's truck apron provides turning room for the rear wheels of large trucks.

sec10-card-f15.front: Which five road users are prohibited from riding or walking on a roundabout's truck apron?
sec10-card-f15.memory_hook: Passenger vehicles, bikes, walkers stay off
sec10-card-f15.expected_back: Cars, SUVs, pickups, cyclists and pedestrians may not use the truck apron.

sec10-card-f16.front: How should you manage speed and the approach crosswalk as you near a roundabout?
sec10-card-f16.expected_back: Approach a roundabout at the posted advisory speed and yield to pedestrians and bicyclists in the approach crosswalk.

sec10-card-f17.front: Which vehicles have priority when you reach the yield line of a roundabout?
sec10-card-f17.expected_back: Yield to vehicles approaching from the left that are already circulating, and enter only a safe gap.

sec10-card-f18.front: What two actions must you take as you reach your roundabout exit?
sec10-card-f18.expected_back: Signal right when nearing your roundabout exit and yield to pedestrians and cyclists in the exit crosswalk.

sec10-card-f19.front: How do you choose the right lane ahead of entering a two-lane roundabout?
sec10-card-f19.expected_back: Before entering a two-lane roundabout, use its signs and arrows to select the correct lane.

sec10-card-f20.front: In Nebraska's general two-lane roundabout layout, which approach lanes serve left turns versus right turns?
sec10-card-f20.memory_hook: Left uses left, right uses right
sec10-card-f20.expected_back: In the described general two-lane layout, left turns use the shared through slash left lane and right turns use the shared through slash right lane.

sec10-card-f21.front: What three rules govern going straight through a two-lane roundabout?
sec10-card-f21.memory_hook: Obey arrows, yield both, hold lane
sec10-card-f21.expected_back: For straight travel through a two-lane roundabout, follow its signs and arrows, yield to all circulating traffic on the left and remain in the selected lane.

sec10-card-f22.front: Why must you never drive alongside or overtake a large truck at a roundabout?
sec10-card-f22.expected_back: Avoid driving beside or passing a large truck at a roundabout because it may need another lane or the apron to turn.

sec10-card-f23.front: How do you clear the way for an emergency vehicle before versus after entering a roundabout?
sec10-card-f23.expected_back: For an emergency vehicle, pull over before entering a roundabout; if already inside, take your exit and pull over beyond the splitter island.

sec10-card-f24.front: Where must you avoid stopping when yielding to an approaching emergency vehicle at a roundabout?
sec10-card-f24.expected_back: Avoid stopping inside the roundabout while yielding to an emergency vehicle.

sec10-card-r01.front: What lane action is required on a multilane controlled-access highway near stopped emergency, roadside, utility, maintenance, or sanitation vehicles flashing lights?
sec10-card-r01.expected_back: On a multilane controlled-access highway, move at least one travel lane away from a stopped emergency, road-assistance, utility-maintenance, highway-maintenance, waste or recycling vehicle displaying flashing lights.

sec10-card-r02.front: What must you do under the Move Over law when heavy traffic or road conditions block changing lanes?
sec10-card-r02.expected_back: If traffic or other conditions prevent the required move-over lane change, slow down and pass the stopped vehicle at a safe speed.

sec10-card-r03.front: Which four vehicle types make up the road-assistance group covered by Nebraska's Move Over rule?
sec10-card-r03.expected_back: The printed road-assistance category includes DOT vehicles, State Patrol motorist assistance, federally registered towing or roadside assistance and utility-company service vehicles.

sec10-card-r04.front: What maximum fine does the Nebraska handbook list for a first Move Over violation?
sec10-card-r04.expected_back: The handbook lists a first move-over violation as carrying a fine of up to one hundred dollars.

sec10-card-r05.front: What maximum penalties apply to a second or subsequent Move Over violation in Nebraska?
sec10-card-r05.expected_back: The printed maximum for a later move-over violation is five hundred dollars, seven days in jail, or both.

sec10-card-r06.front: What must you do after a minor freeway or interstate crash when nobody is hurt and vehicles still drive?
sec10-card-r06.expected_back: After a minor interstate or freeway crash with no injuries and drivable vehicles, move to the nearest shoulder out of the traffic lanes.

sec10-card-r07.front: How may a crashed vehicle be cleared to the shoulder if it cannot be driven under its own power?
sec10-card-r07.expected_back: A vehicle that cannot be moved to the shoulder may be pushed there by law enforcement or removed by others.

sec10-card-r08.front: Where must you stop and whom must you yield to when pulling out of an alley, driveway, or parking lot?
sec10-card-r08.expected_back: When exiting an alley, driveway or parking lot, stop before the sidewalk or sidewalk area and proceed slowly while yielding to pedestrians and approaching traffic.

sec10-card-r09.front: When does an authorized emergency vehicle gain priority over surrounding traffic?
sec10-card-r09.expected_back: Yield when an authorized emergency vehicle activates its siren or flashing lights.

sec10-card-r10.front: How must you position your car for a moving emergency vehicle, and when may opposing traffic keep moving?
sec10-card-r10.expected_back: For the described moving emergency vehicle, pull parallel and close to the right edge and stop outside intersections unless an officer directs otherwise; opposing traffic across a median need not stop.

sec10-card-r11.front: How long must you remain stopped for an emergency vehicle, and what check comes before pulling back out?
sec10-card-r11.expected_back: Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle passes, then check for additional emergency vehicles before moving.

sec13-card-f01.front: What kind of roadway does the Nebraska handbook mean when it uses the word interstate?
sec13-card-f01.expected_back: The handbook uses interstate to mean a controlled-access highway with multiple lanes.

sec13-card-f02.front: What must you spot in the nearest traffic lane before pulling onto an interstate?
sec13-card-f02.expected_back: Before entering an interstate, identify a gap in the nearest traffic lane.

sec13-card-f03.front: Which pavement-line transition on an entrance ramp marks where you adjust speed, signal, and merge?
sec13-card-f03.expected_back: At an entrance ramp, wait for the broken-white-line portion, then adjust speed, signal and merge into a safe gap.

sec13-card-f04.front: How should you manage your speed once cruising on the interstate?
sec13-card-f04.expected_back: On the interstate, maintain a steady traffic-compatible speed while obeying posted limits.

sec13-card-f05.front: Which lane should you normally stay in on an interstate, and what lane habit should you avoid?
sec13-card-f05.expected_back: Keep slower traffic right and avoid unnecessary lane changes; ordinarily remain right unless overtaking.

sec13-card-f06.front: How can you help ramp drivers merge when you are cruising in the right interstate lane?
sec13-card-f06.expected_back: Watch entrance ramps and, if safe, signal and move left to help entering traffic merge.

sec13-card-f07.front: What two steps are mandatory before changing lanes to pass on the interstate?
sec13-card-f07.expected_back: Signal before changing lanes and check blind spots before passing.

sec13-card-f08.front: What must you do if you overshoot your intended interstate exit?
sec13-card-f08.expected_back: After missing an interstate exit, continue to the next exit rather than backing up or using an emergency crossover.

sec13-card-f09.front: Is driving across an interstate median ever allowed?
sec13-card-f09.expected_back: Do not cross an interstate median.

sec13-card-f10.front: What minimum speed does the Nebraska manual list for interstate travel?
sec13-card-f10.expected_back: The manual lists forty miles per hour as the interstate minimum speed.

sec13-card-f11.front: At least how far ahead of an interstate exit should you signal and move into the proper exit lane?
sec13-card-f11.expected_back: Plan an exit early, signal and reach its proper lane at least a mile before the intended exit.

sec13-card-f12.front: When should you start slowing for an interstate exit, and what sign on the ramp must you check?
sec13-card-f12.expected_back: For an interstate exit, slow after entering the deceleration lane and check the ramp's advised speed.

sec13-card-f13.front: What two roadway changes must you watch for right after leaving an interstate?
sec13-card-f13.expected_back: After leaving the interstate, watch for two-way traffic and newly posted speed limits.

sec13-card-f14.front: Between which daily landmarks must your headlights stay turned on?
sec13-card-f14.expected_back: Use headlights between sunset and sunrise.

sec13-card-f15.front: Which lights should you switch on as daylight fades, and what is the rule on driving with parking lamps alone?
sec13-card-f15.expected_back: Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other drivers can see the vehicle; parking lamps alone are unlawful for driving.

sec13-card-f16.front: When must you switch off auxiliary driving lamps while meeting or following other vehicles?
sec13-card-f16.expected_back: Switch off auxiliary driving lamps when approaching from ahead or behind at the same time headlights require dimming.

sec13-card-f17.front: How do you know whether your nighttime cruising speed is safe for your headlights?
sec13-card-f17.expected_back: Choose a night-driving speed that permits stopping within the illuminated roadway.

sec13-card-f18.front: Where should you use high beams, and what two situations require dimming them?
sec13-card-f18.expected_back: Use high beams on open highways, but dim them for oncoming vehicles and when following within two hundred feet.

sec13-card-f19.front: Where should you aim your eyes if an oncoming vehicle's bright headlights start blinding you?
sec13-card-f19.expected_back: If oncoming glare is blinding, look toward the right road edge instead of directly at the lights.

sec13-card-f20.front: What glass-care step and eye habit prevent night-vision fatigue behind the wheel?
sec13-card-f20.expected_back: Keep both sides of the windshield clean and move your gaze instead of staring into the headlight-lit spot.

sec13-card-f21.front: How should you adjust speed in rain, and what happens physically during hydroplaning?
sec13-card-f21.expected_back: In rain, slow to match surface conditions; hydroplaning occurs when the tires ride on water instead of contacting the road.

sec13-card-f22.front: What three adjustments help maintain control and visibility during rainy driving?
sec13-card-f22.expected_back: Rain may require disengaging cruise control; use low beams and increase the following gap.

sec13-card-f23.front: What must you do whenever water covers a roadway ahead?
sec13-card-f23.expected_back: Do not enter a flooded roadway; turn around and find another route.

sec13-card-f24.front: Why is even shallow-looking floodwater across a road deceptive and dangerous?
sec13-card-f24.expected_back: Floodwater can conceal dips or a damaged road surface even when it appears shallow.

sec13-card-f25.front: What shallow flood depth reaches underneath most passenger cars, stalling engines or spoiling steering?
sec13-card-f25.expected_back: The manual warns that six inches of water can reach the underside of most passenger cars and cause stalling or lost control.

sec13-card-f26.front: What depth of moving floodwater can sweep away almost any vehicle, including pickups and SUVs?
sec13-card-f26.expected_back: The manual warns that two feet of moving water can sweep away most vehicles, including SUVs and pickups.

sec13-card-f27.front: What should you do if floodwater blocks every route, and when is flood caution extra critical?
sec13-card-f27.expected_back: If no alternate route exists around flooding, go to higher ground and wait for the water to recede; use extra caution at night.

sec13-card-f28.front: Which beam setting, speed adjustment, and mindset belong whenever driving in fog?
sec13-card-f28.expected_back: In fog, use low beams, reduce speed and proceed with extreme caution.

sec13-card-f29.front: When visibility drops below a quarter mile, which roads does the Nebraska manual advise staying off?
sec13-card-f29.expected_back: The manual advises against travel on roads posted at forty miles per hour or more when visibility is below a quarter mile.

sec13-card-f30.front: Which vehicles feel strong wind hardest, and when should you brace for sudden steering corrections?
sec13-card-f30.expected_back: Small and high-profile vehicles are especially affected by wind; anticipate corrections after leaving shelter or meeting large vehicles.

sec13-card-f31.front: What weather alerts should you monitor when traveling across windy stretches?
sec13-card-f31.expected_back: Watch for high-wind advisories while travelling.

sec13-card-f32.front: Which four habits keep your vehicle controllable on snow- or ice-covered roads?
sec13-card-f32.expected_back: On snow or ice, slow down, increase following distance, clear the windows and make speed or direction changes gradually.

sec13-card-f33.front: May you use cruise control on snowy or icy pavement?
sec13-card-f33.expected_back: Do not use cruise control on snow or ice.

sec13-card-f34.front: How should a driver without antilock brakes slow on snow or ice, and why?
sec13-card-f34.expected_back: For snowy or icy conditions, the handbook tells non-ABS drivers to pump the brake pedal to avoid lockup; rolling tires are needed for steering.

sec13-card-f35.front: How must you use antilock brakes on snowy or icy roads?
sec13-card-f35.expected_back: For snowy or icy conditions with ABS, press firmly and do not pump the brakes.

sec13-card-f36.front: How much throttle should you apply when climbing a slippery hill?
sec13-card-f36.expected_back: On a slippery uphill climb, apply enough power to maintain speed without spinning the wheels.

sec13-card-f37.front: Which calendar dates bound Nebraska's printed studded-tire season?
sec13-card-f37.expected_back: The printed studded-tire season runs from November first to April first.

sec13-card-f38.front: Why does the manual advise staying off the roads altogether during a blizzard?
sec13-card-f38.expected_back: The manual advises against driving in blizzards because poor visibility, slippery surfaces and wind occur together.

sec13-card-r01.front: What is the golden survival rule if a blizzard strands your vehicle?
sec13-card-r01.expected_back: If stranded in a blizzard, stay calm and remain with the vehicle.

sec13-card-r02.front: What ventilation and exhaust checks are mandatory before running the heater sparingly in a snowbound car?
sec13-card-r02.expected_back: For a stranded vehicle, crack a window for ventilation and use the engine and heater sparingly only with ventilation and a snow-free exhaust pipe.

sec13-card-r03.front: Which exterior and nighttime interior lights help plow and rescue crews spot a stranded vehicle?
sec13-card-r03.expected_back: Use hazard flashers to help work crews see a stranded vehicle and use its interior lamp at night.

sec13-card-r04.front: How should multiple occupants manage rest if stranded together in a storm?
sec13-card-r04.expected_back: If several people are stranded together, alternate sleeping and keeping watch.

sec13-card-r05.front: What should you do first if your right wheels drop off the pavement onto a low shoulder?
sec13-card-r05.expected_back: If wheels drop off pavement, grip the steering wheel firmly and straddle the edge instead of immediately turning back.

sec13-card-r06.front: How should you bring your car back onto the road after stabilizing an edge drop?
sec13-card-r06.expected_back: After an edge drop, reduce speed, check traffic and return gradually to the driving lane when safe.

sec13-card-r07.front: What does each category of driver distraction, visual, manual, and cognitive, pull away from driving?
sec13-card-r07.expected_back: Visual distraction takes the eyes away, manual distraction takes the hands away and cognitive distraction takes attention away from driving.

sec13-card-r08.front: Which distraction categories can text messaging trigger at the exact same time?
sec13-card-r08.expected_back: Text messaging can involve visual, manual and cognitive distraction together.

sec13-card-r09.front: What fine range does the Nebraska handbook list for texting and driving?
sec13-card-r09.expected_back: The handbook lists a texting-and-driving fine range of two hundred to five hundred dollars.

sec13-card-r10.front: Does switching to a hands-free phone call eliminate driver distraction?
sec13-card-r10.expected_back: A hands-free phone conversation can still distract the driver.

sec13-card-r11.front: Which common non-phone cabin habits does the handbook flag for distracting drivers?
sec13-card-r11.expected_back: Eating, reading, handling clothing, reaching to the floor, grooming or changing media can distract a driver.

sec13-card-r12.front: Who else riding inside the vehicle can pull a driver's focus off the road?
sec13-card-r12.expected_back: Children, other passengers and pets can distract the driver.

sec13-card-r13.front: How should you prepare children before driving, and what must you do if they need attention en route?
sec13-card-r13.expected_back: Secure children properly, keep them occupied appropriately and pull over safely if they need attention rather than tending to them while moving.

sec13-card-r14.front: How should you handle rowdy passengers, arguments, or upsetting conversations?
sec13-card-r14.expected_back: Keep passenger behavior under control and reserve arguments or upsetting conversations for a safe place outside the driving task.

sec13-card-r15.front: How should pets travel inside a vehicle, and where must a pet never sit?
sec13-card-r15.expected_back: Secure pets in an appropriate carrier, kennel or harness and do not allow a pet on the driver's lap.

sec13-card-r16.front: Which three dashboard adjustments can pull your focus away from controlling the car?
sec13-card-r16.expected_back: Entering navigation destinations, searching for radio content or adjusting climate controls can distract from vehicle control.

sec13-card-r17.front: How does browsing mobile internet or checking email behind the wheel affect safety?
sec13-card-r17.expected_back: Using portable-device internet or email while driving adds distraction and crash risk.

sec13-card-r18.front: When should you adjust your seat, mirrors, climate controls, and radio?
sec13-card-r18.expected_back: Set the seat, mirrors, climate and radio controls before beginning to drive.

sec13-card-r19.front: When should you check messages, and how can passengers help with cabin controls underway?
sec13-card-r19.expected_back: Check messages before driving and ask passengers to operate navigation, radio or climate controls when help is needed.

sec13-card-r20.front: When driving solo, what opportunity does the manual suggest using if vehicle controls need adjusting?
sec13-card-r20.expected_back: The manual suggests using normal stops for vehicle-control adjustments.

sec13-card-r21.front: What handheld wireless actions does Nebraska's printed noncommercial rule prohibit while operating a motor vehicle?
sec13-card-r21.expected_back: The printed noncommercial rule prohibits handheld wireless use to read, type or send written messages while operating a motor vehicle.

sec13-card-r22.front: What rule governs television screens inside a vehicle on a public road?
sec13-card-r22.expected_back: The manual prohibits operating a vehicle on a public road with a television screen visible to the driver.

sec13-card-r23.front: Which roadside sights commonly lure a driver's eyes away from the lane ahead?
sec13-card-r23.expected_back: Watching crash scenes, police stops, construction, advertising, scenery or address details can draw attention away from driving.

sec13-card-r24.front: Which frightening or rude behaviors illustrate aggressive driving in the handbook?
sec13-card-r24.expected_back: Aggressive driving includes frightening or rude behavior such as tailgating, cutting off vehicles, running red lights or failing to yield.

sec13-card-r25.front: What emotional state should keep you from driving, and how should you treat other road users?
sec13-card-r25.expected_back: Avoid driving while angry or upset and treat other road users courteously.

sec13-card-r26.front: How should you start every trip, and what must you do if drowsiness sets in?
sec13-card-r26.expected_back: Begin a trip rested; if drowsy, stop driving and pull over safely for rest.

sec13-card-r27.front: How long is the short fatigue-rest nap option described in the Nebraska handbook?
sec13-card-r27.expected_back: The handbook describes a short ten-to-twenty-minute nap as a fatigue-rest option.

sec13-card-r28.front: What break timing and daily travel hours do the handbook's fatigue tips highlight?
sec13-card-r28.expected_back: The fatigue tips suggest a midafternoon break and avoiding early-morning or late-night driving.

sec13-card-r29.front: Which physical and driving clues warn that dangerous fatigue has already set in?
sec13-card-r29.expected_back: Fatigue warnings include heavy eyelids, yawning, head nodding, missed signs, poor memory of recent miles and unintended lane departures.

sec13-card-r30.front: When traveling with another licensed person, what simple fatigue solution does the handbook mention?
sec13-card-r30.expected_back: The handbook mentions changing drivers as one response to fatigue.

sec13-card-r31.front: What does the manual say about cold air, gum, loud music, caffeine, and energy drinks for fighting drowsiness?
sec13-card-r31.expected_back: The manual says an open window, chewing gum or loud radio does not prevent drowsiness and that caffeine or energy drinks are unreliable for alertness.

sec13-card-r32.front: May you use phone calls or texting to keep yourself awake behind the wheel?
sec13-card-r32.expected_back: Do not use phone calls or texting as a way to stay awake while driving.

sec13-card-r33.front: In plain terms, what does defensive driving mean?
sec13-card-r33.expected_back: Defensive driving means staying alert to prevent crashes.

sec13-card-r34.front: What minimum look-ahead planning interval does the Nebraska handbook recommend?
sec13-card-r34.expected_back: The handbook describes a look-ahead planning interval of at least ten to fifteen seconds.

sec13-card-r35.front: Where should you scan to both sides, including right after an intersection signal turns green?
sec13-card-r35.expected_back: Look to both sides where road users could cross, and check both directions at an intersection even after the signal changes.

sec13-card-r36.front: At least how often should you check rear traffic, plus before which four situations?
sec13-card-r36.expected_back: Check rear traffic at least every ten seconds and when changing lanes, backing, slowing or descending steep hills.

sec13-card-r37.front: What exact zone does an over-the-shoulder glance check that mirrors miss?
sec13-card-r37.expected_back: A shoulder glance checks the blind area beside the vehicle that mirrors do not show.

sec13-card-r38.front: At least how far ahead must you signal before turns, lane changes, freeway entries, or leaving a curb?
sec13-card-r38.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet before a planned direction change, including lane changes, turns, freeway entry or leaving a curb.

sec13-card-r39.front: Under what visibility condition and wiper condition must you switch on headlights?
sec13-card-r39.expected_back: Use headlights when other vehicles are hard to see and whenever the windshield wipers are used.

sec13-card-r40.front: How do a sharp horn blast and brief brake-pedal taps serve different warning jobs?
sec13-card-r40.expected_back: A sharp horn blast can warn of an immediate collision danger; brief brake taps can warn following drivers of slowing.

sec13-card-r41.front: Why must you maintain an open space cushion around your vehicle?
sec13-card-r41.expected_back: Maintain a space cushion around the vehicle to allow time to react, stop or pass safely.

sec13-card-r42.front: How do you time your following gap with a roadside object, and what count proves you are too close?
sec13-card-r42.expected_back: To check following space, time the gap from a fixed roadside marker; reaching it in less than three seconds is too close, and adversity calls for a longer gap.

sec13-card-r43.front: Starting from Nebraska's three-second minimum gap, how much following time should you add for adverse conditions?
sec13-card-r43.expected_back: The handbook treats three seconds as a following-distance minimum and adds one second for each adverse factor, such as rain or heavy traffic.

sec13-card-r44.front: How do you protect your side cushions and your rear space cushion in traffic?
sec13-card-r44.expected_back: Keep lateral space from oncoming traffic and parked vehicles, and protect rear space through steady speed and advance slowing signals.

sec01-card-f01.question_text: What credential must a Nebraska resident hold to drive a motor vehicle on state streets or highways?
sec01-card-f01.teaching_text: Taking any motor vehicle onto public streets without valid state driving credentials exposes an unlicensed resident to citations and court penalties.

sec01-card-f02.question_text: How soon must a new resident holding a valid license from another state get Nebraska licensing?
sec01-card-f02.teaching_text: Waiting past your first month after moving leaves your out-of-state credential invalid for resident driving during a routine traffic stop.

sec01-card-f03.question_text: Why does Nebraska phase in teen driving privileges in stages through its graduated licensing system?
sec01-card-f03.teaching_text: Easing new drivers into tougher traffic conditions step by step prevents fatal crashes while judgment and hazard scanning are still developing.

sec01-card-f04.question_text: When do graduated-license restrictions forbid using an interactive wireless device?
sec01-card-f04.teaching_text: Glancing at a screen while rolling pulls both eyes and attention off traffic right when inexperienced drivers need full reaction time.

sec01-card-f05.question_text: Who must wear a seat belt inside a vehicle operated by a permit holder?
sec01-card-f05.teaching_text: One unbuckled friend in the back seat violates permit terms and turns that passenger into a dangerous projectile during a crash.

sec01-card-f06.question_text: Which passengers may a school-permit holder carry to the school that driver attends?
sec01-card-f06.teaching_text: Giving a neighbor or classmate a lift to school breaks passenger restrictions even when everyone is headed to the exact same campus.

sec01-card-f07.question_text: During the first six months, how many non-immediate-family passengers under nineteen may a provisional-permit driver carry?
sec01-card-f07.teaching_text: Packing extra teen friends into the car spikes distraction and crash risk during the most vulnerable early months of solo driving.

sec01-card-f08.question_text: Which two travel purposes are exempt from the midnight-to-six-in-the-morning limit for provisional-permit drivers?
sec01-card-f08.teaching_text: Cruising home from a late hangout after midnight violates curfew because only legitimate employment shifts and school activities qualify as exceptions.

sec01-card-f09.question_text: What can happen to your license if you break a driving restriction?
sec01-card-f09.teaching_text: Treating permit conditions like optional suggestions can sideline your driving privileges completely through administrative or court-ordered suspension or revocation.

sec01-card-f10.question_text: What must a driver under twenty-one do after earning six or more points within one year?
sec01-card-f10.teaching_text: Ignoring that three-month training deadline after piling up citations puts a young driver on track to lose driving privileges entirely.

sec01-card-f11.question_text: What driving goal does the school learner permit allow an eligible student to practice toward?
sec01-card-f11.teaching_text: Students who qualify geographically use this supervised stage to log legal wheel time before testing or qualifying for solo school commutes.

sec01-card-f12.question_text: What is the minimum age for a school learner permit, and can an applicant apply early?
sec01-card-f12.teaching_text: Unlike standard learner credentials that allow early paperwork, showing up before turning fourteen results in an automatic turn-away at licensing.

sec01-card-f13.question_text: Who must sit beside a school learner driving a passenger car?
sec01-card-f13.teaching_text: Having an older sibling under twenty-one or an adult riding in the back seat fails the supervision requirement for legal practice.

sec01-card-f14.question_text: Which two tests are required to get a school learner permit?
sec01-card-f14.teaching_text: Before practicing on public roads with a supervisor, a young student must prove sharp eyesight and solid knowledge of traffic rules.

sec01-card-f15.question_text: How long does a school learner permit stay valid after it is issued?
sec01-card-f15.teaching_text: Because that practice window is short, families need to plan supervised driving hours promptly before the six-month credential expires.

sec01-card-f16.question_text: How does a school-permit applicant meet the city-population geographic requirement?
sec01-card-f16.teaching_text: Test writers love checking whether you know that either living outside or attending school outside a five-thousand-resident city satisfies eligibility.

sec01-card-f17.question_text: Where and how may a school-permit driver travel without a supervising adult?
sec01-card-f17.teaching_text: Detouring for food or errands turns an authorized solo trip between home and school or scheduled activity grounds into a violation.

sec01-card-f18.question_text: When may a school-permit holder drive outside solo school routes?
sec01-card-f18.teaching_text: Riding with a licensed adult twenty-one or older unlocks legal driving at any hour for errands, family trips, and extra practice.

sec01-card-f19.question_text: What is the exact minimum age to apply for a Nebraska school permit?
sec01-card-f19.teaching_text: Memorize those extra two months past fourteen because exam choices often try to bait students with plain age fourteen or fifteen.

sec01-card-f20.question_text: How long must an applicant hold a school learner permit or learner permit before applying for a school permit?
sec01-card-f20.teaching_text: Rushing in before completing two full months on a learner credential blocks your upgrade even if your practice hours are finished.

sec01-card-f21.question_text: Besides logging fifty practice hours, what course option qualifies an applicant for a school permit?
sec01-card-f21.teaching_text: Completing a state-approved safety course gives teens structured behind-the-wheel instruction instead of relying solely on a fifty-hour family log.

sec01-card-f22.question_text: How many certified driving hours and whose signature are needed on the supervised-practice route to a school permit?
sec01-card-f22.teaching_text: Showing up without a signed fifty-hour certification from a parent, guardian, or licensed adult twenty-one or older stalls your permit upgrade.

sec01-card-f23.question_text: How many of the certified school-permit practice hours must take place between sunset and sunrise?
sec01-card-f23.teaching_text: Headlight glare and reduced depth perception make dark roads harder to read, so ten supervised night hours are mandatory before solo driving.

sec01-card-f24.question_text: Which tests are waived for a school-permit applicant who finishes a Nebraska DMV-approved driver-safety course?
sec01-card-f24.teaching_text: Passing an approved course covers both knowledge and road skills, leaving only the vision screening at the licensing counter.

sec01-card-f25.question_text: Which two tests must a school-permit applicant still take when qualifying through the fifty-hour practice certification?
sec01-card-f25.teaching_text: Logging hours with family does not replace a state road evaluation, so licensing staff still check eyesight and behind-the-wheel control.

sec01-card-f26.question_text: When is the written test waived for a school-permit applicant using the fifty-hour practice certification?
sec01-card-f26.teaching_text: Letting a prior learner credential sit expired past twelve months forces you to retake the knowledge exam before upgrading.

sec01-card-f27.question_text: What safety restraint rule applies to every occupant riding with a school-permit driver?
sec01-card-f27.teaching_text: Whether carrying a younger sibling in a booster or a parent up front, every single rider must use proper occupant protection.

sec01-card-f28.question_text: At what exact age does a Nebraska school permit expire?
sec01-card-f28.teaching_text: Watch out for those three extra months past sixteen, which give teen drivers a short bridge window to transition into provisional licensing.

sec01-card-f29.question_text: Which future credentials does a standard learner permit allow you to practice driving toward?
sec01-card-f29.teaching_text: Whether aiming for a teen provisional permit at sixteen or an adult operator license later, legal road practice starts here.

sec01-card-f30.question_text: How early may you apply for a learner permit, and what is the minimum age for issuance?
sec01-card-f30.teaching_text: Starting paperwork two months early helps beat counter lines, though the state will not issue the permit card before birthday fifteen.

sec01-card-f31.question_text: What penalties apply to a first wireless-device violation under graduated-license restrictions?
sec01-card-f31.teaching_text: One quick text behind the wheel hits both your wallet and your point record, pushing young drivers closer to mandatory intervention.

sec01-card-f32.question_text: What dollar fine applies to a seat-belt violation under Nebraska graduated-license restrictions?
sec01-card-f32.teaching_text: Skipping a belt check before shifting out of park costs twenty-five dollars and leaves riders unprotected in a sudden impact.

sec01-card-f33.question_text: How many driving-record points come from breaking a graduated-permit passenger restriction?
sec01-card-f33.teaching_text: Even a short ride with unauthorized friends adds a point that can block or delay your next license upgrade.

sec01-card-f34.question_text: How many points are added to your driving record for a provisional-permit nighttime-driving violation?
sec01-card-f34.teaching_text: Driving past midnight without a work or school-activity reason puts a point on your record and threatens your clean upgrade streak.

sec01-card-f35.question_text: What happens to the permit or license on a first under-twenty-one zero-tolerance offense?
sec01-card-f35.teaching_text: Any measurable underage alcohol violation lets the court impound your driving credential for a full month right on the first offense.

sec01-card-f36.question_text: What law applies when a driver younger than twenty-one has a BAC of zero point zero eight or higher?
sec01-card-f36.teaching_text: Being under twenty-one offers zero shield from full adult drunk-driving prosecution once blood alcohol reaches the adult impairment threshold.

sec01-card-f37.question_text: What underlying permit standards must every school learner permit applicant already satisfy?
sec01-card-f37.teaching_text: Students living and attending school inside a larger city cannot grab a school learner permit just to start driving at fourteen.

sec01-card-f38.question_text: What must an applicant bring if they finished the safety course before being old enough for a school learner permit?
sec01-card-f38.teaching_text: Electronic course records cannot attach to a nonexistent permit profile, so bringing the school paper waiver proves completion at application time.

sec01-card-r01.question_text: Who must occupy the seat next to a passenger-car learner-permit driver?
sec01-card-r01.teaching_text: Every passenger-car practice drive requires an alert licensed adult twenty-one or older right beside you to coach decisions immediately.

sec01-card-r02.question_text: Which prior permits waive the learner-permit written test if valid or expired no more than one year?
sec01-card-r02.teaching_text: Holding a current or recently expired school learner, school, or learner permit spares you from repeating the same knowledge questions.

sec01-card-r03.question_text: How long after issuance does a standard Nebraska learner permit expire?
sec01-card-r03.teaching_text: Do not confuse the one-year standard learner permit with the six-month school learner permit when comparing expiration timelines.

sec01-card-r04.question_text: During which daily hours may a provisional-permit holder drive unsupervised for any purpose?
sec01-card-r04.teaching_text: Daylight and evening hours carry far lower teen crash rates than post-midnight roads where fatigue and low visibility peak.

sec01-card-r05.question_text: Which unsupervised trips are allowed on a provisional permit between midnight and six in the morning?
sec01-card-r05.teaching_text: Only direct travel between home and your job or a scheduled school activity keeps unsupervised late-night driving legal.

sec01-card-r06.question_text: Who must accompany a provisional driver to allow driving at any hour of the day or night?
sec01-card-r06.teaching_text: Having a parent, guardian, or licensed driver twenty-one or older in the car lifts the overnight curfew for late family travel.

sec01-card-r07.question_text: When can you start applying for a provisional permit, and when can it be issued?
sec01-card-r07.teaching_text: Starting your application up to sixty days before turning sixteen avoids birthday delays while honoring the strict age-sixteen issuance floor.

sec01-card-r08.question_text: How long must an applicant hold a qualifying permit before applying for a provisional permit?
sec01-card-r08.teaching_text: Six full months on a school learner, school, or learner permit ensures steady four-season experience before broader solo privileges begin.

sec01-card-r09.question_text: What point-record standard must a provisional-permit applicant meet over the six months right before applying?
sec01-card-r09.teaching_text: Earning three or more points during that six-month lookback resets your momentum and blocks your provisional upgrade at the counter.

sec01-card-r10.question_text: What certified driving hours and signature are required on the practice route to a provisional permit?
sec01-card-r10.teaching_text: Make sure at least ten of your fifty logged hours happen between sunset and sunrise and carry a qualifying adult signature.

sec01-card-r11.question_text: Which provisional-permit tests are waived by completing a DMV-approved Nebraska driver-safety course?
sec01-card-r11.teaching_text: Finishing a state-approved course satisfies both knowledge and road-skill testing so you only complete vision screening at licensing.

sec01-card-r12.question_text: Which tests apply to a provisional applicant using practice certification, and what waives the written test?
sec01-card-r12.teaching_text: Keep your learner permit active or expired within one year so you only face the vision check and road drive evaluation.

sec01-card-r13.question_text: What restraint requirement applies to every person riding with a provisional-permit driver?
sec01-card-r13.teaching_text: As the driver, you are responsible for making sure every passenger uses proper occupant protection before the wheels start rolling.

sec01-card-r14.question_text: On which birthday does a Nebraska provisional permit expire?
sec01-card-r14.teaching_text: Planning your operator-license upgrade before turning eighteen prevents an unexpected lapse in legal driving privileges on your birthday.

sec01-card-r15.question_text: Which vehicles does a Class O license cover, and which two categories does it exclude?
sec01-card-r15.teaching_text: While mopeds, autocycles, and utility or all-terrain vehicles fall under Class O, two-wheeled motorcycles and commercial rigs need separate credentials.

sec01-card-r16.question_text: Can an applicant use an autocycle to take the Class O drive test?
sec01-card-r16.teaching_text: Even though a Class O license lets you drive an autocycle afterward, three-wheeled enclosed vehicles cannot represent standard passenger cars.

sec01-card-r17.question_text: What is the earliest age a driver can qualify for a Nebraska operator license?
sec01-card-r17.teaching_text: Teens who hold a clean provisional permit for a full year can step up to a full operator license at seventeen.

sec01-card-r18.question_text: How does an applicant under eighteen qualify for an operator license?
sec01-card-r18.teaching_text: Holding your provisional permit a full year while keeping points below three proves you are ready for unrestricted Class O driving.

sec01-card-r19.question_text: Which tests are waived when an applicant under eighteen qualifies for an operator license through a clean twelve-month provisional record?
sec01-card-r19.teaching_text: Rewarding twelve low-point months with written and road waivers makes moving from provisional to Class O fast and stress-free.

sec01-card-r20.question_text: Which tests are waived when a provisional holder upgrades to an operator license at ages eighteen through twenty-one?
sec01-card-r20.teaching_text: Prior provisional experience carries forward into young adulthood so applicants aged eighteen through twenty-one skip repeat written and road testing.

sec01-card-r21.question_text: Which tests apply to an adult eighteen or older seeking a first operator license without prior provisional status?
sec01-card-r21.teaching_text: Starting fresh at eighteen or older requires all three evaluations unless a current or recently expired learner permit covers the written exam.

sec01-card-r22.question_text: When does a learner permit waive the written test for a first-time operator applicant aged eighteen or older?
sec01-card-r22.teaching_text: Upgrading within twelve months of learner-permit expiration saves adult first-time drivers from taking the written knowledge screening twice.

sec01-card-r23.question_text: Which requirements apply to an applicant under eighteen who surrenders a valid out-of-state permit or license?
sec01-card-r23.teaching_text: Moving from another state under eighteen does not bypass graduated safety rules, so incoming teens must satisfy provisional-permit standards.

sec01-card-r24.question_text: What testing applies when a new resident aged eighteen or older surrenders a valid out-of-state license?
sec01-card-r24.teaching_text: Handing over an unexpired license from your prior state waives written testing, leaving mandatory vision screening and optional road checks.

sec01-card-r25.question_text: When must a new Nebraska resident aged eighteen or older take the written test?
sec01-card-r25.teaching_text: Losing your prior state card or letting it expire before visiting Nebraska licensing puts the written knowledge screening back on your checklist.

sec03-card-f01.question_text: Can one person simultaneously carry a State ID Card alongside a Nebraska driving permit or license?
sec03-card-f01.teaching_text: Upgrading from a State ID to a permit or license cancels your ID card because Nebraska allows only one active credential.

sec03-card-f02.question_text: How long is a Nebraska license or State ID valid for a holder with lawful immigration status?
sec03-card-f02.teaching_text: Expiration matches your authorized federal stay end date, or caps at twelve months whenever your lawful status carries an open-ended duration.

sec03-card-f03.question_text: Will Nebraska issue a license while your driving privileges are suspended or revoked somewhere else?
sec03-card-f03.teaching_text: National driver registries share sanction records across borders, so unresolved suspensions or revocations in another jurisdiction stop Nebraska issuance cold.

sec03-card-f04.question_text: What does a license suspension do to your card and driving privilege?
sec03-card-f04.teaching_text: Do not treat a suspension lightly because driving at all while privileges are temporarily paused triggers harsher criminal and license penalties.

sec03-card-f05.question_text: How does license revocation affect your driving privilege and physical card?
sec03-card-f05.teaching_text: Unlike a brief pause, revocation strips away both your driving privilege and your license for a set statutory or court period.

sec03-card-f06.question_text: When does a Nebraska license suspension or revocation actually end?
sec03-card-f06.teaching_text: Privileges never snap back automatically on a calendar date unless you complete every reinstatement step and pay required state fees.

sec03-card-f07.question_text: What happens to your license and driving privilege during court impoundment?
sec03-card-f07.teaching_text: During impoundment a judge physically holds your plastic credential at the court while barring any driving for the ordered span.

sec03-card-f08.question_text: What does license confiscation mean during an impaired-driving investigation?
sec03-card-f08.teaching_text: Failing an alcohol test or refusing chemical testing lets the investigating officer take your plastic license right at the stop.

sec03-card-f09.question_text: How many days does the temporary license last after an officer confiscates your plastic card?
sec03-card-f09.teaching_text: That brief fifteen-day window gives drivers just enough time to arrange legal steps or permit options before administrative revocation hits.

sec03-card-f10.question_text: What happens when the fifteen-day temporary license ends after an alcohol-test failure or refusal?
sec03-card-f10.teaching_text: Unless an administrative hearing throws out the violation, full license revocation kicks in right as day fifteen closes.

sec03-card-f11.question_text: How can a motor-vehicle homicide affect your Nebraska driver license?
sec03-card-f11.teaching_text: Causing a fatal crash through unlawful operation strips away driving privileges alongside severe felony criminal prosecution.

sec03-card-f12.question_text: What can repeated traffic violations in Nebraska or other states do to your driving privileges?
sec03-card-f12.teaching_text: Tickets earned on out-of-state road trips follow you home and stack with local citations toward losing your driving privilege.

sec03-card-f13.question_text: What licensing consequence can follow from using a motor vehicle to commit a crime?
sec03-card-f13.teaching_text: Even when the underlying offense is not a routine traffic error, using a car in criminal conduct jeopardizes your license.

sec03-card-f14.question_text: How can an arrest or conviction for impaired driving under drugs or alcohol impact your license?
sec03-card-f14.teaching_text: Notice that even an impaired-driving arrest can trigger administrative loss before criminal court finishes a conviction.

sec03-card-f15.question_text: What can happen if you falsify or hide information on a licensing application?
sec03-card-f15.teaching_text: Hiding prior suspensions or faking application details voids trust in your record and can cost you your license.

sec03-card-f16.question_text: What licensing penalty can hit a driver who leaves a crash without giving a name and address?
sec03-card-f16.teaching_text: Driving off from a collision without exchanging your name and address turns an accident into a license-losing offense.

sec03-card-f17.question_text: What can happen to your license if you ignore a court judgment or citation in Nebraska or elsewhere?
sec03-card-f17.teaching_text: Tossing an out-of-state speeding ticket in the glovebox triggers interstate noncompliance holds that suspend your Nebraska license.

sec03-card-f18.question_text: How can alcoholism or drug addiction affect a person's Nebraska driving privileges?
sec03-card-f18.teaching_text: Uncontrolled substance dependence threatens roadway safety around the clock, giving the state grounds to withdraw driving privileges.

sec03-card-f19.question_text: What licensing consequence can result from fleeing an officer to avoid arrest?
sec03-card-f19.teaching_text: Refusing to pull over endangers everyone on the road and exposes the driver to losing their license.

sec03-card-f20.question_text: What can happen to your license if you refuse a chemical test?
sec03-card-f20.teaching_text: Saying no to chemical breath, blood, or urine testing carries its own independent path to losing your license.

sec03-card-f21.question_text: Can reckless driving cost you your Nebraska driver license?
sec03-card-f21.teaching_text: Operating with willful disregard for people or property stacks heavy points and can strip away your license.

sec03-card-f22.question_text: What can happen if you lend your driver license to someone else?
sec03-card-f22.teaching_text: Letting a friend borrow your plastic card for driving or age checks puts your own driving privileges on the chopping block.

sec03-card-f23.question_text: What licensing penalty can follow from having someone else take your licensing test?
