sec03-card-f23.teaching_text: Sending a stand-in to pass written or road evaluations is licensing fraud that strips away driving privileges.

sec03-card-f24.question_text: How can a conviction for failing to show proof of insurance affect your license?
sec03-card-f24.teaching_text: Keep active auto insurance proof accessible on every trip because a no-proof conviction can cost you your license.

sec03-card-f25.question_text: What non-driving court noncompliance can lead to losing a Nebraska driver license?
sec03-card-f25.teaching_text: Falling behind on court-ordered child support or alimony can trigger administrative suspension even with a spotless driving record.

sec03-card-f26.question_text: When can a driver under twenty-one lose driving privileges over driver-improvement training?
sec03-card-f26.teaching_text: Ignoring required improvement training after hitting six points in a year turns a fixable warning into lost privileges.

sec03-card-f27.question_text: What licensing consequence can strike a driver who transports a child while intoxicated?
sec03-card-f27.teaching_text: Putting an impaired driver behind the wheel with a minor aboard triggers severe criminal charges and license loss.

sec03-card-f28.question_text: Until what age is a teen barred from getting another permit after violating school learner, school, or learner permit terms?
sec03-card-f28.teaching_text: Violating early permit rules does more than cancel your current card by blocking any replacement permit until birthday sixteen.

sec03-card-f29.question_text: What happens automatically if a driver accumulates twelve points within two years?
sec03-card-f29.teaching_text: Hitting twelve points inside any twenty-four-month span triggers automatic six-month operator-license revocation without needing a judge's order.

sec03-card-f30.question_text: What action does the DMV's point-revocation letter direct the driver to take?
sec03-card-f30.teaching_text: Once that revocation notice arrives, holding onto your plastic card instead of turning it in violates state law.

sec03-card-f31.question_text: What maximum fine and jail sentence can follow from failing to surrender a revoked license?
sec03-card-f31.teaching_text: Keeping a revoked card in your wallet risks up to five hundred dollars in fines, thirty county-jail days, or both.

sec03-card-f32.question_text: What training course must a driver pay for and finish to reinstate after point revocation?
sec03-card-f32.teaching_text: Point reinstatement requires completing at least four hours of DMV-approved driver education and training at your own expense.

sec03-card-f33.question_text: How long must financial-responsibility proof stay active after a point revocation ends?
sec03-card-f33.teaching_text: Dropping certified insurance coverage early during those three post-revocation years triggers a fresh suspension right away.

sec03-card-f34.question_text: How long are driving privileges removed for a second Nebraska point revocation within five years?
sec03-card-f34.teaching_text: Maxing out twelve points again inside five years jumps the revocation penalty from six months all the way to three years.

sec03-card-f35.question_text: How many points does a motor-vehicle-homicide conviction add to a Nebraska record?
sec03-card-f35.teaching_text: Twelve points from a single motor-vehicle-homicide conviction hits the full revocation threshold all by itself.

sec03-card-f36.question_text: How many points does a third drunk-driving offense carry?
sec03-card-f36.teaching_text: While an initial impaired-driving conviction adds six points, a third offense lands the full twelve-point maximum at once.

sec03-card-f37.question_text: How many points come from failing to report a crash to law enforcement?
sec03-card-f37.teaching_text: Skipping a required police crash report puts six points on your record, halfway to automatic revocation.

sec03-card-f38.question_text: How many points are assessed for failing to help after a crash involving the driver?
sec03-card-f38.teaching_text: Every involved driver owes reasonable post-crash assistance, and failing to help adds six immediate record points.

sec03-card-f39.question_text: How many points does driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs carry?
sec03-card-f39.teaching_text: A single alcohol- or drug-impaired driving conviction drops six points onto your record alongside court and administrative penalties.

sec03-card-f40.question_text: How many points does willful reckless driving carry in Nebraska?
sec03-card-f40.teaching_text: Notice the one-point jump from standard five-point reckless driving up to six points when recklessness is willful.

sec03-card-f41.question_text: How many points does leaving a crash scene carry?
sec03-card-f41.teaching_text: Fleeing the scene of a collision stacks six points on your driving record in a single conviction.

sec03-card-f42.question_text: How many points does standard reckless driving carry?
sec03-card-f42.teaching_text: Keep the driving-conduct ladder straight on exam day with reckless at five points between six-point willful and four-point careless.

sec03-card-f43.question_text: How many points are added for careless driving?
sec03-card-f43.teaching_text: Careless driving sits at four points on Nebraska's point ladder, one step above three-point negligent driving.

sec03-card-f44.question_text: How many points come from failing to yield when a pedestrian is injured?
sec03-card-f44.teaching_text: Injuring a walker doubles the failure-to-yield point hit from two points without injury up to four points.

sec03-card-f45.question_text: How many points come from reading, typing, or sending written messages on a handheld phone while driving?
sec03-card-f45.teaching_text: Texting on a handheld device adds three adult record points, unlike the one-point wireless penalty under teen permits.

sec03-card-f46.question_text: How many points does negligent driving carry?
sec03-card-f46.teaching_text: Negligent driving lands three points on your record, just below four-point careless driving.

sec03-card-f47.question_text: How many points come from passing a school bus with its stop arm extended and red lights flashing?
sec03-card-f47.teaching_text: Blowing past a stopped school bus endangers children crossing the street and puts three points on your record.

sec03-card-f48.question_text: How many points come from failing to yield to a pedestrian when no injury occurs?
sec03-card-f48.teaching_text: Cutting off a pedestrian in a crosswalk still costs two points even when the walker avoids getting hurt.

sec03-card-f49.question_text: How many points does unlawfully blocking the driver's view carry?
sec03-card-f49.teaching_text: Hanging bulky objects or clutter that obstructs clear sightlines through glass adds one point to your record.

sec03-card-f50.question_text: How many driving-record points are assigned for refusing an alcohol-content test?
sec03-card-f50.teaching_text: Even though refusal triggers a full year of administrative revocation, its point-schedule entry itself adds just one point.

sec03-card-f51.question_text: How many points does a child-restraint violation add to your driving record?
sec03-card-f51.teaching_text: Failing to secure a young rider in a proper child restraint adds one driving-record point alongside citation fines.

sec03-card-f52.question_text: Which insurer form usually satisfies financial-responsibility proof after a point revocation?
sec03-card-f52.teaching_text: Standard wallet insurance cards are not enough after point revocation because your insurer normally files written Form SR-twenty-two certification.

sec03-card-f53.question_text: What usually serves as financial-responsibility proof after a court-ordered license revocation?
sec03-card-f53.teaching_text: Just like point revocations, reinstating after a court-ordered revocation typically requires written Form SR-twenty-two certification filed by your insurer.

sec03-card-f54.question_text: Which three violations does the handbook list as carrying zero points?
sec03-card-f54.teaching_text: Parking tickets, loud muffler citations, and forgetting to carry your valid operator card on your person add zero points.

sec03-card-f55.question_text: How long is a sobriety program permit valid when issued after the subsequent-offense or refusal waiting period?
sec03-card-f55.teaching_text: Serving the mandatory front-end holdoff leaves your sobriety permit active only for whatever balance remains on the one-year revocation.

sec03-card-f56.question_text: How long does a later-offense interlock permit last during administrative revocation?
sec03-card-f56.teaching_text: After a repeat administrative revocation offense clears its initial holdoff, the interlock permit covers the rest of that one-year span.

sec03-card-f57.question_text: Once the chemical-test refusal waiting period ends, how long does the interlock permit remain valid?
sec03-card-f57.teaching_text: Because ninety days pass before eligibility starts, the refusal interlock permit runs only through the rest of the one-year revocation.

sec03-card-f58.question_text: What offense level and license penalty apply to fleeing an officer over a misdemeanor, traffic infraction, or moving local ordinance?
sec03-card-f58.teaching_text: Speeding away from a routine moving-violation stop escalates a minor ticket into a Class I misdemeanor and potential license revocation.

sec03-card-f59.question_text: Under the general juvenile-court offense rule for age seventeen and younger, how long is an unlicensed youth barred from getting a permit or license?
sec03-card-f59.teaching_text: Having no permit yet does not dodge juvenile-court consequences because eligibility gets frozen for thirty days.

sec03-card-r01.question_text: For citations dated November fourteen, two thousand twenty or later, how many points come from driving one through five miles per hour over the limit?
sec03-card-r01.teaching_text: Modern citations for one through five miles per hour over add zero points whether inside or outside city limits.

sec03-card-r02.question_text: Inside city limits, how many points come from speeding more than five up to ten miles per hour over the limit?
sec03-card-r02.teaching_text: Urban streets carry denser pedestrian and cross-traffic hazards, so going six through ten over inside town costs two points.

sec03-card-r03.question_text: Inside city limits, how many points come from going over ten up through thirty-five miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r03.teaching_text: Exceeding a city limit by more than ten up through thirty-five miles per hour jumps the penalty to three points.

sec03-card-r04.question_text: How many points come from going over thirty-five miles per hour past the speed limit anywhere in Nebraska?
sec03-card-r04.teaching_text: Whether on an urban street or open rural highway, topping thirty-five miles per hour over the limit adds four points.

sec03-card-r05.question_text: Outside city limits, how many points come from going over five up through ten miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r05.teaching_text: Compare city and rural brackets carefully because six through ten over adds one point outside town versus two inside.

sec03-card-r06.question_text: Outside city limits, how many points come from going over ten up through fifteen miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r06.teaching_text: Rural highways split the middle speed bracket so exceeding the limit by eleven through fifteen miles per hour adds two points.

sec03-card-r07.question_text: Outside city limits, how many points come from going over fifteen up through thirty-five miles per hour past the limit?
sec03-card-r07.teaching_text: Once rural speeding passes fifteen miles per hour over the limit up through thirty-five, the hit reaches three points.

sec03-card-r08.question_text: How many points come from driving on an expired license or without ever having been licensed?
sec03-card-r08.teaching_text: Keep forgetting your valid wallet card at zero points distinct from driving expired or never licensed at one point.

sec03-card-r09.question_text: How many points come from a passenger violation on a provisional or school permit?
sec03-card-r09.teaching_text: Carrying unauthorized peers on either a school permit or provisional permit puts one point onto your driving record.

sec03-card-r10.question_text: How many points come from breaking wireless-device restrictions on a school learner, learner, school, or provisional permit?
sec03-card-r10.teaching_text: Any moving wireless violation across Nebraska's four teen and learner permits adds one point plus the statutory fine.

sec03-card-r11.question_text: Which date determines when points from a traffic conviction are counted on your record?
sec03-card-r11.teaching_text: Delaying a court appearance will not game the two-year point window because points attach retroactively to the violation date.

sec03-card-r12.question_text: How long do traffic convictions remain on your Nebraska driving record?
sec03-card-r12.teaching_text: Even after active points stop counting at two years, the underlying traffic conviction stays on your record five years.

sec03-card-r13.question_text: When do active points stop counting toward revocation?
sec03-card-r13.teaching_text: Keep two years for active point totals separate from five years for how long convictions stay on your record.

sec03-card-r14.question_text: How does Nebraska score an out-of-state traffic conviction on your point record?
sec03-card-r14.teaching_text: Getting convicted of speeding or reckless driving in another state adds the exact same Nebraska points as local roads.

sec03-card-r15.question_text: How can a non-CDL, non-CLP driver earn a two-point credit on their record?
sec03-card-r15.teaching_text: You must finish the DMV-approved improvement course before committing the violation that would push your total to twelve points.

sec03-card-r16.question_text: How often can an eligible driver use the driver-improvement course two-point credit?
sec03-card-r16.teaching_text: Because that two-point cushion is available only once every five years, consistent safe habits matter far more than classes.

sec03-card-r17.question_text: What can a court order upon a serious traffic conviction?
sec03-card-r17.teaching_text: Even below twelve total points, a judge sentencing a serious traffic conviction can revoke your license for a set term.

sec03-card-r18.question_text: After a court-ordered revocation ends, how long must financial-responsibility proof stay in place?
sec03-card-r18.teaching_text: Both point revocations and court-ordered revocations share the same three-year post-revocation financial-responsibility tail.

sec03-card-r19.question_text: Who returns an impounded license once the ordered impoundment period finishes?
sec03-card-r19.teaching_text: Unlike revocations that require full DMV reinstatement, an impounded card comes back from the court when its term expires.

sec03-card-r20.question_text: Compare the revocation penalties for driving during general court impoundment versus underage drinking or refusal impoundment?
sec03-card-r20.teaching_text: Getting caught behind the wheel during general court impoundment brings a one-year revocation, whereas underage alcohol impoundment brings six months.

sec03-card-r21.question_text: For a driver aged twenty or younger, how long does a conviction under the zero point zero two percent alcohol rule impound the license?
sec03-card-r21.teaching_text: Even a single drink can put a driver twenty or younger at zero point zero two percent and trigger thirty-day impoundment.

sec03-card-r22.question_text: How long does a zero point zero two percent underage alcohol conviction stay on the record before deletion?
sec03-card-r22.teaching_text: Unlike standard five-year convictions, this underage zero point zero two percent entry clears off the record after ninety days.

sec03-card-r23.question_text: How many days of court impoundment result from an underage chemical-test refusal conviction?
sec03-card-r23.teaching_text: Refusing an underage alcohol check triples court impoundment from thirty days up to a full ninety days.

sec03-card-r24.question_text: How long does an underage refusal conviction stay on the driving record before deletion?
sec03-card-r24.teaching_text: Keep ninety-day impoundment separate from the one-hundred-twenty-day record retention span on an underage refusal conviction.

sec03-card-r25.question_text: What penalty hits a driver convicted of driving during underage drinking or refusal impoundment?
sec03-card-r25.teaching_text: Breaking a thirty- or ninety-day underage court impoundment escalates your penalty into a full six-month court revocation.

sec03-card-r26.question_text: What roadside events allow immediate license confiscation under administrative revocation?
sec03-card-r26.teaching_text: Either failing an alcohol test or refusing an alcohol-or-drug chemical test triggers immediate administrative confiscation.

sec03-card-r27.question_text: How long is the administrative revocation for a first alcohol-test failure?
sec03-card-r27.teaching_text: Memorize one hundred eighty days specifically for an initial administrative alcohol-test failure rather than six calendar months.

sec03-card-r28.question_text: How long is the administrative revocation for a later alcohol-test failure?
sec03-card-r28.teaching_text: A subsequent alcohol-test failure doubles administrative revocation up to one full year.

sec03-card-r29.question_text: How long is the administrative revocation for refusing a chemical alcohol-or-drug test?
sec03-card-r29.teaching_text: Refusing chemical testing skips the shorter initial tier and lands a full one-year administrative revocation immediately.

sec03-card-r30.question_text: How can a driver contest an administrative license revocation?
sec03-card-r30.teaching_text: Drivers who dispute the administrative revocation grounds may formally request a departmental hearing.

sec03-card-r31.question_text: How does requesting an administrative-revocation hearing affect interlock or sobriety permit access?
sec03-card-r31.teaching_text: Filing an administrative hearing challenge bars driving on an interlock or sobriety permit unless a court later orders it at sentencing.

sec03-card-r32.question_text: What driving option can open up if an eligible driver waives the administrative-revocation hearing?
sec03-card-r32.teaching_text: Giving up the administrative hearing fight lets eligible drivers apply to keep driving with an ignition-interlock permit during revocation.

sec03-card-r33.question_text: What credential must a twenty-four over seven sobriety program participant with a court-certified order obtain?
sec03-card-r33.teaching_text: Court enrollment alone does not authorize driving until the participant secures an active Sobriety Program Permit from licensing.

sec03-card-r34.question_text: When does a sobriety program permit actually allow driving during administrative revocation?
sec03-card-r34.teaching_text: An unrelated point suspension or child-support hold still blocks driving even if you hold a sobriety program permit.

sec03-card-r35.question_text: For a subsequent offense, when does sobriety-permit eligibility begin?
sec03-card-r35.teaching_text: Notice the clock starts after the fifteen-day temporary license expires rather than on the night of the traffic stop.

sec03-card-r36.question_text: After a chemical-test refusal, when does sobriety-permit eligibility start?
sec03-card-r36.teaching_text: Refusing chemical testing doubles the post-temporary holdoff from forty-five days to ninety days before sobriety-permit eligibility.

sec03-card-r37.question_text: Which two events revoke a sobriety program permit?
sec03-card-r37.teaching_text: Receiving either a conviction abstract that revokes driving privileges or a court order canceling the permit ends sobriety privileges.

sec03-card-r38.question_text: What age and licensing history must a sobriety-permit participant have?
sec03-card-r38.teaching_text: Participants must be eighteen or older and have previously passed testing for or held a Class M or Class O credential.

sec03-card-r39.question_text: Does a Nebraska sobriety program permit allow operating a commercial motor vehicle?
sec03-card-r39.teaching_text: Commercial rigs are strictly off-limits under a sobriety program permit regardless of what class you held before.

sec03-card-r40.question_text: What travel is permitted under an employment drive permit issued after a point or child-support revocation?
sec03-card-r40.teaching_text: Side errands for groceries or social stops violate an employment drive permit, which covers only direct work travel.

sec03-card-r41.question_text: Can an employment drive permit authorize commercial motor vehicle operation?
sec03-card-r41.teaching_text: Even if you drive trucks for a living, an employment drive permit never authorizes operating commercial motor vehicles.

sec03-card-r42.question_text: When may an eligible first-time administrative-revocation offender apply for an interlock permit?
sec03-card-r42.teaching_text: First-time administrative offenders skip the forty-five- and ninety-day holdoffs and become eligible right after the fifteen-day temporary card ends.

sec03-card-r43.question_text: For a first-time administrative-revocation offender, how long does the interlock permit last and what vehicle may be driven?
sec03-card-r43.teaching_text: For six months, every trip must be inside a vehicle fitted with a functioning ignition-interlock breath device.

sec03-card-r44.question_text: For a later administrative-revocation offense, when does interlock-permit eligibility start?
sec03-card-r44.teaching_text: Just like sobriety permits, repeat administrative offenders serve forty-five no-driving days after temporary-license expiration before interlock eligibility.

sec03-card-r45.question_text: After a chemical-test refusal, when does interlock-permit eligibility start?
sec03-card-r45.teaching_text: Refusing chemical testing imposes ninety hard no-driving days after your fifteen-day temporary license expires before interlock eligibility.

sec03-card-r46.question_text: Up to how many years may a court or the Board of Pardons order ignition-interlock use?
sec03-card-r46.teaching_text: Depending on prior convictions and driving history, courts or the Board of Pardons can mandate interlock devices for fifteen years.

sec03-card-r47.question_text: What is the base criminal classification for tampering with, circumventing, or driving without a required interlock device?
sec03-card-r47.teaching_text: Having a friend blow into the mouthpiece or borrowing an unequipped car commits a Class I misdemeanor even sober.

sec03-card-r48.question_text: How does the handbook describe the alcohol-related felony enhancement for interlock tampering, circumvention, or driving unequipped?
sec03-card-r48.teaching_text: Adding alcohol escalates interlock tampering or driving unequipped to a Class IV felony, though the handbook omits the alcohol-threshold unit.

sec03-card-r49.question_text: Which prior license classes qualify a driver for interlock-permit eligibility?
sec03-card-r49.teaching_text: Unlike sobriety permits that allow prior testing, interlock eligibility requires having previously held a Class M or Class O credential.

sec03-card-r50.question_text: Where may a driver travel on a medical-hardship permit issued after point revocation?
sec03-card-r50.teaching_text: Medical-hardship permits strictly cover round-trip travel from home or work to the designated treatment facility and nowhere else.

sec03-card-r51.question_text: What offense classification and license consequence apply to fleeing to avoid arrest for a felony?
sec03-card-r51.teaching_text: Running from police to dodge a felony arrest adds a separate Class IV felony charge and can revoke your license.

sec03-card-r52.question_text: Up to how long can your driver license be revoked upon conviction for fleeing a motor-vehicle crash scene?
sec03-card-r52.teaching_text: Beyond adding six points, a hit-and-run conviction can strip away your driver license for as long as one year.

sec03-card-r53.question_text: For a driver aged twenty or younger, how long does a first minor-in-possession conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r53.teaching_text: You do not even need to be near a car for an underage alcohol-possession conviction to impound your license thirty days.

sec03-card-r54.question_text: For someone aged twenty or younger, how long does a second minor-in-possession conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r54.teaching_text: A repeat underage alcohol-possession conviction triples court license impoundment from thirty days up to ninety days.

sec03-card-r55.question_text: For someone aged twenty or younger, how long does a third or later minor-in-possession conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r55.teaching_text: A third underage possession offense sidelines your permit or license in court impoundment for a full twelve months.

sec03-card-r56.question_text: How long is an unlicensed person aged twenty or younger barred from getting a permit or license after first, second, or third minor-in-possession convictions?
sec03-card-r56.teaching_text: Unlicensed youths face the exact same thirty-day, ninety-day, and twelve-month lockouts before they can obtain any permit or license.

sec03-card-r57.question_text: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, how long does a first juvenile-court drug conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r57.teaching_text: Juvenile-court drug impoundments mirror the minor-in-possession ladder, starting with thirty days off the road on offense one.

sec03-card-r58.question_text: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, how long does a second juvenile-court drug conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r58.teaching_text: A repeat juvenile-court drug conviction triples the driving-document impoundment period to ninety days.

sec03-card-r59.question_text: For a juvenile aged seventeen or younger, how long does a third or later juvenile-court drug conviction impound the permit or license?
sec03-card-r59.teaching_text: Reaching a third juvenile-court drug offense impounds the youth's permit or license for twelve full months.

sec03-card-r60.question_text: How long is an unlicensed juvenile aged seventeen or younger barred from getting a permit or license after first, second, or third drug convictions?
sec03-card-r60.teaching_text: Unlicensed juveniles aged seventeen or younger face thirty-day, ninety-day, and twelve-month eligibility lockouts across repeat drug convictions.

sec03-card-r61.question_text: For any juvenile-court offense involving someone aged seventeen or younger, how long may the court impound driving documents?
sec03-card-r61.teaching_text: Even when a juvenile-court case has nothing to do with cars, alcohol, or drugs, judges can impound driving cards thirty days.

sec03-card-r62.question_text: What must a driver finish before a new license can be issued after suspension, revocation, cancellation, or disqualification?
sec03-card-r62.teaching_text: Whether a prior card was suspended, revoked, cancelled, or disqualified, clearing full state reinstatement is mandatory before new issuance.

sec04-card-f01.question_text: How does Nebraska law treat driving while impaired by alcohol or another drug?
sec04-card-f01.teaching_text: Exam questions often test prescription or other drugs alongside alcohol because impairment from any substance breaks the law.

sec04-card-f02.question_text: Who is barred from drinking alcohol or holding an open alcoholic container inside a vehicle on Nebraska public roads or public parking areas?
sec04-card-f02.teaching_text: Many teens mistakenly think sober passengers can hold open drinks, or forget public parking lots count just like highways.

sec04-card-f03.question_text: Which two core driving essentials can alcohol and other drugs impair?
sec04-card-f03.teaching_text: Safe driving relies on sharp judgment first and physical handling second, and intoxicants degrade both before a crash happens.

sec04-card-f04.question_text: Which age group falls under Nebraska's zero-tolerance alcohol rule?
sec04-card-f04.teaching_text: Even if an eighteen-year-old holds a full adult operator license, underage alcohol limits still govern every drive until twenty-one.

sec04-card-f05.question_text: What are the legal consequences of providing alcohol to a minor in Nebraska?
sec04-card-f05.teaching_text: Handing drinks to underage friends is not just a criminal offense, because you can be sued for crash damages afterward.

sec04-card-f06.question_text: At what minimum blood alcohol concentration does driving become unlawful for someone younger than twenty-one?
sec04-card-f06.teaching_text: A single drink can easily push a teen past this tiny threshold, triggering license loss long before adult intoxication.

sec04-card-f07.question_text: What blood alcohol concentration makes driving unlawful for any driver regardless of age or vehicle type?
sec04-card-f07.teaching_text: Test writers try to trick you with vehicle exceptions, yet this ceiling applies across the board to every motorist.

sec04-card-f08.question_text: What two types of consequences can follow a violation of Nebraska's alcohol-driving provisions?
sec04-card-f08.teaching_text: Losing driving privileges through an administrative track can happen fast even while separate court charges are still pending.

sec04-card-f09.question_text: What agreement do you automatically make regarding chemical alcohol-or-drug testing simply by driving on Nebraska roads?
sec04-card-f09.teaching_text: You do not sign a separate roadside waiver because operating on public pavement already counts as legal consent when asked.

sec04-card-f10.question_text: Under Nebraska's implied-consent rule, how is refusing an officer's request for a blood, breath, or urine test classified?
sec04-card-f10.teaching_text: Saying no at the roadside does not dodge trouble because the refusal itself creates an independent criminal charge.

sec04-card-f11.question_text: What happens if, in the officer's judgment, a driver fails to complete a requested blood, breath, or urine test?
sec04-card-f11.teaching_text: Pretending to blow weakly into a breath machine will not outsmart the law since the officer judges completion.

sec04-card-f12.question_text: How long is the administrative license revocation for refusing a requested chemical test under Nebraska's implied-consent law?
sec04-card-f12.teaching_text: Exam options mix up shorter suspensions, so lock in a full twelve months of administrative revocation for saying no.

sec04-card-f13.question_text: Criminal test-refusal penalties match an impaired-driving conviction at what minimum blood alcohol concentration?
sec04-card-f13.teaching_text: Nebraska punishes refusal just like aggravated high-alcohol driving so motorists cannot gain softer sentencing by withholding samples.

sec04-card-f14.question_text: Depending on prior convictions, for how many years can a criminal refusal conviction revoke your license alongside fines and jail?
sec04-card-f14.teaching_text: Stacking multi-year court revocation on top of fines and jail time can wipe out driving freedom into adulthood.

sec04-card-f15.question_text: Can significant driving impairment happen before a motorist reaches zero point zero eight percent alcohol concentration?
sec04-card-f15.teaching_text: Treating the adult legal ceiling like a safe-driving score gets drivers arrested and wrecked when skills fade early.

sec04-card-f16.question_text: How does a person's body weight relate to alcohol in the bloodstream?
sec04-card-f16.teaching_text: Two friends drinking identical amounts can reach very different concentrations because smaller bodies have less tissue water.

sec04-card-f17.question_text: Why can biological sex influence how quickly alcohol is absorbed?
sec04-card-f17.teaching_text: Matching someone drink for drink is risky because differences in body composition change how concentrated alcohol becomes.

sec04-card-f18.question_text: What role does food in the digestive tract play when someone consumes alcohol?
sec04-card-f18.teaching_text: Drinking on an empty stomach lets alcohol enter the bloodstream faster, catching drivers off guard before they notice.

sec04-card-f19.question_text: How does the amount of time spent drinking connect to alcohol absorption?
sec04-card-f19.teaching_text: Downing several drinks quickly overwhelms the body and spikes blood concentration much faster than spacing drinks apart.

sec04-card-f20.question_text: If a drinker appears calm and in control socially, what can still be true behind the wheel?
sec04-card-f20.teaching_text: Practiced drinkers may walk and chat smoothly at a party while split-second traffic reflexes are already dangerously degraded.

sec04-card-f21.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does simple reaction time become impaired?
sec04-card-f21.teaching_text: At half the general unlawful ceiling, slower brake-pedal response adds critical car lengths when traffic halts ahead.

sec04-card-f22.question_text: Beginning at what blood alcohol concentration does choosing between possible driving responses become impaired?
sec04-card-f22.teaching_text: Real traffic rarely gives one simple cue, and hesitating between braking or steering starts at remarkably low alcohol.

sec04-card-f23.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does tracking a single object become impaired?
sec04-card-f23.teaching_text: Keeping eyes locked smoothly on even one lead car falters well before a driver feels legally drunk.

sec04-card-f24.question_text: How does the alcohol concentration that impairs tracking several objects compare with tracking just one object?
sec04-card-f24.teaching_text: Intersections force you to watch cross traffic, pedestrians, and signals together, which breaks down earlier than single-target focus.

sec04-card-f25.question_text: Below what blood alcohol concentration can dividing attention across multiple driving tasks already be impaired?
sec04-card-f25.teaching_text: Steering while scanning mirrors and checking speed requires constant multitasking that unravels after very small amounts of alcohol.

sec04-card-f26.question_text: What happens to understanding sights and sounds once blood alcohol concentration reaches zero point zero five percent?
sec04-card-f26.teaching_text: Seeing a hazard or hearing a horn does not save you if your brain takes extra moments to interpret it.

sec04-card-f27.question_text: Which visual mechanics decline at a blood alcohol concentration of zero point zero five percent?
sec04-card-f27.teaching_text: Sluggish eye movements and trouble blending images from both eyes distort depth perception during night lane changes.

sec04-card-f28.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does seeing detail in a moving object decline?
sec04-card-f28.teaching_text: Spotting whether a cyclist or pedestrian near the curb is stepping out gets harder when dynamic vision blurs.

sec04-card-f29.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration are hand-and-foot coordination and precise muscular tasks impaired?
sec04-card-f29.teaching_text: Smooth steering inputs and crisp pedal transitions turn clumsy before a motorist ever reaches the general unlawful threshold.

sec04-card-f30.question_text: Which six vehicle-handling and judgment skills are impaired at zero point zero eight percent blood alcohol concentration?
sec04-card-f30.teaching_text: Every major physical and spatial driving task fails together at this point, explaining why crash risk skyrockets.
sec04-card-f30.must_match_memory_hook: Steering braking speed lanes gears distance

visual_sync.text_span: Steering braking speed lanes gears distance

sec04-card-f31.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does emergency response become impaired?
sec04-card-f31.teaching_text: Sudden tire blowouts or darting hazards demand instant composure that degrades at just half the adult per-se limit.

sec04-card-f32.question_text: What transportation step should you take ahead of time whenever drinking is planned?
sec04-card-f32.teaching_text: Waiting until after drinks start to figure out a ride home lets impaired judgment talk you into driving.

sec04-card-f33.question_text: What is the only thing that actually lowers alcohol concentration in the body and clears its effects?
sec04-card-f33.teaching_text: Classic test distractors push coffee, cold showers, or fresh air, which merely create a wide-awake impaired motorist.

sec04-card-f34.question_text: How does Nebraska's handbook contrast single-task focus up to zero point zero eight percent alcohol concentration against divided attention?
sec04-card-f34.teaching_text: Staring hard at pavement lines fools drinkers into feeling capable while hazards outside that narrow tunnel go unnoticed.

sec04-card-f35.question_text: What fine, fee, and license-record penalty come with a Nebraska child-restraint violation?
sec04-card-f35.teaching_text: Unlike standard adult belt citations, failing to secure a child adds a driving-record point alongside monetary court expenses.

sec04-card-f36.question_text: What monetary penalty applies to a general occupant-protection violation in Nebraska?
sec04-card-f36.teaching_text: Watch how the exam separates general belt tickets from child-seat violations by leaving off the operator-record point here.

sec04-card-r01.question_text: What authority does a primary-law violation give a police officer?
sec04-card-r01.teaching_text: Officers need no other traffic infraction to pull you over when you break a primary safety rule.

sec04-card-r02.question_text: When can an officer issue a citation for a secondary-law violation?
sec04-card-r02.teaching_text: Getting pulled over and cited for speeding or a broken lamp opens the door to added secondary belt fines.

sec04-card-r03.question_text: Do vehicle airbags replace the need to buckle your seat belt?
sec04-card-r03.teaching_text: Without a buckled belt holding you in position, an unrestrained body can slide into an inflating bag violently.

sec04-card-r04.question_text: What happens to crash protection when occupants wear seat belts together with airbags?
sec04-card-r04.teaching_text: Seat belts restrain your torso during rollovers and side impacts while airbags cushion forward head and chest motion.

sec04-card-r05.question_text: Where should you place your hands on the steering wheel in a vehicle equipped with a steering-wheel airbag?
sec04-card-r05.teaching_text: Gripping high across the top rim puts forearms and wrists directly in the explosive path of airbag deployment.

sec04-card-r06.question_text: Which passengers face injury risk from an airbag deployment even during a low-speed crash?
sec04-card-r06.teaching_text: Rapid inflation force hits smaller or frailer bodies hard when they sit too close to dashboard modules.

sec04-card-r07.question_text: Up through what age should children ride in a rear seat for greatest crash safety?
sec04-card-r07.teaching_text: Keeping kids twelve and under in the back row shields developing bones from front-seat impact forces and airbags.

sec04-card-r08.question_text: Where must you never place a rear-facing infant seat in an airbag-equipped vehicle?
sec04-card-r08.teaching_text: A deploying passenger airbag strikes the back of a rear-facing carrier right behind the baby's head with lethal force.

sec04-card-r09.question_text: At least how many inches should a driver keep between their body and the steering wheel in an airbag-equipped vehicle?
sec04-card-r09.teaching_text: Giving the bag ten inches of room lets the cushion inflate fully before catching your chest safely.

sec04-card-r10.question_text: Until what age or manufacturer limit must a young child ride rear-facing?
sec04-card-r10.teaching_text: Rear-facing shells cradle a toddler's heavy head and fragile neck far better than turning forward too early.

sec04-card-r11.question_text: Which children must be properly secured in a federally approved child safety seat in Nebraska?
sec04-card-r11.teaching_text: Adult lap and shoulder belts cut across a small child's stomach and neck unless a booster positions them properly.

sec04-card-r12.question_text: When must a child younger than eight ride in a nonfront seat?
sec04-card-r12.teaching_text: Only if every restraint-equipped rear spot already holds another child under eight may a young rider sit up front.

sec04-card-r13.question_text: Is Nebraska's child-safety-seat and nonfront-seating requirement for children younger than eight enforced as a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r13.teaching_text: An officer spotting an unrestrained six-year-old or improper front seating can pull the vehicle over immediately.

sec04-card-r14.question_text: What restraint rule applies to passengers from age eight until age eighteen?
sec04-card-r14.teaching_text: Youth passengers must stay secured in either a seat belt or an appropriate safety seat depending on body size.

sec04-card-r15.question_text: Is Nebraska's restraint requirement for children aged eight through seventeen a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r15.teaching_text: Test questions contrast under-eight primary enforcement against ages eight through seventeen, where another violation triggers the stop.

sec04-card-r16.question_text: Who is prohibited from riding in vehicle cargo areas in Nebraska?
sec04-card-r16.teaching_text: Pickup beds and unseated cargo spaces have zero crash restraints, turning bumps or hard braking into fatal ejections.

sec04-card-r17.question_text: Is the ban on children younger than eighteen riding in cargo areas enforced as a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r17.teaching_text: Police do not wait for speeding or equipment violations when minors are riding loose in a pickup bed.

sec04-card-r18.question_text: Who must be buckled when the driver holds a provisional operator permit or a school permit?
sec04-card-r18.teaching_text: Even back-seat adult passengers must click their belts whenever a provisional or school-permit teen is driving.

sec04-card-r19.question_text: Is the all-passenger buckle rule for provisional or school permit drivers a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r19.teaching_text: Getting stopped for curfew, phone use, or speeding lets the officer cite unbuckled riders in a permit-driven car.

sec04-card-r20.question_text: Which seating positions inside a vehicle are covered by child-restraint requirements?
sec04-card-r20.teaching_text: Moving a child to a third row never waives safety-seat or seat-belt duties inside a moving vehicle.

sec04-card-r21.question_text: What restraint rule must childcare providers follow when transporting children?
sec04-card-r21.teaching_text: Transporting groups of kids carries zero shortcut allowances, requiring proper safety seats or belts for every rider.

sec04-card-r22.question_text: What professional consequence can hit a childcare provider who fails to secure children properly?
sec04-card-r22.teaching_text: Beyond traffic fines, skipping child restraints can revoke the provider's state authorization to operate a childcare business.

sec04-card-r23.question_text: Is the child-restraint requirement for childcare providers enforced as a primary or secondary law?
sec04-card-r23.teaching_text: Officers can pull over a childcare van immediately whenever any transported child appears unrestrained.

sec04-card-r24.question_text: What occupant protection must drivers and front-seat passengers use?
sec04-card-r24.teaching_text: Front-seat riders face windshield and dashboard impacts first, making belts or child seats mandatory up front.

sec04-card-r25.question_text: Does Nebraska's front-seat occupant-protection requirement also apply inside autocycles?
sec04-card-r25.teaching_text: Three-wheeled enclosed autocycles drive with steering wheels and seats, so occupants must buckle up just like car drivers.

sec04-card-r26.question_text: Is the general seat-belt requirement for drivers and front-seat passengers a primary or secondary law in Nebraska?
sec04-card-r26.teaching_text: Even though police cite adult front belts after another stop, unbuckled crashes never wait for a traffic ticket.

sec04-card-r27.question_text: May you ever leave a child alone or unsupervised inside a vehicle?
sec04-card-r27.teaching_text: Parked cabins trap lethal heat rapidly and curious kids can shift gears, operate power windows, or wander into traffic.

sec04-card-r28.question_text: How quickly can a pet left inside a parked vehicle suffer fatal heatstroke, even in mild weather?
sec04-card-r28.teaching_text: Closed car glass acts like a greenhouse even on pleasant days, cooking cabin air far faster than owners expect.

sec04-card-r29.question_text: What is the handbook's direct rule about leaving pets inside a motor vehicle?
sec04-card-r29.teaching_text: Cracking a window barely slows rising interior temperatures, so bring animals along only when they never stay parked.

sec04-card-r30.question_text: In a passenger vehicle, how does swerving to avoid a deer affect your risk of death or injury?
sec04-card-r30.teaching_text: Yanking the wheel turns a survivable bumper strike into a deadly rollover, tree impact, or head-on collision.

sec04-card-r31.question_text: What three actions should you take when hitting a deer is unavoidable?
sec04-card-r31.teaching_text: Straight-line braking sheds massive crash energy while keeping your crumple zones and airbags aligned with the impact.

sec04-card-r32.question_text: What three dangerous maneuvers must you avoid when a deer enters your path?
sec04-card-r32.teaching_text: Ditches, guardrails, and oncoming trucks kill far more motorists than controlled straight-ahead braking ever does.

sec04-card-r33.question_text: Which three driving habits lower your chance of colliding with a deer?
sec04-card-r33.teaching_text: Outdriving your headlights at night means a deer standing in dark rural highway lanes appears too late to stop.

sec04-card-r34.question_text: During which daily hours, seasons, and roadside settings should you watch closely for deer?
sec04-card-r34.teaching_text: Breeding and migration in spring and fall send deer across roads near creeks and timber right as twilight dims.

sec04-card-r35.question_text: Why must you keep scanning for more deer right after spotting one near the road?
sec04-card-r35.teaching_text: Drivers relax as the first deer clears the shoulder, then strike the second or third animal sprinting behind it.

sec05-card-f01.question_text: Which two personal states can influence your driving performance?
sec05-card-f01.teaching_text: Fatigue, illness, anger, or stress quietly dull hazard awareness and pedal timing just when traffic gets tight.

sec05-card-f02.question_text: Which two mental habits does the handbook connect directly with safe driving?
sec05-card-f02.teaching_text: Losing your temper or letting thoughts drift turns routine lane merges into aggressive mistakes or missed brake lights.

sec05-card-f03.question_text: How does clear forward vision help a motorist while driving?
sec05-card-f03.teaching_text: Scanning well ahead down your lane gives you space to read signs, brake smoothly, and steer around trouble.

sec05-card-f04.question_text: What traffic awareness benefit comes from peripheral vision?
sec05-card-f04.teaching_text: Side vision alerts you to cross-street cars, cyclists, and pedestrians entering your path before they reach dead center.

sec05-card-f05.question_text: Why is judging distance an essential visual skill behind the wheel?
sec05-card-f05.teaching_text: Misjudging gaps when turning left, passing, or following another car leads straight to intersection and rear-end crashes.

sec05-card-f06.question_text: How do horns, sirens, and nearby vehicle sounds help you drive?
sec05-card-f06.teaching_text: Blasting cabin music drowns out emergency sirens or warning horns hidden behind blind corners and tall trucks.

sec05-card-f07.question_text: What two ways does the handbook advise drivers with hearing loss to stay safe?
sec05-card-f07.teaching_text: Frequent mirror sweeps and active head checks make up for missed sound cues when traffic closes in quickly.

sec05-card-f08.question_text: Who should you consult when an illness or disability might affect your ability to drive safely?
sec05-card-f08.teaching_text: A doctor can spot hidden dizziness, slow reflexes, or vision limits before a medical flare-up causes a wreck.

sec05-card-f09.question_text: Reporting a seizure or loss of consciousness within what lookback window before licensing or renewal triggers a physician's safe-driving certification?
sec05-card-f09.teaching_text: Blacking out behind the wheel leaves a moving vehicle completely unguided, so recent episodes demand medical verification.

sec05-card-f10.question_text: What routine checkup does the handbook recommend for drivers who have diabetes?
sec05-card-f10.teaching_text: Blood-sugar shifts and diabetic eye changes can gradually blur road signs and night contrast without obvious warning.

sec05-card-f11.question_text: What step should people with heart disease, high blood pressure, or circulation problems take before driving?
sec05-card-f11.teaching_text: Sudden lightheadedness or fainting from cardiovascular trouble can strike mid-turn unless a physician confirms stability.

sec05-card-f12.question_text: When does diabetes, a heart condition, or another medical issue require a physician's safe-driving certification for license issuance or renewal?
sec05-card-f12.teaching_text: Exam questions test the three-month consciousness-loss trigger rather than assuming every chronic diagnosis automatically blocks renewal.

sec05-card-f13.question_text: Whom should you ask about how a prescription medicine might affect your driving?
sec05-card-f13.teaching_text: Legal prescriptions can still cause heavy drowsiness or blurred sight that impairs lane control like alcohol.

sec05-card-f14.question_text: What should you inspect before driving after taking nonprescription medicine?
sec05-card-f14.teaching_text: Everyday allergy, cold, and sleep remedies sold on store shelves frequently carry drowsiness warnings that slow braking.

sec05-card-f15.question_text: What does the handbook state about nitrous oxide use inside a vehicle operating on a Nebraska public roadway?
sec05-card-f15.teaching_text: Inhaling nitrous oxide starves the brain of oxygen and causes instant dizziness or blackouts in live traffic.

sec05-card-f16.question_text: What legal basis does the handbook describe for a police officer conducting a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f16.teaching_text: Either a traffic infraction like a dark tail lamp or suspected criminal activity justifies flashing patrol lights.

sec05-card-f17.question_text: How should both the driver and passengers act when emergency lights appear behind the vehicle?
sec05-card-f17.teaching_text: Keeping everyone composed inside the cabin lowers tension and prevents misunderstandings from the first second.

sec05-card-f18.question_text: How and where should you pull over when an officer signals a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f18.teaching_text: Using your turn indicator tells the officer you saw the lights while you clear active travel lanes.

sec05-card-f19.question_text: Which two vehicle systems should you switch off once stopped by an officer?
sec05-card-f19.teaching_text: Turning off the motor shows you will stay put while silencing music lets everyone hear instructions clearly.

sec05-card-f20.question_text: When should you step out of your vehicle during a police stop?
sec05-card-f20.teaching_text: Popping your door open unannounced looks alarming to an approaching officer and exposes you to passing traffic.

sec05-card-f21.question_text: What lighting step should you take if an officer pulls you over at night?
sec05-card-f21.teaching_text: Lighting up the interior removes dark shadows so the officer can see calm, empty hands immediately.

sec05-card-f22.question_text: Why might an officer shine a bright spotlight on your vehicle during a stop?
sec05-card-f22.teaching_text: Expect bright beams in your mirrors at night as routine safety lighting rather than staring backward into glare.

sec05-card-f23.question_text: Where should you keep your hands while waiting during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f23.teaching_text: Rummaging in consoles or pockets before the officer arrives creates unnecessary alarm during the roadside walk-up.

sec05-card-f24.question_text: Whose instructions must both you and your passengers follow during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-f24.teaching_text: Clear compliance by drivers and passengers alike keeps everyone safe alongside fast-moving shoulder traffic.

sec05-card-r01.question_text: From which side of your vehicle might an officer approach during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-r01.teaching_text: On busy highways, officers frequently walk up to the passenger window to avoid standing near speeding traffic.

sec05-card-r02.question_text: Which window should you roll down so you and the officer can speak easily?
sec05-card-r02.teaching_text: Opening the window on whichever side the officer walks up prevents muffled shouting through closed glass.

sec05-card-r03.question_text: When must you inform the officer if there is a weapon inside the vehicle?
sec05-card-r03.teaching_text: Calmly stating a weapon's presence right away while keeping hands on the wheel prevents dangerous surprises.

sec05-card-r04.question_text: When should you reach for your driver license or vehicle paperwork during a stop?
sec05-card-r04.teaching_text: Digging into a glove box or jacket before the officer reaches your window can look like hiding contraband.

sec05-card-r05.question_text: What may you do if a nonuniformed officer conducts a stop without showing official credentials?
sec05-card-r05.teaching_text: Plainclothes officers normally display identification right away, and verifying credentials protects motorists when none appear.

sec05-card-r06.question_text: What does an officer ordinarily explain and ask during a routine traffic stop?
sec05-card-r06.teaching_text: Routine questions about where you are headed are standard patrol procedure rather than something to argue over.

sec05-card-r07.question_text: Which three documents does an officer ordinarily request during a traffic stop?
sec05-card-r07.teaching_text: Keeping current registration and proof of insurance organized avoids frantic searching when patrol lights flash.

sec05-card-r08.question_text: What should you do before retrieving requested paperwork stored out of easy reach?
sec05-card-r08.teaching_text: Telling the officer your registration is in the glove compartment and waiting for an okay keeps movements predictable.

sec05-card-r09.question_text: How should you behave if the officer directs you to exit the vehicle?
sec05-card-r09.teaching_text: Standing exactly where instructed keeps both you and the officer clear of blind spots and passing lane mirror strikes.

sec05-card-r10.question_text: What three enforcement outcomes can result from a police traffic stop?
sec05-card-r10.teaching_text: Depending on the offense severity and driver record, stops end anywhere from a verbal reminder to custody.

sec05-card-r11.question_text: What may you do if an officer does not explain the enforcement action being taken?
sec05-card-r11.teaching_text: Knowing whether you received a warning or citation ensures you never miss a court date or payment deadline.

sec05-card-r12.question_text: How should you ask if you need an officer to clarify an instruction or action?
sec05-card-r12.teaching_text: Polite questions clear up confusion fast without escalating a routine roadside stop into a confrontation.

sec05-card-r13.question_text: Where should you challenge an officer's decision instead of arguing on the roadside?
sec05-card-r13.teaching_text: Roadside debates never cancel a written citation and only prolong time spent parked near hazardous highway traffic.

sec05-card-r14.question_text: Does signing and accepting a traffic ticket admit that you are guilty?
sec05-card-r14.teaching_text: Your signature on the citation simply confirms receipt and your promise to respond through proper court channels.

sec05-card-r15.question_text: What serious consequence can happen if you refuse to sign a traffic ticket?
sec05-card-r15.teaching_text: Turning a minor traffic citation into handcuffs happens fast when a driver stubbornly refuses to acknowledge the ticket.

sec05-card-r16.question_text: Whom may you ask to speak with regarding an officer's conduct, and when is best?
sec05-card-r16.teaching_text: Contacting a supervisor promptly after the stop preserves fresh details without interfering with roadside traffic control.

sec05-card-r17.question_text: What coverage obligation applies to motor vehicles operated on Nebraska public roadways?
sec05-card-r17.teaching_text: Driving uninsured on public streets leaves crash victims unpaid and exposes your registration and license to suspension.

sec05-card-r18.question_text: What minimum liability dollar amount covers injury to or death of one person in a single crash?
sec05-card-r18.teaching_text: Memorize Nebraska's three liability numbers carefully because test choices swap single-person and total-crash amounts.

sec05-card-r19.question_text: What minimum liability dollar amount covers injury to or death of two or more people in one crash?
sec05-card-r19.teaching_text: Even when several people are hurt in one wreck, payouts remain subject to the separate per-person limit.

sec05-card-r20.question_text: What minimum liability dollar amount covers damage to other people's property in a single crash?
sec05-card-r20.teaching_text: Liability property coverage pays for the other motorist's smashed car, fence, or building rather than your own bumper.

sec06-card-f01.question_text: What reports does the federal highway safety agency collect regarding vehicles, tires, and child safety seats?
sec06-card-f01.teaching_text: Drivers reporting strange brake failures, tire blowouts, or broken car-seat latches help investigators spot nationwide patterns.

sec06-card-f02.question_text: What safety outcome can reporting a vehicle problem help trigger?
sec06-card-f02.teaching_text: One owner's complaint can connect the dots on a hidden engineering flaw that manufacturers must repair free.

sec06-card-f03.question_text: Which four lighting components are included in the handbook's required equipment list?
sec06-card-f03.teaching_text: Working lamps let you see dark pavement ahead while telling drivers behind you every brake press and turn.

sec06-card-f04.question_text: Alongside lighting and brakes, which three sound, visibility, and exhaust items sit on the required-equipment list?
sec06-card-f04.teaching_text: Streaking blades blind you in storms, missing mufflers create illegal noise and fumes, and dead horns silence warnings.

sec06-card-f05.question_text: What vehicle detail determines which seat-belt equipment is legally required?
sec06-card-f05.teaching_text: Older classic cars follow the federal belt standards in effect when they were originally built.

sec06-card-f06.question_text: Which two separate braking systems does the handbook require on a motor vehicle?
sec06-card-f06.teaching_text: Your hydraulic pedal system handles traffic stops while the mechanical parking brake holds hills and backs up failures.

sec06-card-f07.question_text: What material must every window on a motor vehicle use?
sec06-card-f07.teaching_text: Tempered and laminated automotive glass crumbles or holds together in a crash instead of slicing occupants with shards.

sec06-card-f08.question_text: What tire type and minimum tread depth appear on Nebraska's required-equipment list?
sec06-card-f08.teaching_text: Worn-down slick rubber cannot channel rainwater away, making hydroplaning and long skids far more likely.

sec06-card-f09.question_text: What rule governs items hung from mirrors or posted on vehicle windows?
sec06-card-f09.teaching_text: Oversized air fresheners, parking tags, or stickers create blind spots wide enough to hide a crossing pedestrian.

sec06-card-f10.question_text: Which unique code should vehicle owners look up when checking for manufacturer safety recalls?
sec06-card-f10.teaching_text: Searching your exact seventeen-character serial code reveals whether unrepaired airbag or brake recalls apply to your car.

sec06-card-f11.question_text: Where on the vehicle is the vehicle identification number usually located?
sec06-card-f11.teaching_text: Looking through the outside bottom corner of the front glass lets you read the stamped plate easily.

sec06-card-f12.question_text: What happens in many vehicles when the ignition key is turned to the lock position?
sec06-card-f12.teaching_text: Anti-theft column pins snap into place once the cylinder hits lock, freezing wheel rotation until unlocked.

sec06-card-f13.question_text: Why must you never turn the ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is still moving?
sec06-card-f13.teaching_text: Shutting the key all the way back during a roll clamps the steering column and sends you straight off-road.

sec06-card-f14.question_text: When does the handbook recommend having the steering-wheel lock inspected?
sec06-card-f14.teaching_text: Catching a sticky or worn ignition lock at the shop prevents sudden column binding on the road.

sec06-card-f15.question_text: When is sunscreen material allowed below the upper windshield mark in Nebraska?
sec06-card-f15.teaching_text: Dark tint across the main windshield area blocks night sightlines and hides eye contact at four-way stops.

sec06-card-f16.question_text: What is the maximum luminous reflectance allowed on front side windows?
sec06-card-f16.teaching_text: Mirror-like metallic film above thirty-five percent bounces blinding sunlight into adjacent drivers' eyes and hides cabin occupants.

sec06-card-f17.question_text: Below what light-transmission percentage is tint prohibited on front side windows?
sec06-card-f17.teaching_text: Limo-dark front glass makes spotting cyclists or pedestrians in dim intersections dangerous after sunset.

sec06-card-f18.question_text: What is the maximum luminous reflectance allowed under the printed rear-window rule?
sec06-card-f18.teaching_text: Just like front side glass, rear windows cannot wear overly shiny reflective tint that dazzles following traffic.

sec06-card-f19.question_text: Below what light-transmission percentage is tint prohibited on the rear window?
sec06-card-f19.teaching_text: Notice the exam contrast: rear glass allows darker twenty-percent transmission while front side windows require thirty-five.

sec06-card-f20.question_text: How does the handbook classify owning or operating a vehicle that violates Nebraska's window-tint restrictions?
sec06-card-f20.teaching_text: Both the registered owner and whoever drives the illegally tinted car can face criminal misdemeanor charges.

sec06-card-r01.question_text: How much air pressure can a normal tire naturally lose over a single month?
sec06-card-r01.teaching_text: Slow permeation through rubber adds up quietly over a season until underinflated sidewalls overheat at highway speed.

sec06-card-r02.question_text: How often, and in which tires, should you check air pressure?
sec06-card-r02.teaching_text: Forgetting the spare leaves you stranded on the shoulder when you swap out a flat for an empty spare.

sec06-card-r03.question_text: What tool should you rely on when checking tire inflation?
sec06-card-r03.teaching_text: Eyeballing modern radial sidewalls fails because a tire can lose dangerous pressure while still looking round.

sec06-card-r04.question_text: Where on the vehicle do you normally find the recommended tire-pressure numbers?
sec06-card-r04.teaching_text: Automakers print exact front and rear inflation specs right on the driver door jamb for quick checks.

sec06-card-r05.question_text: When should you measure tire pressure to get an accurate reading?
sec06-card-r05.teaching_text: Rolling friction heats trapped air and artificially inflates readings until the car rests at least three hours.

sec06-card-r06.question_text: Where do you press the pressure gauge to take a tire reading?
sec06-card-r06.teaching_text: Sealing the gauge squarely onto the valve stem pops the inner pin cleanly for a crisp reading.

sec06-card-r07.question_text: Does the tiny puff of air during a gauge reading hurt tire pressure?
sec06-card-r07.teaching_text: A quick press barely changes inflation, whereas holding the stem crooked and hissing bleeds real pressure.

sec06-card-r08.question_text: Should you match your gauge reading to the vehicle door label and manual or to the number molded on the tire sidewall?
sec06-card-r08.teaching_text: Sidewall numbers show maximum cold burst rating rather than the automaker's smooth, balanced handling pressure.

sec06-card-r09.question_text: How should you correct tire inflation that reads either too high or too low?
sec06-card-r09.teaching_text: Both overinflated center wear and underinflated shoulder heat hurt braking grip until matched to target pressure.

sec06-card-r10.question_text: How often should you inspect your tires visually for damage and tread wear?
sec06-card-r10.teaching_text: Spotting sidewall bulges, embedded nails, or uneven wear early prevents high-speed interstate blowouts.

sec06-card-r11.question_text: How do you position a penny when checking tire tread depth?
sec06-card-r11.teaching_text: Testing the most worn groove catches alignment bald spots that a deeper outer groove would hide.

sec06-card-r12.question_text: What should you see on the coin when your tire passes the handbook's penny comparison?
sec06-card-r12.teaching_text: Seeing the entire top of Lincoln's head means rubber has worn down past the safe two-thirty-seconds mark.

sec06-card-r13.question_text: What happens to vehicle performance when tire tread wears shallower than the penny-test benchmark?
sec06-card-r13.teaching_text: Bald grooves cannot bite slush or evacuate standing rain, stretching stopping distances right when roads turn slick.

sec07-card-f01.question_text: In what order does an ordinary automated traffic signal cycle through its colors?
sec07-card-f01.teaching_text: Expecting yellow right after green keeps you from getting surprised when an approach phase prepares to stop.

sec07-card-f02.question_text: What are the only two situations where Nebraska drivers may disregard a traffic signal's normal command?
sec07-card-f02.teaching_text: Outside live police hand commands or making room for emergency sirens, signal phases stay strictly binding.

sec07-card-f03.question_text: How must you treat a dark traffic signal when no officer, flagger, or backup control is present?
sec07-card-f03.teaching_text: Blowing straight through a dead power-outage intersection causes high-speed T-bone crashes from cross streets.

sec07-card-f04.question_text: Where must you stop at a steady red light, and how long must you wait absent a permitted turn?
sec07-card-f04.teaching_text: Halting completely ahead of the stop bar, crosswalk, or corner protects cross traffic and walkers.

sec07-card-f05.question_text: What does a steady yellow signal warn, and what must you do if you have not entered the intersection?
sec07-card-f05.teaching_text: Braking smoothly before the entry line prevents getting caught inside the intersection when cross traffic gets green.

sec07-card-f06.question_text: What should you do when the light turns steady yellow after your vehicle is already in the intersection?
sec07-card-f06.teaching_text: Slamming on the brakes mid-intersection strands your car directly across perpendicular travel lanes.

sec07-card-f07.question_text: How does Nebraska law treat hitting the gas to beat a changing traffic signal?
sec07-card-f07.teaching_text: Flooring the pedal on stale yellow turns minor timing miscalculations into violent red-light collisions.

sec07-card-f08.question_text: What two conditions govern moving forward when a traffic signal turns green?
sec07-card-f08.teaching_text: Green grants permission rather than a guarantee, so never charge into blocked lanes or lingering cross traffic.

sec07-card-f09.question_text: What three steps are required before proceeding past a flashing red traffic signal?
sec07-card-f09.teaching_text: Treating a flashing red lens like a slowdown warning instead of a stop command causes broadside wrecks.

sec07-card-f10.question_text: Must you stop for flashing red railroad-crossing lights when the tracks look empty?
sec07-card-f10.teaching_text: Curves, brush, or freight cars on near sidings can hide a fast locomotive until seconds before arrival.

sec07-card-f11.question_text: How should you drive through an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow signal?
sec07-card-f11.teaching_text: Staying sharp and easing speed gives you time to react if cross-street traffic misjudges a gap.

sec07-card-f12.question_text: Why are standalone flashing yellow warning beacons mounted alongside certain signs or roadway spots?
sec07-card-f12.teaching_text: Blinking amber lamps draw your eyes early to school zones, sharp curves, or hidden hazards ahead.

sec07-card-f13.question_text: What two rules apply whenever a red arrow is lit for your movement?
sec07-card-f13.teaching_text: Unlike a circular red light, an illuminated red arrow forbids turning in its pointed direction altogether.

sec07-card-f14.question_text: How must you respond to a steady yellow arrow when you have not yet entered the intersection?
sec07-card-f14.teaching_text: Protected turn time is ending, so braking cleanly before the line avoids turning across released oncoming cars.

sec07-card-f15.question_text: What should you do if a turn arrow switches to steady yellow after you already entered the intersection?
sec07-card-f15.teaching_text: Completing your turn promptly clears the center of the intersection before cross-street phases turn green.

sec07-card-f16.question_text: Is accelerating to beat a changing yellow arrow legal in Nebraska?
sec07-card-f16.teaching_text: Whip-turning at high speed as protected arrow time expires risks rolling or clipping oncoming traffic.

sec07-card-f17.question_text: Which movement and lane rule apply when a flashing yellow arrow is displayed?
sec07-card-f17.teaching_text: Permissive blinking arrows allow turning only from the designated turn bay once conflicting traffic leaves room.

sec07-card-f18.question_text: To whom must you yield before turning on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec07-card-f18.teaching_text: Oncoming straight cars and parallel walkers share green time while your yellow arrow flashes.

sec07-card-f19.question_text: From where and under what roadway condition may you follow an illuminated green arrow?
sec07-card-f19.teaching_text: Cutting into a turn from an outer through lane causes side-swipe collisions with legal turn-bay drivers.

sec07-card-f20.question_text: What three checks are mandatory before making any permitted turn at a red light?
sec07-card-f20.teaching_text: Rolling corners without scanning both directions and crosswalks causes preventable pedestrian and cross-traffic hits.

sec07-card-f21.question_text: When may a Nebraska driver turn right after halting at a round red light?
sec07-card-f21.teaching_text: Always scan corners and signal mast arms for No Turn On Red plaques before easing right.

sec07-card-f22.question_text: Which street configuration permits turning left after halting at a round red light?
sec07-card-f22.teaching_text: Turning left on red from or onto a two-way street crosses active opposing lanes illegally.

sec07-card-f23.question_text: Can you make a right or one-way left turn against a steady red arrow?
sec07-card-f23.teaching_text: Intersections use red arrows specifically where blind angles or dedicated pedestrian phases make red-light turns unsafe.

sec07-card-r01.question_text: How do reversible-lane signs and overhead signals manage traffic across the day?
sec07-card-r01.teaching_text: Commuter corridors switch middle lanes inward mornings and outward evenings, making habit-based entry dangerous.

sec07-card-r02.question_text: What does an overhead red X command regarding the lane underneath?
sec07-card-r02.teaching_text: Driving under a red cross puts you straight into a closed lane or head-on opposing rush traffic.

sec07-card-r03.question_text: Why must you vacate a lane displaying a steady yellow X as soon as safe?
sec07-card-r03.teaching_text: A solid yellow overhead cross means directional flow is about to close and flip against you.

sec07-card-r04.question_text: What does a downward-pointing overhead green arrow indicate about the lane beneath it?
sec07-card-r04.teaching_text: Seeing green pointing straight down confirms reversible traffic currently flows in your direction.

sec07-card-r05.question_text: What kind of crossing location does a pedestrian hybrid beacon control?
sec07-card-r05.teaching_text: Midblock crosswalks along multi-lane streets use hybrid beacons so walkers can halt fast traffic on demand.

sec07-card-r06.question_text: How are the red and yellow lenses arranged on a pedestrian hybrid beacon?
sec07-card-r06.teaching_text: Recognizing the T-shaped three-lens cluster keeps drivers from confusing pedestrian beacons with railroad flashers.

sec07-card-r07.question_text: What are the first two light stages when a pedestrian triggers a hybrid beacon?
sec07-card-r07.teaching_text: Blinking amber wakes approaching drivers up before transitioning into a standard steady yellow warning.

sec07-card-r08.question_text: How should drivers interpret the steady-yellow phase of a pedestrian hybrid beacon?
sec07-card-r08.teaching_text: Just like an intersection signal, steady yellow warns that solid red stop lamps are coming next.

sec07-card-r09.question_text: What must drivers do while both top red lights on a hybrid beacon shine steadily?
sec07-card-r09.teaching_text: Solid twin reds mean pedestrians have the WALK indication and full priority across the roadway.

sec07-card-r10.question_text: How do the hybrid beacon's red lenses behave once WALK changes to flashing DON'T WALK?
sec07-card-r10.teaching_text: Wig-wag alternating reds match the pedestrian countdown while walkers finish clearing the crossing.

sec07-card-r11.question_text: Before proceeding on alternating red hybrid-beacon lights, what must you do and verify?
sec07-card-r11.teaching_text: Checking both your own lane and neighboring lanes prevents striking a walker hidden beside another stopped car.

sec07-card-r12.question_text: What does a pedestrian hybrid beacon display after its pedestrian crossing cycle ends?
sec07-card-r12.teaching_text: Resting unlit until someone presses the curb button keeps main-street traffic flowing smoothly.

sec07-card-r13.question_text: Does a dark midblock pedestrian hybrid beacon require an all-way stop like a dead intersection signal?
sec07-card-r13.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily at an idle midblock beacon invites rear-end collisions from drivers expecting continuous flow.

sec07-card-r14.question_text: Which four critical traffic commands are associated with red sign coloring?
sec07-card-r14.teaching_text: Red always signals immediate danger, priority limits, or prohibited movement where ignoring the post causes wrecks.

sec07-card-r15.question_text: What category of roadway message does standard yellow sign coloring convey?
sec07-card-r15.teaching_text: Yellow alerts you ahead of curves, intersections, or surface surprises so you adjust speed early.

sec07-card-r16.question_text: Which five community and non-motorist zones use fluorescent yellow-green warning signs?
sec07-card-r16.teaching_text: High-visibility yellow-green pops in peripheral vision wherever children, cyclists, or walkers cross traffic.

sec07-card-r17.question_text: What special kind of roadway situation do pink traffic signs address?
sec07-card-r17.teaching_text: Coral-pink panels alert drivers to unplanned crashes, wildfires, floods, or emergency detours ahead.

sec07-card-r18.question_text: What kind of travel information do green highway signs provide?
sec07-card-r18.teaching_text: Scanning overhead green boards early lets you pick exit lanes smoothly without last-second swerves.

sec07-card-r19.question_text: What roadside facilities do blue highway signs identify for travelers?
sec07-card-r19.teaching_text: Blue boards point drivers toward medical care, rest stops, gas, food, and lodging near exits.

sec07-card-r20.question_text: What category of enforceable rules do white background signs communicate?
sec07-card-r20.teaching_text: White panels state binding traffic laws such as maximum speeds, lane rules, and parking restrictions.

sec07-card-r21.question_text: What roadway activity do orange background signs warn drivers about?
sec07-card-r21.teaching_text: Spotting orange ahead means crews, cones, and narrowed lanes require extra space and slower speeds.

sec07-card-r22.question_text: What types of destinations are marked by brown roadside signs?
sec07-card-r22.teaching_text: Brown boards guide visitors cleanly toward state parks, campgrounds, exhibits, and historic landmarks.

sec09-card-f01.question_text: What three core traffic functions do pavement markings perform on Nebraska roads?
sec09-card-f01.teaching_text: Roadway paint carries binding legal authority alongside vertical posts rather than serving as optional lane decor.

sec09-card-f02.question_text: Which paint colors or combinations appear in standard Nebraska road markings?
sec09-card-f02.teaching_text: Reading stripe color tells you immediately whether adjacent traffic moves with you or straight toward you.

sec09-card-f03.question_text: What relationship between traffic streams does a yellow center line indicate?
sec09-card-f03.teaching_text: Keeping yellow center stripes to your left prevents drifting head-on into oncoming vehicles.

sec09-card-f04.question_text: Under what condition may you pass on the left across a broken yellow center line?
sec09-card-f04.teaching_text: Dashed yellow allows overtaking only when far sightlines are clear and zero oncoming traffic approaches.

sec09-card-f05.question_text: When a solid yellow stripe runs beside a broken yellow stripe, which side is allowed to pass?
sec09-card-f05.teaching_text: Crossing when the solid stripe sits next to your lane sends you blind over crests or curves.

sec09-card-f06.question_text: What passing rule applies where double solid yellow lines mark the center of the road?
sec09-card-f06.teaching_text: Twin solid yellow bars lock down overtaking from both directions across blind hills, curves, or busy blocks.

sec09-card-f07.question_text: When does the Nebraska manual allow turning left across double solid yellow lines?
sec09-card-f07.teaching_text: Double yellow bans overtaking slower traffic, yet permits safe left turns into or out of private access unless signed otherwise.

sec09-card-f08.question_text: Who uses a center lane bordered by solid outer and broken inner yellow lines, and for what move?
sec09-card-f08.teaching_text: Drivers from both directions pull into the middle bay to wait out oncoming gaps before turning left.

sec09-card-f09.question_text: How must you enter and use a shared center turn lane, and what maneuver is strictly forbidden inside it?
