sec09-card-f09.teaching_text: Cruising down a shared middle bay to overtake backed-up traffic risks a head-on crash with an opposing left-turner.
sec09-card-f09.must_match_memory_hook: Enter cautiously, lefts only, never pass

visual_sync.text_span: Enter cautiously, lefts only, never pass

sec09-card-f10.question_text: Beyond yellow boundary lines, what two visual cues help identify a shared left-turn lane?
sec09-card-f10.teaching_text: Checking both overhead or roadside plaques and painted opposing arrows confirms you are not entering a reversible lane.

sec09-card-f11.question_text: What traffic flow direction is divided by white lane markings?
sec09-card-f11.teaching_text: Seeing white stripes on both sides confirms every neighboring lane travels forward with your stream.

sec09-card-f12.question_text: When may a driver cross a broken white line between lanes?
sec09-card-f12.teaching_text: Dashed white lines allow lane shifts only after signaling and checking mirrors plus blind spots.

sec09-card-f13.question_text: What two intersection purposes do solid white lane lines serve?
sec09-card-f13.teaching_text: Last-second lane hopping right at signal queues clips turning mirrors and triggers rear-end chain reactions.

sec09-card-f14.question_text: What must you do if your lane displays a curved pavement arrow paired with the word ONLY?
sec09-card-f14.teaching_text: Driving straight out of a mandatory turn bay cuts directly across adjacent through traffic.

sec09-card-f15.question_text: Which movements are legal from a lane painted with both a curved arrow and a straight arrow?
sec09-card-f15.teaching_text: Shared option arrows let curb or center lanes handle both turning queues and straight-through flow.

sec09-card-r01.question_text: What does a wide white stop line painted across an intersection approach mark?
sec09-card-r01.teaching_text: Stopping behind the thick white bar keeps your front bumper clear of crossing walkers and turning trucks.

sec09-card-r02.question_text: Where a white stop line is painted, do you stop at the line or even with the sign or signal?
sec09-card-r02.teaching_text: Posts and signal poles often sit behind or beyond the crosswalk, so rolling up to the post blocks walkers.

sec09-card-r03.question_text: About how far ahead of a crosswalk is an urban white stop line typically painted?
sec09-card-r03.teaching_text: Leaving a four-foot buffer gives pedestrians breathing room away from hot hoods and creeping bumpers.

sec09-card-r04.question_text: Does a pedestrian lose crosswalk right-of-way if stripes go only partly across or are unpainted?
sec09-card-r04.teaching_text: Walkers occupying any legal crossing hold priority whether city crews painted full bars, partial lines, or none.

sec09-card-r05.question_text: In which two kinds of neighborhoods should you watch for crosswalks placed midblock?
sec09-card-r05.teaching_text: Kids and neighborhood walkers cross between corners near schools and parks where drivers least expect a stop.

sec09-card-r06.question_text: What hazard ahead is announced by large white R x R lettering painted on your lane?
sec09-card-r06.teaching_text: Pavement stencils back up roadside circles so tall trucks ahead never hide an upcoming rail line.

sec09-card-r07.question_text: What does a solid yellow line painted beside the center line near a railroad crossing prohibit?
sec09-card-r07.teaching_text: Overtaking near tracks blocks your view of flashing lights and risks getting trapped left of queued cars.

sec09-card-r08.question_text: How do rumble strips wake up an inattentive driver, and what two dangers can they warn about?
sec09-card-r08.teaching_text: Grooved asphalt shakes the steering wheel and hums loudly before drowsy drift or missed stop signs turn fatal.

sec09-card-r09.question_text: Where on a roadway might highway engineers place rumble strips?
sec09-card-r09.teaching_text: Edge grooves prevent run-off-road rollovers, center grooves prevent head-on drift, and transverse grooves announce rural stops.

sec09-card-r10.question_text: Why must you use extra caution and never pass inside a two-way center turn lane?
sec09-card-r10.teaching_text: Oncoming drivers enter the exact same middle lane simultaneously, making high-speed passing a head-on trap.

sec09-card-r11.question_text: Who is a designated bicycle lane reserved for on public streets?
sec09-card-r11.teaching_text: Using marked bike lanes as extra motor travel lanes crowds vulnerable cyclists off their protected strip.

sec09-card-r12.question_text: For what three destinations may a motorist legally cross a designated bicycle lane?
sec09-card-r12.teaching_text: Reaching turn bays, street parking, or driveways requires crossing bike paint briefly rather than cruising along it.

sec09-card-r13.question_text: What must you check and do before steering across a bicycle lane?
sec09-card-r13.teaching_text: Right-hook crashes happen when drivers cut across a faster cyclist's path without checking mirrors and right blind spots.

sec09-card-r14.question_text: In what step-by-step sequence should you make a turn across an adjacent bicycle lane?
sec09-card-r14.teaching_text: Merging into a clear dashed bike zone before turning blocks cyclists from getting pinched on your right flank.

sec09-card-r15.question_text: What two things does a painted shared-lane bicycle marking communicate?
sec09-card-r15.teaching_text: Chevrons over a bike stencil remind drivers cyclists belong in the full lane away from opening car doors.

sec09-card-r16.question_text: How much side clearance must be available before you overtake a bicyclist in Nebraska?
sec09-card-r16.teaching_text: Squeezing closer than three feet buffets riders with mirror windblast and leaves zero margin for potholes.

sec12-card-f01.question_text: How should you manage your lane and speed while another driver passes you?
sec12-card-f01.teaching_text: Speeding up traps the passing car in oncoming traffic, while unplanned braking can block their fallback space behind you.

sec12-card-f02.question_text: Which four visual clues on parked cars warn that one may pull into traffic?
sec12-card-f02.teaching_text: Spotting white reverse lamps or angled front tires early gives you time to ease left or cover the brake.

sec12-card-f03.question_text: What does spotting someone sitting behind the wheel of a parked vehicle tell you?
sec12-card-f03.teaching_text: An occupied parked car can swing a door open or nose into your lane before its turn signal ever blinks.

sec12-card-f04.question_text: What hidden hazards can dart into the street from between parked vehicles?
sec12-card-f04.teaching_text: Tall pickups and vans hide small children and animals until the instant they step past the front fender.

sec12-card-f05.question_text: When must you use your turn signal around lanes and individual parking spaces?
sec12-card-f05.teaching_text: Drivers and walkers in busy lots rely on blinkers to anticipate cars swinging into or backing out of stalls.

sec12-card-f06.question_text: What communication step is required when pulling into street traffic from a parking area or alley?
sec12-card-f06.teaching_text: Blinking before nosing across the apron tells approaching motorists which lane direction you intend to join.

sec12-card-f07.question_text: At least how far ahead must you signal before turning or shifting laterally?
sec12-card-f07.teaching_text: Flicking the lever mid-turn gives trailing drivers and cyclists zero warning to adjust their speed or lane position.

sec12-card-f08.question_text: What special lane do double broken yellow lines mark, and what controls its direction?
sec12-card-f08.teaching_text: Commuter corridors flip flow direction between morning and evening rush hours, making overhead lane signals essential checks.

sec12-card-f09.question_text: Which signaling and mirror checks come ahead of every lane change?
sec12-card-f09.teaching_text: Scanning both interior and side glass tracks fast-closing vehicles before you turn your head for the shoulder check.

sec12-card-f10.question_text: What two conflicts must you look for over your shoulder right before changing lanes?
sec12-card-f10.teaching_text: On multilane roads, a driver two lanes over can drift into the exact center gap at the same moment.

sec12-card-f11.question_text: May you switch lanes while crossing through an intersection?
sec12-card-f11.teaching_text: Turning cross-street drivers judge gaps based on your approach lane and get sideswiped when cars weave mid-crossing.

sec12-card-f12.question_text: When should you plan a turn and move into the proper turning lane?
sec12-card-f12.teaching_text: Diving across multiple lanes at the crosswalk forces panic braking and causes classic intersection sideswipes.

sec12-card-f13.question_text: Along with signaling and slowing, where must you check for people and vehicles before turning?
sec12-card-f13.teaching_text: Checking both ahead in the crosswalk and in your mirror prevents clipping walkers or getting rear-ended while slowing.

sec12-card-f14.question_text: Where should your vehicle end a turn, and what comes next?
sec12-card-f14.teaching_text: Swinging wide into an outer lane surprises adjacent traffic, while lingering slow invites rear-end conflicts.

sec12-card-f15.question_text: Where on the roadway should you position and guide your car for a right turn?
sec12-card-f15.teaching_text: Swinging left before turning right tricks cyclists and trailing drivers into squeezing past on your curb side.

sec12-card-f16.question_text: When no center turn lane is marked, which lane starts and finishes a left turn?
sec12-card-f16.teaching_text: Entering the nearest lawful left lane leaves the outer curb lane open for opposing right-turning traffic.

sec12-card-f17.question_text: How are double turn lanes marked, and which lane must curb-lane traffic turn into?
sec12-card-f17.teaching_text: Drifting out of the inside curb path pushes your fender straight into the car turning beside you.

sec12-card-f18.question_text: How do you stay on course when turning from the second turn lane away from the curb?
sec12-card-f18.teaching_text: Tracking the painted guide arc through the intersection keeps both turning streams separated bumper to bumper.

sec12-card-f19.question_text: Where should you steer after signaling for an emergency roadside stop?
sec12-card-f19.teaching_text: Every extra foot onto solid shoulder margin reduces the risk of sleepy highway drivers clipping your mirror.

sec12-card-f20.question_text: How close and in what alignment must you park beside the curb or road edge during a roadside stop?
sec12-card-f20.teaching_text: Leaving the tail angled or more than a foot out narrows the adjacent travel lane unexpectedly.

sec12-card-f21.question_text: Which side of the roadway must you use for that roadside stop, and what is the sole exception?
sec12-card-f21.teaching_text: Facing wrong-way against oncoming curb traffic blinds nighttime drivers with headlights and forces head-on pullouts.

sec12-card-f22.question_text: Which two controls secure a parked vehicle against rolling?
sec12-card-f22.teaching_text: Relying on transmission park pawls alone risks rollaways if a bumper tap or steep grade pops the gear.

sec12-card-f23.question_text: After securing an emergency roadside stop, what four steps come before stepping out?
sec12-card-f23.teaching_text: Checking mirrors before cracking a street-side door keeps passing trucks from shearing the door and hitting you.

sec12-card-r01.question_text: What does the Nebraska handbook say about double parking alongside a stopped or parked vehicle?
sec12-card-r01.teaching_text: Stopping in the live travel lane beside curb-parked cars traps boxed-in drivers and chokes street visibility.

sec12-card-r02.question_text: Which three pedestrian and crossing zones never allow stopping or parking?
sec12-card-r02.teaching_text: Cars parked across walkways force wheelchair users and children out into blind live traffic lanes.

sec12-card-r03.question_text: Within what distance of a stop sign, yield sign, flashing beacon, or traffic-control device is stopping or parking banned?
sec12-card-r03.teaching_text: Tall SUVs and pickups parked right in front of octagon signs hide critical warnings from approaching drivers.

sec12-card-r04.question_text: How far back from an intersection crosswalk does Nebraska's no-parking zone extend?
sec12-card-r04.teaching_text: Keeping twenty feet open at corners preserves mutual sightlines between stepping walkers and turning motorists.

sec12-card-r05.question_text: Where is parking or stopping banned around bridges, highway tunnels, and railroad tracks?
sec12-card-r05.teaching_text: Bridges and tunnels lack emergency shoulders, while cars within fifty feet of rails block crossing sightlines and signals.

sec12-card-r06.question_text: What rules apply to public or private driveways and posted curb restriction signs?
sec12-card-r06.teaching_text: Blocking even a quiet residential apron can trap residents or block emergency ambulance access to a home.

sec12-card-r07.question_text: What minimum distance must you leave open when parking near a fire hydrant?
sec12-card-r07.teaching_text: Fire crews need unobstructed curb room to swing heavy supply couplings onto hydrant outlets during a blaze.

sec12-card-r08.question_text: How must you set the brake and front wheels when parking uphill next to a curb?
sec12-card-r08.teaching_text: Angling tires left lets the back of the right front tire catch gently against the curb if brakes slip.

sec12-card-r09.question_text: Which way do you turn your wheels for downhill curb parking or any hill without a curb?
sec12-card-r09.teaching_text: Pointing tires toward the curb or shoulder guides a rolling car off the roadway instead of into center traffic.

sec12-card-r10.question_text: When are accessible spaces reserved, and what must happen with the qualifying person for legal use?
sec12-card-r10.teaching_text: Borrowing a relative's placard while that person stays home or stays in the car still violates state law.

sec12-card-r11.question_text: Is parking ever allowed inside the striped access aisle next to an accessible stall?
sec12-card-r11.teaching_text: Wheelchair vans deploy side lifts and ramps into that striped zone, trapping disabled riders if a car crowds it.

sec12-card-r12.question_text: What maximum fines does the handbook list for first, second, and third accessible-parking offenses?
sec12-card-r12.teaching_text: Permit exams test all three escalating fine caps to reinforce that accessible spaces are strictly enforced around the clock.

sec12-card-r13.question_text: What enforcement consequence applies if you park blocking a curb cut or wheelchair ramp?
sec12-card-r13.teaching_text: Even outside marked blue stalls, obstructing a sloped sidewalk cut strands mobility-aid users in the gutter.

sec12-card-r14.question_text: Which signs and pavement markings warn drivers of an upcoming railroad crossing?
sec12-card-r14.teaching_text: Rural crossings often lack automated gates, making advance round signs, white pavement letters, and crossbucks your primary warnings.

sec12-card-r15.question_text: How should you control speed and mindset every time you approach railroad tracks?
sec12-card-r15.teaching_text: Freight and maintenance trains run on irregular schedules day and night, surprising locals who assume tracks are quiet.

sec12-card-r16.question_text: Which four crossing warnings require an immediate stop before railroad tracks?
sec12-card-r16.teaching_text: Treating a crossing stop sign, flagger, or flashing red mast as optional pits sheet metal against thousands of tons.

sec12-card-r17.question_text: What must you do when you see an approaching train or hear its whistle close enough to pose danger?
sec12-card-r17.teaching_text: Optical illusions make wide locomotive fronts look far slower than their true closing speed down the rails.

sec12-card-r18.question_text: Where must you stop at a railroad crossing with a stop line versus without one?
sec12-card-r18.teaching_text: Stopping closer than fifteen feet risks overhang strikes from wide railcars, while past fifty blocks rear sightlines.

sec12-card-r19.question_text: May you ever drive around, beneath, or through a railroad crossing gate or barrier?
sec12-card-r19.teaching_text: Weaving around lowered arms invites fatal impacts from fast passenger trains or hidden second-track locomotives.

sec12-card-r20.question_text: What two checks must you complete after stopping before driving across railroad rails?
sec12-card-r20.teaching_text: Queueing behind red-light traffic with your rear bumper hanging over the rails leaves you trapped if gates drop.

sec12-card-r21.question_text: Which two vehicle categories should you expect to stop at railroad crossings even without train warnings?
sec12-card-r21.teaching_text: Tailgating a school bus or fuel tanker toward tracks causes rear-end crashes when they brake for mandatory stops.

sec12-card-r22.question_text: What transmission habit is banned on railroad tracks, and what else must you watch for?
sec12-card-r22.teaching_text: Missing a manual shift can stall the engine across live steel while a second train hides behind the first.

sec12-card-r23.question_text: What is your immediate first priority if your vehicle stalls across a railroad crossing?
sec12-card-r23.teaching_text: Spending precious seconds cranking a dead starter risks lives when a freight train needs over a mile to stop.

sec12-card-r24.question_text: Once everyone is clear of a stalled car and no train is visible, what number does the manual direct you to call?
sec12-card-r24.teaching_text: Reaching railroad dispatch directly is the fastest way to halt rail traffic on that line before a train arrives.

sec12-card-r25.question_text: What must you do if rail traffic is approaching a stalled crossing, and which emergency line should also be called?
sec12-card-r25.teaching_text: Impact scatters heavy car debris down the track bed, so move well away and alert local emergency responders.

sec12-card-r26.question_text: What color is a railroad Emergency Notification System sign, where is it mounted, and who answers?
sec12-card-r26.teaching_text: Knowing to look on the crossbuck post or signal mast saves frantic searching during a track-side emergency.

sec12-card-r27.question_text: What action can railroad dispatchers take when someone calls the ENS emergency number?
sec12-card-r27.teaching_text: Direct radio links let rail control centers warn locomotive engineers miles up the line before they reach your crossing.

sec12-card-r28.question_text: What does the DOT code printed beneath the phone number on a blue ENS sign identify?
sec12-card-r28.teaching_text: Street names often repeat across counties, whereas the unique federal tag tells dispatchers the exact milepost instantly.

sec12-card-r29.question_text: Which four types of crossing hazards can motorists report using the blue ENS sign?
sec12-card-r29.teaching_text: Reporting stuck gates or burned-out flashers protects the next driver before an unwarned train enters town.

sec12-card-r30.question_text: Why do railroad crossings demand extra caution around trains and maintenance rail equipment?
sec12-card-r30.teaching_text: Massive train weight on smooth steel rails stretches emergency braking far beyond a locomotive engineer's visual range.

sec12-card-r31.question_text: What rule applies to trying to beat an approaching train or rail vehicle across the tracks?
sec12-card-r31.teaching_text: Misjudging locomotive closing speed by a single second leaves zero survivability against multi-thousand-ton rail equipment.

sec12-card-r32.question_text: Why does the handbook warn against changing gears while crossing railroad tracks?
sec12-card-r32.teaching_text: Bumpy timber or concrete rail aprons can cause a missed clutch engagement, stranding your car across live rails.

sec08-card-f01.question_text: Which mandatory command belongs exclusively to an eight-sided traffic sign?
sec08-card-f01.teaching_text: Octagonal geometry lets drivers recognize a mandatory intersection halt even from behind or through frost.

sec08-card-f02.question_text: What right-of-way meaning is carried by a triangular traffic sign?
sec08-card-f02.teaching_text: Spotting a three-sided outline tells cross traffic and approaching drivers alike who must give way.

sec08-card-f03.question_text: What does a diamond-shaped warning sign alert you to, and how should you adjust your driving?
sec08-card-f03.teaching_text: Easing off the accelerator at a diamond panel buys extra braking distance before reaching hidden hazards.

sec08-card-f04.question_text: What type of message is generally posted on vertical rectangular road signs?
sec08-card-f04.teaching_text: Tall upright rectangles frame enforceable speed limits, turn rules, and lane commands you must obey.

sec08-card-f05.question_text: What kind of helpful travel details appear on horizontal rectangular signs?
sec08-card-f05.teaching_text: Wide horizontal boards give highway signs room to display town names, exit arrows, and distances.

sec08-card-f06.question_text: Which two school-related zones are marked by a five-sided sign?
sec08-card-f06.teaching_text: House-shaped five-sided silhouettes alert you immediately to watch for young walkers near campuses.

sec08-card-f07.question_text: What restriction does a pennant-shaped traffic sign identify?
sec08-card-f07.teaching_text: Tapering sideways triangles stand out on two-lane highways so drivers abort risky passes before blind hills.

sec08-card-f08.question_text: What four actions do crossbuck and circular railroad warning signs require from approaching drivers?
sec08-card-f08.teaching_text: Quiet cabins mask horn blasts, so scanning both ways and covering the brake prevents deadly track entries.

sec08-card-f09.question_text: What does a numbered plaque mounted directly beneath a railroad crossbuck tell you?
sec08-card-f09.teaching_text: Knowing more than one set of rails crosses the road keeps you alert for hidden second trains.

sec08-card-f10.question_text: When flashing railroad lights activate, what must you do and how long must you wait?
sec08-card-f10.teaching_text: Pulling onto active rails before warning lamps clear risks colliding with fast freight or passenger trains.

sec08-card-f11.question_text: What specific danger must you watch for after one train clears a multiple-track crossing?
sec08-card-f11.teaching_text: A departing caboose on the near track easily hides an express locomotive closing fast on parallel rails.

sec08-card-f12.question_text: At a gated railroad crossing, should you wait for the gate arm to drop before stopping?
sec08-card-f12.teaching_text: Halting as soon as red lamps blink keeps your roof and hood clear of descending gate arms.

sec08-card-f13.question_text: Which two conditions must both be met before you move forward at a gated railroad crossing?
sec08-card-f13.teaching_text: Rolling forward while lamps still blink after gates start rising risks meeting a second approaching train.

sec08-card-f14.question_text: How does Nebraska treat weaving around a lowered railroad crossing gate?
sec08-card-f14.teaching_text: Bypassing dropped crossing arms gambles your life against multi-ton trains unable to stop in time.

sec08-card-f15.question_text: What legal weight do regulatory traffic signs carry for drivers?
sec08-card-f15.teaching_text: Every regulatory board posts an active traffic statute where disobedience brings citations or crashes.

sec08-card-f16.question_text: What universal meaning does a red circle with a diagonal slash over a symbol convey?
sec08-card-f16.teaching_text: Graphic slash emblems communicate instant prohibitions across language barriers before you commit to an illegal move.

sec08-card-f17.question_text: What action is mandatory before entering an intersection controlled by a stop sign?
sec08-card-f17.teaching_text: Slowing to a rolling creep instead of locking wheels briefly misses cross traffic hidden behind pillars.

sec08-card-f18.question_text: Where must your vehicle stop when a white stop line is painted on the approach?
sec08-card-f18.teaching_text: Creeping past the painted limit bar pushes your bumper into pedestrian and cross-street paths.

sec08-card-f19.question_text: Where must you stop at an intersection crosswalk, and does lack of paint change the rule?
sec08-card-f19.teaching_text: Sidewalk extensions form legal crossings even without white stripes, so keep corners clear for walkers.

sec08-card-f20.question_text: Where should you stop when an intersection has neither a painted stop line nor a crosswalk?
sec08-card-f20.teaching_text: Halting just short of cross lanes where you can scan approaching cars keeps your nose out of traffic.

sec08-card-f21.question_text: What speed and stopping obligation applies when approaching a yield sign?
sec08-card-f21.teaching_text: Treating yield as an automatic merge without preparing to halt causes side-impact collisions with through cars.

sec08-card-f22.question_text: What legal cap does a standard speed-limit sign establish?
sec08-card-f22.teaching_text: Exceeding the posted top figure breaks state speed statutes even on dry, empty pavement.

sec08-card-f23.question_text: What maneuver is forbidden wherever a No Left Turn sign stands?
sec08-card-f23.teaching_text: Turning left against a posted ban cuts across oncoming lanes or one-way streets not timed for turns.

sec08-card-f24.question_text: What movement does a posted No Right Turn sign forbid?
sec08-card-f24.teaching_text: Right-turn bans often guard one-way cross streets, transit lanes, or heavy pedestrian crossings.

sec08-card-f25.question_text: What directional maneuver is barred by a No U-Turn sign?
sec08-card-f25.teaching_text: Swinging around across tight medians or busy intersections blocks multiple lanes and surprises fast traffic.

sec08-card-f26.question_text: What must you never do past Wrong Way or Do Not Enter signs, and what roads do they often guard?
sec08-card-f26.teaching_text: Driving beyond either red warning puts you nose-to-nose against expressway off-ramps or one-way streets.

sec08-card-f27.question_text: How may vehicles travel on a roadway marked by a One Way sign?
sec08-card-f27.teaching_text: Checking One Way arrows before turning out of alleys or parking lots prevents wrong-way urban entries.

sec08-card-f28.question_text: What restriction applies at any curb or zone displaying a No Parking sign?
sec08-card-f28.teaching_text: Leaving a car in No Parking zones blocks fire hydrants, sightlines, delivery bays, or rush-hour lanes.

sec08-card-f29.question_text: For what single maneuver may you use a center lane marked Left Turn Only?
sec08-card-f29.teaching_text: Using a center turn bay as a passing lane or merge runway invites head-on collisions.

sec08-card-f30.question_text: Which side of a median, traffic island, or obstruction does a Keep Right sign direct you to pass?
sec08-card-f30.teaching_text: Passing left of a raised island puts your vehicle straight into opposing oncoming lanes.

sec08-card-f31.question_text: What two traffic problems do Slower Traffic Keep Right signs prevent on multilane highways?
sec08-card-f31.teaching_text: Camping below normal pace in left lanes frustrates faster traffic into risky right-side weaving.

sec08-card-f32.question_text: How should you prepare when you pass a Signal Ahead warning sign?
sec08-card-f32.teaching_text: Curves, hills, or rural trees can hide an upcoming intersection until braking distance runs short.

sec08-card-f33.question_text: What upcoming change does a Reduce Speed Ahead sign alert drivers to expect?
sec08-card-f33.teaching_text: Coasting down early lets you match town or school speed caps cleanly right at the regulatory post.

sec08-card-f34.question_text: What hidden or upcoming control does a Stop Ahead warning announce?
sec08-card-f34.teaching_text: Advance notice prevents skidding past rural or blind-curve stop signs at highway speed.

sec08-card-f35.question_text: What upcoming right-of-way control does a Yield Ahead sign warn about?
sec08-card-f35.teaching_text: Early warning gives you time to drop speed and scan cross or ramp traffic before reaching the triangle.

sec08-card-f36.question_text: What roadway change does Divided Highway Begins warn of, and where must you steer?
sec08-card-f36.teaching_text: Staying right of the beginning center island keeps you out of separated opposing lanes.

sec08-card-f37.question_text: What does Divided Highway Ends warn is changing ahead, and how must you position your car?
sec08-card-f37.teaching_text: Forgetting the center barrier ended leads drivers to turn or pass as if still on a one-way roadway.

sec08-card-f38.question_text: What traffic pattern does a Two Way Traffic warning sign tell you to expect?
sec08-card-f38.teaching_text: Leaving a one-way street or divided freeway requires immediate awareness of oncoming cars in the left lane.

sec08-card-r01.question_text: Why is merging unnecessary right at an Added Lane warning sign?
sec08-card-r01.teaching_text: Continuing smoothly in your own lane avoids panic braking or needless swerves alongside ramp traffic.

sec08-card-r02.question_text: What speed guidance is shown on an Advisory Exit Speed sign?
sec08-card-r02.teaching_text: Tight cloverleaf ramps can roll top-heavy cars and trucks that carry freeway pace into the curve.

sec08-card-r03.question_text: How should you respond at a Slippery When Wet warning sign when pavement is damp?
sec08-card-r03.teaching_text: Rain mixes with road oil to slash tire grip, turning abrupt steering or braking into a skid.

sec08-card-r04.question_text: What upcoming roadway change and driver action does a Lane Ends warning announce?
sec08-card-r04.teaching_text: Signaling and matching adjacent-lane gaps early beats getting squeezed onto the shoulder at the taper.

sec08-card-r05.question_text: When must you refuse to drive underneath a bridge or overpass showing a Low Clearance sign?
sec08-card-r05.teaching_text: Wedging a tall truck, camper, or roof load under a low bridge rips roofs off and showers traffic.

sec08-card-r06.question_text: What terrain feature does a Hill warning sign mark, and what check does it advise?
sec08-card-r06.teaching_text: Testing brakes and downshifting before a long descent prevents overheated brake fade halfway down.

sec08-card-r07.question_text: What two responses does a Deer Crossing warning call for?
sec08-card-r07.teaching_text: Deer bolt unpredictably at dawn and dusk, and one spotted in a ditch usually means others follow.

sec08-card-r08.question_text: Do deer cross only where yellow Deer Crossing signs are posted in Nebraska?
sec08-card-r08.teaching_text: Signs mark concentrated crash corridors, yet wildlife can bound across rural highways or town edges anywhere.

sec08-card-r09.question_text: What traffic condition does a Horse-Drawn Vehicle sign warn you to expect?
sec08-card-r09.teaching_text: Closing at highway pace on a five-mile-per-hour buggy leaves seconds to brake gently without spooking horses.

sec08-card-r10.question_text: What three steps apply when approaching a Pedestrian Crossing warning sign?
sec08-card-r10.teaching_text: Easing off the gas early ensures you can halt smoothly if someone steps into the crossing.

sec08-card-r11.question_text: What lies up ahead when you pass a School Advance Crossing sign?
sec08-card-r11.teaching_text: Advance school pentagons give you space to drop speed before reaching children at the curb.

sec08-card-r12.question_text: Where is a School Crossing sign posted, and whose handheld signs must you obey there?
sec08-card-r12.teaching_text: Adult or student crossing guards hold legal authority to halt traffic until every child reaches the sidewalk.

sec08-card-r13.question_text: What hazard should you scan for at a Bicycle warning sign?
sec08-card-r13.teaching_text: Multi-use trails often intersect roadways midblock where brisk riders appear quickly from tree cover.

sec08-card-r14.question_text: What road geometry does a Reverse Turn sign warn of?
sec08-card-r14.teaching_text: Back-to-back sharp corners demand low entry speed so weight transfer on the second bend stays controlled.

sec08-card-r15.question_text: What sequence of bends does a Reverse Curve warning announce?
sec08-card-r15.teaching_text: Matching arrow direction tells you whether the roadway sweeps left-then-right or right-then-left ahead.

sec08-card-r16.question_text: What does a Curve warning identify, and what speed adjustment does it call for?
sec08-card-r16.teaching_text: Slowing BEFORE turning the wheel keeps tires planted instead of drifting wide across the center line.

sec08-card-r17.question_text: What information does a small yellow advisory-speed plaque add beneath a diamond warning sign?
sec08-card-r17.teaching_text: Engineers calculate curve banking and sightlines to post the safest pace for average dry conditions.

sec08-card-r18.question_text: What road alignment lies ahead when you see a Winding Road warning sign?
sec08-card-r18.teaching_text: Continuous twisting stretches limit passing sightlines and demand steady moderate speed throughout.

sec08-card-r19.question_text: What intersection layout and hazard does a Crossroad warning sign announce?
sec08-card-r19.teaching_text: Rural cross-street drivers hidden behind cornfields or embankments may enter or cross your highway abruptly.

sec08-card-r20.question_text: What happens to your lane ahead at a T-intersection warning, and what must you use before turning?
sec08-card-r20.teaching_text: Missing a T-intersection warning at night risks overrunning the dead end into a ditch or embankment.

sec08-card-r21.question_text: What junction and traffic risk are shown by a Sideroad warning with a stem on the right?
sec08-card-r21.teaching_text: Vehicles pulling out from a blind side road may accelerate slowly into your right lane.

sec08-card-r22.question_text: How must you adjust speed and priority when approaching a roundabout warning sign?
sec08-card-r22.teaching_text: Traffic already counter-clockwise inside the circle holds right-of-way over every entering approach.

sec08-card-r23.question_text: How should mainline drivers respond at a warning for traffic merging from the right?
sec08-card-r23.teaching_text: Moving left a lane or easing throttle opens a cooperative gap so ramp traffic blends smoothly.

sec08-card-r24.question_text: What two obligations does a Railroad Crossing warning sign place on drivers?
sec08-card-r24.teaching_text: Approaching every track ready to brake prevents panic skids if bells or headlights appear.

sec08-card-r25.question_text: What does a No Train Horn plaque below a railroad warning tell drivers?
sec08-card-r25.teaching_text: Engineers do not sound routine approach whistles in quiet zones, making visual track checks doubly vital.

sec08-card-r26.question_text: What two navigation details are displayed on green-and-white guide signs?
sec08-card-r26.teaching_text: Reading green mileage and exit boards early prevents abrupt multi-lane dives across freeway gores.

sec08-card-r27.question_text: How do interchange guide diagrams help drivers on complex highways?
sec08-card-r27.teaching_text: Mapped lane arrows show left-side exits or split ramps well before concrete barriers divide lanes.

sec08-card-r28.question_text: Which vehicles on Nebraska public roads must display a slow-moving-vehicle emblem?
sec08-card-r28.teaching_text: Spotting the fluorescent orange triangle on farm machinery warns you immediately of a huge speed gap.

sec08-card-r29.question_text: Which motorist facilities do blue-and-white service signs point toward?
sec08-card-r29.teaching_text: Blue exit plaques let tired or low-fuel drivers plan safe off-highway stops without guesswork.

sec08-card-r30.question_text: Where on the roadway is a yellow no-passing pennant mounted?
sec08-card-r30.teaching_text: Placing the yellow pennant on the left shoulder puts it directly in the sightline of drivers peeking out to pass.

sec08-card-r31.question_text: How far apart sit Nebraska highway reference posts, and how do they help in emergencies?
sec08-card-r31.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers your exact milepost number gets tow trucks, troopers, or ambulances to rural stretches fast.

sec08-card-r32.question_text: Who may legally park in spaces marked with accessible parking signs?
sec08-card-r32.teaching_text: Keeping accessible stalls open ensures drivers and riders with mobility permits have ramp and aisle room.

sec08-card-r33.question_text: How can route markers be mounted to guide drivers through turns or straight stretches?
sec08-card-r33.teaching_text: Supplemental arrow plaques underneath highway shields warn you before a numbered route turns at an intersection.

sec08-card-r34.question_text: What real-time updates do dynamic message signs display to motorists?
sec08-card-r34.teaching_text: Overhead digital boards warn of blizzards, crashes, or lane closures miles before traffic backs up.

sec08-card-r35.question_text: Where are most permanent dynamic message signs installed, and where are portable units used?
sec08-card-r35.teaching_text: Trailer-mounted LED boards bring live lane and detour warnings straight to temporary work sites or festivals.

sec08-card-r36.question_text: What special zone is identified by black lettering or symbols on an orange warning sign?
sec08-card-r36.teaching_text: Orange belongs exclusively to temporary traffic control where workers and equipment operate near moving lanes.

sec08-card-r37.question_text: Where in relation to a construction site do work-zone signs help drivers?
sec08-card-r37.teaching_text: Advance panels prepare your speed drop early while interior signs steer you safely past open trenches.

sec08-card-r38.question_text: What mindset is required as soon as black-on-orange signs announce a work zone ahead?
sec08-card-r38.teaching_text: Sudden brake lights, narrowed shoulders, and workers feet from your mirror leave zero room for distraction.

sec08-card-r39.question_text: Which two driving adjustments do advance work-zone warnings commonly call for?
sec08-card-r39.teaching_text: Matching lower construction limits and open lanes early keeps work-zone traffic flowing without panic stops.

sec08-card-r40.question_text: Why should you act on advance work-zone directions early instead of waiting until the cones?
sec08-card-r40.teaching_text: Racing to the closed taper nose bottlenecks the entire queue and triggers side-swipe collisions.

sec08-card-r41.question_text: What two messages do large flashing or sequential arrow panels convey in work zones?
sec08-card-r41.teaching_text: Towering lighted chevrons cut through glare and dust miles ahead so drivers vacate closed lanes smoothly.

sec08-card-r42.question_text: What shape are most work-zone warning signs, and what do they alert you to?
sec08-card-r42.teaching_text: Pairing warning diamond shapes with bright orange flags uneven pavement, loose gravel, or shifted lines.

sec08-card-r43.question_text: How must you prepare when you spot an orange Flagger warning sign?
sec08-card-r43.teaching_text: One-lane construction alternating traffic in turns often queues cars just around the next bend.

sec08-card-r44.question_text: What visibility gear and handheld tool does the Nebraska handbook describe a work-zone flagger using?
sec08-card-r44.teaching_text: High-visibility vests and octagonal STOP or SLOW paddles make human commands unmistakable in dusty work zones.

sec08-card-r45.question_text: Once a work-zone flagger stops your vehicle, when are you allowed to drive forward?
sec08-card-r45.teaching_text: Pulling out early because the lane looks empty can put you head-on into oncoming single-lane traffic.

sec08-card-r46.question_text: Which four channelizing devices commonly guide vehicles along temporary paths through a work zone?
sec08-card-r46.teaching_text: Following orange channelizers cleanly keeps tires out of fresh concrete, drop-offs, and crew work areas.

sec11-card-f01.question_text: How far back must you trail responding fire apparatus, and what block restriction applies where it stops?
sec11-card-f01.teaching_text: Crowding fire engines or parking on the emergency block tangles hose lines and traps arriving ladder trucks.

sec11-card-f02.question_text: When must drivers yield to a funeral-procession escort vehicle?
sec11-card-f02.teaching_text: Cutting through an escorted procession splits grieving drivers apart and triggers sudden chain-reaction braking.

sec11-card-f03.question_text: What three actions are required when pedestrians occupy a crosswalk ahead?
sec11-card-f03.teaching_text: Easing off the accelerator early prevents panic braking if a walker hesitates, drops something, or reverses direction.

sec11-card-f04.question_text: How much lateral clearance does the Nebraska manual call for when passing a pedestrian on a roadway?
sec11-card-f04.teaching_text: Side mirrors and highway wind blast extend past your fender, easily clipping a walker who stumbles near the edge.

sec11-card-f05.question_text: What must you do when encountering a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
sec11-card-f05.teaching_text: Revving past right behind a visually impaired walker masks traffic sound cues they rely on to finish crossing.

sec11-card-f06.question_text: Whose instructions govern your movement whenever a police officer is actively directing traffic?
sec11-card-f06.teaching_text: Officers managing crash scenes, power outages, or stadium crowds override normal light cycles to prevent gridlock.

sec11-card-f07.question_text: What pace does Nebraska's basic speed rule require at all times?
sec11-card-f07.teaching_text: Posted signs assume dry daylight pavement, so fog, ice, glare, or heavy congestion legally demand a slower pace.

sec11-card-f08.question_text: What is Nebraska's default maximum speed in an unposted business district?
sec11-card-f08.teaching_text: Downtown storefronts mix angled parking, delivery vans, and frequent mid-block foot traffic into tight sightlines.

sec11-card-f09.question_text: What maximum speed applies in an unposted Nebraska residential district?
sec11-card-f09.teaching_text: Test questions frequently pair business twenty against residential twenty-five, where driveways, pets, and kids appear suddenly.

sec11-card-f10.question_text: What unposted speed limit governs gravel or other nondustless roads in Nebraska?
sec11-card-f10.teaching_text: Loose aggregate cuts tire grip dramatically and kicks up dust clouds that hide oncoming pickups and farm equipment.

sec11-card-f11.question_text: What is the unposted maximum speed on a paved or dustless road outside the state highway system?
sec11-card-f11.teaching_text: County paved routes still feature farm entrances, narrow shoulders, and hills that warrant lower speed than state highways.

sec11-card-f12.question_text: What unposted speed cap applies to a four-lane divided highway outside the state highway system?
sec11-card-f12.teaching_text: Separating opposing lanes with a median reduces head-on risk, raising the default cap above two-lane county pavement.

sec11-card-f13.question_text: What unposted maximum applies on a standard state highway that is not an expressway, super-two, or freeway?
sec11-card-f13.teaching_text: Two-lane state routes carry brisk regional traffic while still intersecting county cross-roads and rural driveways at grade.

sec11-card-f14.question_text: What unposted limit covers state expressways, super-two highways, and freeways, and how do rural interstates differ?
sec11-card-f14.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing seventy on super-two and expressway corridors versus the higher rural-interstate number.

sec11-card-f15.question_text: What unposted speed limit does the Nebraska manual list for rural interstate highways?
sec11-card-f15.teaching_text: Even on wide rural interstates, urban segments and construction zones post lower signs that immediately override the default.

sec11-card-f16.question_text: Why must you keep scanning roadside speed signs instead of relying on default road-type rules?
sec11-card-f16.teaching_text: Town approaches, curves, and school corridors drop limits sharply without changing the look of the pavement underneath.

sec11-card-f17.question_text: Why should you generally match pace with the main legal traffic stream?
sec11-card-f17.teaching_text: Large speed gaps between cars multiply lane changes and rear-end conflicts while smoother pacing gives room to adjust.

sec11-card-f18.question_text: When may a vehicle moving slower than normal traffic leave the right available lane?
sec11-card-f18.teaching_text: Staying right until you need to overtake or set up a left turn keeps faster lanes predictable and unclogged.

sec11-card-f19.question_text: When is driving slower than normal traffic flow justified despite the rule against obstructing traffic?
sec11-card-f19.teaching_text: Crawling needlessly invites rear-end crashes, yet severe weather, active emergencies, or minimum-speed statutes always take priority.

sec11-card-f20.question_text: What four habits keep traffic moving safely through a highway work zone?
sec11-card-f20.teaching_text: Concrete barriers and cones shrink shoulder escape routes, leaving zero margin for distracted drifting or erratic speed swings.

sec11-card-f21.question_text: How should you manage lane position and braking around active work-zone crews and machinery?
sec11-card-f21.teaching_text: Slamming brakes unexpectedly inside narrow cone chutes triggers chain-reaction rear-enders right beside exposed road workers.

sec11-card-f22.question_text: What three behaviors does the handbook require inside every school zone?
sec11-card-f22.teaching_text: Young students dart unpredictably between buses and parked parent cars without judging oncoming vehicle speed.

sec11-card-f23.question_text: In which two settings does the Nebraska manual double speeding fines?
sec11-card-f23.teaching_text: Notice the key exam distinction that work zones require workers present to double fines while school zones double directly.

sec11-card-r01.question_text: What base fines apply when going one to five miles an hour above a posted limit normally versus in work or school zones?
sec11-card-r01.teaching_text: Even creeping a handful of miles per hour above the sign triggers court costs on top of the statutory fine.

sec11-card-r02.question_text: What fine amounts plus court costs apply when going six to ten miles an hour above the speed limit?
sec11-card-r02.teaching_text: Every step up Nebraska's speeding schedule doubles cleanly inside active worker corridors and posted school zones.

sec11-card-r03.question_text: What printed fines plus court costs apply for eleven through fifteen miles per hour above the limit?
sec11-card-r03.teaching_text: Crossing past ten over triples the normal fine tier immediately, reflecting sharply rising stopping-distance danger.

sec11-card-r04.question_text: What fine amounts plus court costs apply when speeding sixteen through twenty miles per hour over?
sec11-card-r04.teaching_text: Carrying nearly twenty extra miles per hour through cones or crosswalks turns minor miscalculations into severe impacts.

sec11-card-r05.question_text: What fines plus court costs apply when going twenty-one to thirty-five miles an hour above a speed limit?
sec11-card-r05.teaching_text: High-bracket speeding adds heavy license-point hits alongside steep court-cost and fine totals.

sec11-card-r06.question_text: What printed fines plus court costs apply when driving more than thirty-five miles per hour over the limit?
sec11-card-r06.teaching_text: Extreme speed strips away steering recovery margin and tops out the handbook's civil fine chart.

sec11-card-r07.question_text: What condition triggers the doubled-fine column in a work zone, and which other zone shares that column?
sec11-card-r07.teaching_text: Exam distractors often claim empty overnight cone zones always double fines, so watch for worker presence.

sec11-card-r08.question_text: Is overtaking ever permitted inside a marked no-passing zone?
sec11-card-r08.teaching_text: Solid yellow lines and pennant signs mark hidden dips and curves where oncoming traffic appears with zero warning.

sec11-card-r09.question_text: May you go faster than the posted speed limit briefly in order to overtake another vehicle?
sec11-card-r09.teaching_text: Many drivers wrongly believe the law grants a temporary speed cushion while overtaking, making this a classic test trap.

sec11-card-r10.question_text: When is passing a school bus strictly prohibited?
sec11-card-r10.teaching_text: Children cross in front of and behind the bus bumper where passing motorists cannot spot them until impact.

sec11-card-r11.question_text: Within what distance of an intersection or railroad crossing is passing prohibited?
sec11-card-r11.teaching_text: Cross-street turns and approaching trains create sudden side-and-front conflicts right where an overtaking car occupies the opposing lane.

sec11-card-r12.question_text: On which three roadway features is passing prohibited whenever sight distance is blocked?
sec11-card-r12.teaching_text: Two cars closing head-on at highway speed cover hundreds of feet per second inside blind crests and narrow bridge decks.

sec11-card-r13.question_text: What should you weigh and how far back should you stay before starting a pass?
sec11-card-r13.teaching_text: Tailgating right on a bumper blinds your view down the oncoming lane and robs room to build speed cleanly.

sec11-card-r14.question_text: What two checks come right before steering into the passing lane?
sec11-card-r14.teaching_text: Another car behind you may already be overtaking in the left lane, turning an unchecked pull-out into a sideswipe.

sec11-card-r15.question_text: How do you execute the move into the passing lane while staying within legal speed rules?
sec11-card-r15.teaching_text: If overtaking cleanly would require breaking the posted limit, the vehicle ahead is already fast enough to follow.

sec11-card-r16.question_text: What mirror cue tells you it is safe to signal right, return to lane, and resume normal speed?
sec11-card-r16.teaching_text: Pulling right before seeing the full front end in your center mirror cuts dangerously close across their bumper.

sec14-card-f01.question_text: How do a motorcycle's legal rights and privileges on Nebraska roads compare with other vehicles?
sec14-card-f01.teaching_text: Two wheels carry the exact same legal standing at intersections and lanes as any sedan or pickup.

sec14-card-f02.question_text: How much lane width must you give a motorcycle rather than squeezing beside it?
sec14-card-f02.teaching_text: Riders need the entire lane width to shift around wind gusts, oil streaks, and potholes without clipping your mirror.

sec14-card-f03.question_text: What two visual challenges does a motorcycle's narrow profile create for other drivers?
sec14-card-f03.teaching_text: A single headlight makes an approaching bike look farther away and slower than it really is, causing left-turn cutoffs.

sec14-card-f04.question_text: Why must you signal well before merging or changing lanes near motorcycle traffic?
sec14-card-f04.teaching_text: Motorcyclists rely on early blinkers to adjust lane position smoothly without panic-braking on two narrow tires.

sec14-card-f05.question_text: Where and when must you check specifically for motorcycles in mirrors and blind areas?
sec14-card-f05.teaching_text: Bikes slip completely behind roof pillars and side mirrors right before lane shifts and intersection turns.

sec14-card-f06.question_text: Why shouldn't you pull out just because an approaching motorcycle's turn signal is blinking?
sec14-card-f06.teaching_text: Many motorcycle turn indicators do not self-cancel, so pulling out on a leftover blink puts you straight into the rider.

sec14-card-f07.question_text: Which road-surface conditions commonly force motorcyclists to adjust speed or lane position suddenly?
sec14-card-f07.teaching_text: Minor seams, slick patches, grooved pavement, or gravel that cars barely feel can dump a two-wheeled bike instantly.

sec14-card-f08.question_text: What following gap does the Nebraska handbook recommend behind a motorcycle, and why?
sec14-card-f08.teaching_text: Extra time cushion protects a rider who has to swerve around debris or brake hard without steel bumpers around them.

sec14-card-f09.question_text: On dry pavement, how does a motorcycle's stopping capability compare with a passenger car's?
sec14-card-f09.teaching_text: Light weight gives dry-road bikes shorter stopping distances, turning a tailgating car into an instant rear-end threat.

sec14-card-f10.question_text: What rights and responsibilities apply to bicyclists riding on Nebraska roadways?
sec14-card-f10.teaching_text: Bikes on the street operate under the same traffic laws, signals, and yielding duties as motor vehicles.

sec14-card-f11.question_text: Where do bicyclists generally position themselves along a roadway?
sec14-card-f11.teaching_text: Staying as far right as practical or using a paved shoulder separates slower pedaling pace from faster cars.

sec14-card-f12.question_text: When is a bicyclist allowed to occupy the full travel lane instead of hugging the right edge?
sec14-card-f12.teaching_text: Claiming a narrow lane prevents drivers from attempting dangerous close-quarters squeezes inside the same lane.

sec14-card-f13.question_text: Why might a bicyclist move out of the right lane approaching an intersection?
sec14-card-f13.teaching_text: Leaving a right-turn-only curb lane lets a rider turn left or continue straight without conflicting with turning cars.

sec14-card-f14.question_text: Which additional lane may bicyclists ride in on an urban one-way street?
sec14-card-f14.teaching_text: Riding left on city one-way streets positions cyclists cleanly for upcoming left turns and avoids right-curb bus stops.

sec14-card-f15.question_text: Why should you expect a cyclist ahead to shift laterally inside their lane?
sec14-card-f15.teaching_text: Broken glass, storm grates, and potholes along the gutter can trap thin bicycle wheels and flip the rider.

sec14-card-f16.question_text: How should you position your vehicle relative to same-direction bike traffic before turning right?
sec14-card-f16.teaching_text: Overtaking a rider and whipping right across their front wheel causes the classic right-hook crash.

sec14-card-f17.question_text: How must a left-turning driver treat an oncoming bicyclist?
sec14-card-f17.teaching_text: Underestimating a pedaling rider's speed leads drivers to turn left straight across the cyclist's right-of-way.

sec14-card-f18.question_text: What horn habit and parked-car habit protect bicyclists nearby?
sec14-card-f18.teaching_text: A sudden horn blast startles riders off balance, while swinging an unchecked car door creates an unavoidable wall.

sec14-card-f19.question_text: What minimum lateral clearance must you keep when overtaking a bicycle moving in the same direction?
sec14-card-f19.teaching_text: Holding at least three full feet until completely past keeps mirror wash and wind buffeting from knocking riders down.

sec14-card-f20.question_text: What must you do when oncoming traffic or road width prevents a safe three-foot pass around a bicycle?
sec14-card-f20.teaching_text: Easing off the gas for a few seconds beats risking a cyclist's life on a tight blind squeeze.
sec14-card-f20.must_match_memory_hook: Under three feet, slow and wait

visual_sync.text_span: Under three feet, slow and wait

sec14-card-f21.question_text: How can children on bicycles surprise drivers along residential blocks?
sec14-card-f21.teaching_text: Young riders shoot out of driveways, alleys, and curbs midblock focused on fun rather than approaching cars.

sec14-card-f22.question_text: What do swerving or riding wrong-way against traffic signal about a cyclist, and how should you respond?
sec14-card-f22.teaching_text: An inexperienced rider facing traffic may make unpredictable moves, calling for slower speed and wider room.

sec14-card-f23.question_text: Why must you look both ways along sidewalks and parallel trails before making a turn?
sec14-card-f23.teaching_text: Trail and sidewalk cyclists close ground much faster than walkers from either side of your turning path.

sec14-card-f24.question_text: Which right-of-way rules govern bicycles and motor vehicles at intersections and roundabouts?
sec14-card-f24.teaching_text: Treating a circulating or crossing bicycle just like another car keeps intersection and roundabout yielding consistent.

sec14-card-f25.question_text: Where must you anticipate pedestrians stepping out, especially away from corners?
sec14-card-f25.teaching_text: Neighborhood streets around homes, parks, and schools generate constant midblock crossings between parked cars.

sec14-card-f26.question_text: What pedestrian signal mistakes must drivers stay alert for at intersections?
sec14-card-f26.teaching_text: A distracted walker or slow-moving senior caught mid-crossing still requires you to hold back rather than hit them.

sec14-card-f27.question_text: When turning across crosswalks, which permitted signal maneuver demands extra pedestrian caution?
sec14-card-f27.teaching_text: Drivers craning left for oncoming car gaps on red often overlook pedestrians stepping off the right curb.

sec14-card-f28.question_text: Where must your front bumper stop at a stop sign or red light relative to marked or unmarked crosswalks?
sec14-card-f28.teaching_text: Even unpainted corner-to-corner extensions form legal crosswalks that your hood must never block.

sec14-card-f29.question_text: Why is passing a vehicle stopped for a pedestrian strictly forbidden?
sec14-card-f29.teaching_text: Whip-passing a stopped car in the adjacent lane blinds you to the walker stepping right past its front fender.

sec14-card-f30.question_text: What must you do for a blind or visually impaired pedestrian using a white cane or service dog?
sec14-card-f30.teaching_text: Rolling past early startles service dogs and disorients someone navigating by sound rather than sight.

sec14-card-r01.question_text: Under what visibility condition and caution standard may you pass snow-removal equipment?
sec14-card-r01.teaching_text: Swirling snow plumes off wide plow blades can hide oncoming cars and extended wing blades completely.

sec14-card-r02.question_text: What three hazards do plowed snow ridges, plow skids, and flying material create around snow-removal equipment?
sec14-card-r02.teaching_text: Heavy wet windrows grab tires, side loads can kick the plow sideways, and thrown salt or ice chips windshields.

sec14-card-r03.question_text: Except while passing, what minimum distance must you hold behind working snow-removal or maintenance vehicles?
sec14-card-r03.teaching_text: One hundred feet keeps your windshield out of thrown sand and gives room if the heavy plow stops or backs.

sec14-card-r04.question_text: Which warning lights does a school bus driver activate when preparing to load or unload children?
sec14-card-r04.teaching_text: Flashing amber lamps work like a yellow traffic signal telling nearby drivers a full red-light stop is seconds away.

sec14-card-r05.question_text: To what speed must you slow when meeting or overtaking a school bus flashing amber pre-stop warnings?
sec14-card-r05.teaching_text: Nebraska specifically sets twenty-five miles per hour on amber bus warnings so you never try to race the stop arm.

sec14-card-r06.question_text: What action switches a school bus from flashing amber lights to flashing red lamps and an extended stop arm?
sec14-card-r06.teaching_text: The instant the bus door swings open, children step toward pavement and red stop-arm protection locks in.

sec14-card-r07.question_text: When stopped for an active school-bus red-light and stop-arm warning, how long must you remain stopped?
sec14-card-r07.teaching_text: Moving before both the stop arm retracts and the red lamps shut off risks striking late-crossing students.

sec14-card-r08.question_text: Which drivers are exempt from stopping for an active school bus warning?
sec14-card-r08.teaching_text: Only oncoming traffic separated by a physical median is excused; same-side lanes and undivided roads must always stop.

sec14-card-r09.question_text: Outside the divided-median exception, what must every driver approaching or overtaking a red-light, extended-arm school bus do?
sec14-card-r09.teaching_text: On any undivided two-lane or multi-lane road, traffic from both ahead and behind must come to a full stop.

sec14-card-r10.question_text: On dry clear pavement at fifty-five, how many feet at minimum does a loaded truck need to stop?
sec14-card-r10.teaching_text: Three hundred forty feet exceeds an entire football field even with good tires and adjusted air brakes.

sec14-card-r11.question_text: Why must you never dart abruptly in front of a large vehicle or merge ahead of one right before turning off?
sec14-card-r11.teaching_text: Swooping in and braking to turn strips away a loaded rig's three-hundred-forty-foot stopping cushion.

sec14-card-r12.question_text: Near steep uphill climbs or truck weigh stations, why should you move out of the right lane?
sec14-card-r12.teaching_text: Loaded rigs re-entering off scale ramps or climbing steep hills move far slower than main-lane traffic.

sec14-card-r13.question_text: How should you position yourself around trucks displaying explosives, poison, or flammable cargo markings?
sec14-card-r13.teaching_text: Extra buffer space around placarded hazmat tankers keeps you away from fire, toxic spills, or frequent rail stops.

sec14-card-r14.question_text: Why must you avoid sudden stops directly ahead of a large truck or bus?
sec14-card-r14.teaching_text: Air-brake pressure build time and massive cargo weight prevent immediate deceleration when a car slams brakes ahead.

sec14-card-r15.question_text: What purpose does an added right-hand lane marked Slow Traffic Keep Right serve on uphill grades?
sec14-card-r15.teaching_text: Moving heavy climbers right lets normal highway traffic pass smoothly without crossing into oncoming lanes.

sec14-card-r16.question_text: Why do roundabouts include a raised inner truck apron around the central island?
sec14-card-r16.teaching_text: Long trailers off-track inward around tight circles, so stay back instead of riding beside a semi in a roundabout.

sec14-card-r17.question_text: What two dangerous conditions around a truck or bus define a No-Zone?
sec14-card-r17.teaching_text: A No-Zone either hides your car from cab mirrors or crowds the rig's stopping and turning room.

sec14-card-r18.question_text: When a large truck or bus starts reversing or prepares to reverse, what rear movement is banned?
sec14-card-r18.teaching_text: A long box trailer blocks the driver's entire rear view while swinging wide across loading bays or lanes.

sec14-card-r19.question_text: When passing a truck or bus, what mirror cue tells you it is safe to merge back in front?
sec14-card-r19.teaching_text: Waiting until both headlights and the entire grille appear inside your rearview mirror preserves safe front buffer.

sec14-card-r20.question_text: Why shouldn't you tailgate a truck, and what visual cue confirms the driver can spot you behind?
sec14-card-r20.teaching_text: If you cannot see the truck's side mirrors past its trailer box, the driver has zero idea you are back there.

sec14-card-r21.question_text: Why should you avoid lingering alongside a truck or bus?
sec14-card-r21.teaching_text: Long side blind spots stretch down both flanks of a trailer where a lane change or tire blowout hits hardest.

sec14-card-r22.question_text: How must you handle a wide-turning truck or bus that swings out before cornering?
sec14-card-r22.teaching_text: Squeezing into the curb gap beside a right-turning trailer crushes your car as the rear axles track tight inside.

sec15-card-f01.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a stop immediately after a crash?
sec15-card-f01.teaching_text: Driving off turns an ordinary collision into a hit-and-run offense before anyone even checks for injuries.

sec15-card-f02.question_text: When must you assist injured people after a collision?
sec15-card-f02.teaching_text: Promptly helping or calling medical responders when aid is needed or requested can prevent shock or worsening trauma.

sec15-card-f03.question_text: Who must you notify after a crash that requires emergency assistance?
sec15-card-f03.teaching_text: Getting police, fire, and paramedics rolling immediately stabilizes injuries and protects blocked lanes.

sec15-card-f04.question_text: Which warning devices should you set out after a crash, and which directions of traffic need warning?
sec15-card-f04.teaching_text: Secondary pileups happen fast when approaching drivers crest hills or round bends from any direction unaware.

sec15-card-f05.question_text: Which three personal contact details must you exchange with the other drivers involved in a crash?
sec15-card-f05.teaching_text: Complete personal contact details let investigators and insurers follow up accurately after everyone clears the scene.

sec15-card-f06.question_text: Which exterior vehicle identifier belongs in the required driver-to-driver crash exchange?
sec15-card-f06.teaching_text: Recording the exact plate ties the specific registered vehicle to official crash and claim records.

sec15-card-f07.question_text: Which driver credential number must you share when exchanging crash details with other drivers?
sec15-card-f07.teaching_text: Verifying actual driver's license numbers confirms identity beyond a handwritten name or phone number.

sec15-card-f08.question_text: What financial-responsibility details must you provide during a post-crash exchange?
sec15-card-f08.teaching_text: Sharing carrier and policy details lets repair and medical claims start without tracking people down later.

sec15-card-f09.question_text: Which three descriptive facts about the involved vehicle must be exchanged after a crash?
sec15-card-f09.teaching_text: Documenting make, model, and year prevents mix-ups when multiple vehicles or insurers review the report.

sec15-card-f10.question_text: Who must you contact if your vehicle strikes an unattended parked car?
sec15-card-f10.teaching_text: Notifying police creates an official timestamped record proving you handled the unattended collision lawfully.

sec15-card-f11.question_text: Besides contacting authorities, what must you leave behind after striking an unattended vehicle?
sec15-card-f11.teaching_text: Placing complete contact, vehicle, and insurance info visibly on the car lets the returning owner reach you.

sec15-card-f12.question_text: What details should you gather from bystanders who saw the crash happen?
sec15-card-f12.teaching_text: Independent witnesses disappear within minutes unless you write down their names and addresses right away.

sec15-card-f13.question_text: How long must you remain at a crash scene when authorities respond?
sec15-card-f13.teaching_text: Driving off before an investigating officer clears you risks leaving-the-scene citations and incomplete statements.

sec15-card-f14.question_text: When police do not investigate, what deadline and thresholds require filing a Driver's Motor Vehicle Crash Report with NDOT?
sec15-card-f14.teaching_text: Nebraska tests ten days and fifteen hundred dollars to any one person's property whenever injury, death, or uninvestigated damage occurs.

sec15-card-r01.question_text: How does a law-enforcement officer's crash investigation change the handbook's separate driver-report requirement?
sec15-card-r01.teaching_text: When an officer investigates on scene, that official report satisfies NDOT instead of requiring a separate driver filing.

sec15-card-r02.question_text: Which specific NDOT form number and revision date do the handbook's crash-reporting instructions name?
sec15-card-r02.teaching_text: Detail questions from Nebraska's crash chapter can reference Form forty-one directly from the reporting box.

sec15-card-r03.question_text: Which agencies do the printed instructions list as sources where drivers can obtain the crash-report form?
sec15-card-r03.teaching_text: Both Nebraska State Patrol offices and local police or sheriff departments keep crash forms accessible.

sec15-card-r04.question_text: What legal consequence can follow failing to submit a legally required Nebraska crash report?
sec15-card-r04.teaching_text: Ignoring the ten-day reporting mandate is unlawful and can strip away your driver's license or privilege.

sec02-card-f01.question_text: How many documents proving your principal address must accompany a Nebraska application?
sec02-card-f01.teaching_text: Showing up at the licensing counter with only a single piece of mail stops your application before vision screening even starts.

sec02-card-f02.question_text: How must an applicant satisfy the Social Security requirement or establish an exemption?
sec02-card-f02.teaching_text: Without a verifiable Social Security number, only a valid foreign passport holding an unexpired I-ninety-four or A-variant arrival record proves exemption.

sec02-card-f03.question_text: What status must every new Nebraska applicant establish when applying?
sec02-card-f03.teaching_text: Every first-time state credential requires verified proof of either United States citizenship or current lawful immigration presence in the country.

sec02-card-f04.question_text: Once U.S. citizenship proof has been presented, is it needed again at future licensing visits?
sec02-card-f04.teaching_text: Because United States citizenship stays recorded on your state profile, future renewals or replacements skip repeating birth-certificate or passport checks.

sec02-card-f05.question_text: How often must a noncitizen applicant bring lawful-status proof to the licensing office?
sec02-card-f05.teaching_text: Unlike permanent citizenship records, authorized stay dates can change, so licensing staff re-verify immigration status during every office transaction.

sec02-card-f06.question_text: What authentication features must required application documents carry?
sec02-card-f06.teaching_text: Bringing an uncertified printout without a raised seal or issuing stamp guarantees rejection at the document-verification window.

sec02-card-f07.question_text: Are faxed documents or photocopies accepted for a Nebraska licensing application?
sec02-card-f07.teaching_text: Faxes and flat copies hide raised security seals and tamper marks, so staff only accept original or certified source paperwork.

sec02-card-f08.question_text: What can happen if your application paperwork needs deeper document review?
sec02-card-f08.teaching_text: Complex status or name records sometimes cannot clear verification on the spot, requiring extra paperwork and a follow-up appointment.

sec02-card-f09.question_text: Can a document stamped or marked as unsuitable for identification proof establish your identity?
sec02-card-f09.teaching_text: Check the fine print on every card before leaving home because anything labeled not valid for identification fails identity verification.

sec02-card-f10.question_text: What may the Nebraska DMV do with documents you submit alongside an application?
sec02-card-f10.teaching_text: Scanning and keeping copies of submitted proofs lets state auditors confirm credential integrity and protect your identity record.

sec02-card-f11.question_text: Which documents link a changed name to your existing permit, license, or ID?
sec02-card-f11.teaching_text: Every name step between your birth record and current card needs certified marriage, divorce, or court proof, or a lawful-status petition.

sec02-card-f12.question_text: Which type of birth certificate is accepted to prove both citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f12.teaching_text: Only a vital-records birth certificate certified by a state government carries the legal authority needed to establish citizenship and identity.

sec02-card-f13.question_text: Does Nebraska accept a hospital-issued birth certificate for licensing?
sec02-card-f13.teaching_text: Souvenir hospital certificates with baby footprints are commemorative keepsakes rather than certified government vital records, so counters reject them.

sec02-card-f14.question_text: Which Puerto Rico birth certificates are rejected for a Nebraska application?
sec02-card-f14.teaching_text: Federal security updates invalidated older territory vital records, so any Puerto Rico birth certificate issued before that cutoff date fails.

sec02-card-f15.question_text: When can a U.S. passport or passport card establish both citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f15.teaching_text: Check the expiration date before heading in because only a currently valid United States passport book or card satisfies verification.

sec02-card-f16.question_text: What companion documents apply when presenting a valid I-ninety-four or A-variant arrival record for status and identity?
sec02-card-f16.teaching_text: Beyond a valid foreign passport unless Canadian or Refugee, student and exchange holders add SEVIS forms while Refugees may need I-seven hundred ninety-seven.

sec02-card-f17.question_text: What extra SEVIS paperwork must student or exchange applicants in F, J, or M categories provide?
sec02-card-f17.teaching_text: Academic and exchange visitors cannot clear electronic status checks without bringing their program I-twenty or DS-two thousand nineteen form.

sec02-card-f18.question_text: In which two cases is a foreign passport unnecessary alongside an arrival-and-departure record?
sec02-card-f18.teaching_text: Test questions frequently target these exact two exceptions where an arrival record stands without a companion foreign passport.

sec02-card-f19.question_text: Can a visa by itself satisfy Nebraska's accepted lawful-status and identity document list?
sec02-card-f19.teaching_text: A visa only allows port-of-entry travel requests rather than proving active authorized stay, so bringing a visa alone fails verification.

sec02-card-f20.question_text: When does a permanent-resident card count as accepted lawful-status and identity proof?
sec02-card-f20.teaching_text: As long as your permanent-resident card has not expired, that single credential establishes both identity and lawful status.

sec02-card-f21.question_text: When is an employment-authorization card accepted for lawful status and identity?
sec02-card-f21.teaching_text: Verify the card expiration date first because an active employment-authorization card satisfies both identity and lawful-presence checks.

sec02-card-f22.question_text: Which Certificate of Naturalization form numbers establish citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f22.teaching_text: Naturalized citizens can present either original Form N-five hundred fifty or replacement Form N-five hundred seventy at the counter.

sec02-card-f23.question_text: Which Certificate of Citizenship form numbers does the handbook accept for citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f23.teaching_text: Keep Certificate of Citizenship numbers N-five hundred sixty and N-four hundred fifty-one distinct from naturalization form numbers on test day.

sec02-card-f24.question_text: Which State Department Consular Report of Birth Abroad forms prove citizenship and identity?
sec02-card-f24.teaching_text: Citizens born overseas prove identity and citizenship using Consular Birth Abroad Form FS-two hundred forty, FS-five hundred forty-five, or DS-one thousand three hundred fifty.

sec02-card-f25.question_text: What two conditions must your principal-address documents satisfy together?
sec02-card-f25.teaching_text: Bringing two statements from the exact same bank or utility fails because each proof must come from a separate issuing source.

sec02-card-f26.question_text: Does a post-office box qualify as your principal residence address?
sec02-card-f26.teaching_text: Licensing records must tie you to a physical Nebraska street residence, so mail addressed only to a post-office box gets turned down.

sec02-card-f27.question_text: How can an applicant younger than twenty-one prove residence without personal bills or statements?
sec02-card-f27.teaching_text: Teens and young adults living at home rarely have utility bills in their own name, so parent or guardian address proofs work.

sec02-card-f28.question_text: How recent must a bank or financial-institution statement be to prove residence?
sec02-card-f28.teaching_text: Check the statement issue date before printing or packing because anything older than ninety days no longer proves current residence.

sec02-card-f29.question_text: What date window and employer details must appear on a pay stub used for residence proof?
sec02-card-f29.teaching_text: A recent pay stub fails address verification if it omits your employer's name and address or dates back past ninety days.

sec02-card-f30.question_text: How recent must a government document be when used under the recent-document residence category?
sec02-card-f30.teaching_text: Like other recent mail items on the residence list, government letters outside specific multi-year cards must fall within ninety days.

sec02-card-f31.question_text: How recent must a magazine issue be if you bring it as residence proof?
sec02-card-f31.teaching_text: A subscription magazine showing your Nebraska street label works as one source as long as it came from the past ninety days.

sec02-card-f32.question_text: What date mark must appear on a mailed envelope, box, or postcard used for address proof?
sec02-card-f32.teaching_text: Without a visible postal postmark or stamped date from the past ninety days, an envelope cannot verify when you lived there.

sec02-card-f33.question_text: What date limit applies to correspondence, receipts, or invoices in the recent-address category?
sec02-card-f33.teaching_text: Every recent-category letter, receipt, or invoice follows the same ninety-day freshness rule to confirm you still live at that address.

sec02-card-f34.question_text: Can a Nebraska vehicle registration serve as one of your residence documents?
sec02-card-f34.teaching_text: An unexpired state vehicle registration tied to your street address counts as one reliable government-issued source toward your two-document requirement.

sec02-card-f35.question_text: Which four types of valid insurance policies or cards are accepted as residence documents?
sec02-card-f35.teaching_text: Active coverage paperwork or cards for life, health, auto, or home policies count as an accepted address source when showing your street.

sec02-card-f36.question_text: Does Nebraska accept a valid property tax statement or receipt as a residence document?
sec02-card-f36.teaching_text: Homeowners who manage monthly bills paperlessly can bring a valid county tax statement or receipt to establish one principal-address source.

sec02-card-f37.question_text: Can a valid license count as one of the documents establishing Nebraska residence?
sec02-card-f37.teaching_text: If you already hold an unexpired license showing your current street address, it satisfies one of the two required residence sources.

sec02-card-f38.question_text: Is a Nebraska voter-registration card accepted to help prove principal residence?
sec02-card-f38.teaching_text: County election voter cards confirm your registered residential precinct and street address, making them an easy address source.
