sec02-card-f39.question_text: What landlord details must appear on a residential lease or rental agreement submitted for address proof?
sec02-card-f39.teaching_text: An incomplete rental printout missing your landlord's name and contact details cannot be verified as a legitimate residential lease.

sec02-card-f40.question_text: Does a mortgage agreement qualify as an accepted principal-address document?
sec02-card-f40.teaching_text: Homebuyers who recently closed on a house can bring their mortgage agreement as one of their two distinct address sources.

sec02-card-f41.question_text: Can you use your Nebraska DMV renewal notice as one principal-address document?
sec02-card-f41.teaching_text: Hanging onto the mailed renewal postcard from the state gives returning drivers a ready-made address document at the office.

sec02-card-f42.question_text: Can a blank check or deposit slip serve as a principal-address document?
sec02-card-f42.teaching_text: Preprinted bank checks or deposit slips bearing your Nebraska street address count as an accepted financial source without waiting on statements.

sec02-card-f43.question_text: If staff ask for Social Security proof, how much of the number must appear on the document?
sec02-card-f43.teaching_text: Tax or payroll printouts that mask the first five digits with asterisks fail verification because every digit must be visible.

sec02-card-f44.question_text: Which numbers and federal immigration documents does the Nebraska DMV verify?
sec02-card-f44.teaching_text: State computers cross-check both Social Security numbers and United States Citizenship and Immigration Services records before clearing any credential.

sec02-card-f45.question_text: Does a Social Security card qualify as accepted Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-f45.teaching_text: Bringing your original unlaminated Social Security card is the most direct way to satisfy number verification if requested.

sec02-card-f46.question_text: Can an employer Form W-two serve as Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-f46.teaching_text: Just make sure your Form W-two displays all nine digits rather than a truncated employee copy before using it at licensing.

sec02-card-f47.question_text: Is Form SSA-one thousand ninety-nine accepted as Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-f47.teaching_text: Annual benefit statements on Form SSA-one thousand ninety-nine work cleanly as Social Security proof when they show the complete number.

sec02-card-f48.question_text: How many documents from the accepted list are needed to prove U.S. citizenship or lawful status and identity?
sec02-card-f48.teaching_text: Unlike principal address which requires two separate sources, one qualifying birth, passport, or immigration record covers status and identity.

sec02-card-f49.question_text: What extra requirement can apply if you bring a city- or county-issued birth certificate?
sec02-card-f49.teaching_text: Because state vital-records certificates are preferred, presenting a city or county birth record may trigger requests for extra identification.

sec02-card-f50.question_text: What additional form may be required alongside a Refugee-stamped arrival-and-departure record?
sec02-card-f50.teaching_text: Even though a Refugee stamp skips the foreign-passport rule, staff may still ask for Form I-seven hundred ninety-seven to verify status.

sec02-card-f51.question_text: Which three immigration forms does the handbook explicitly exclude from this identity and lawful-status pathway?
sec02-card-f51.teaching_text: Expired green-card predecessor I-one hundred fifty-one, visa-waiver I-ninety-four W, and Border Crosser records are all rejected for licensing.

sec02-card-f52.question_text: When is an ADIT temporary permanent-residence stamp accepted for licensing?
sec02-card-f52.teaching_text: Both the ADIT temporary-residence endorsement date and the underlying foreign passport itself must remain unexpired at your visit.

sec02-card-f53.question_text: What must a valid foreign passport show under the temporary-resident endorsement wording used after June twenty-eight, two thousand four?
sec02-card-f53.teaching_text: Modern immigrant visas double as temporary green cards for one year once endorsed with the proper admission stamp inside a valid passport.

sec02-card-f54.question_text: Which two personal details must appear on citizenship or lawful-status documents for a noncommercial application?
sec02-card-f54.teaching_text: Every noncommercial permit, license, or state ID ties directly to your legal identity through both full name and date of birth.

sec02-card-r01.question_text: When can a pay stub serve as Social Security number proof?
sec02-card-r01.teaching_text: A payroll stub displaying both your name and complete unmasked Social Security number can pull double duty during document checks.

sec02-card-r02.question_text: How is a Nebraska credential marked when issued to an applicant with parolee immigration status?
sec02-card-r02.teaching_text: Parolee status authorizes state licensing or identification, though federal rules mark the card unsuitable for federal identification purposes.

sec02-card-r03.question_text: Which identification, verification, and testing rules apply to a parolee applicant?
sec02-card-r03.teaching_text: Holding parolee status changes only the federal card marking, while every standard identity check, verification, and exam still applies.

sec02-card-r04.question_text: Who receives a vision test when applying for a noncommercial permit or operator license?
sec02-card-r04.teaching_text: Even when safety courses or clean provisional records waive written and road exams, nobody skips the counter vision screening.

sec02-card-r05.question_text: Which two aspects of eyesight does the Nebraska DMV vision screening check?
sec02-card-r05.teaching_text: Safe driving depends on reading distant signs straight ahead and spotting cross-traffic hazards entering from the sides.

sec02-card-r06.question_text: If you need corrective lenses to pass the vision standard, when must you wear them?
sec02-card-r06.teaching_text: Passing the eye machine with glasses or contacts adds a mandatory lens restriction that applies on every single trip.

sec02-card-r07.question_text: Who must check the findings if you do not meet the DMV vision standards at the counter?
sec02-card-r07.teaching_text: Failing the counter screening sends you to a licensed eye specialist who can measure vision precisely or prescribe corrective lenses.

sec02-card-r08.question_text: What happens if an applicant cannot meet Nebraska's minimum vision standard even after specialist evaluation?
sec02-card-r08.teaching_text: Minimum eyesight thresholds protect everyone on the road, so applicants unable to reach the baseline standard cannot be licensed.

sec02-card-r09.question_text: How are Nebraska written knowledge tests organized across different license classes?
sec02-card-r09.teaching_text: Motorcycle, passenger-car, and commercial vehicles follow distinct safety rules, so each license class uses its own targeted knowledge screening.

sec02-card-r10.question_text: Which permit and license applicants get their written-test study material from this driver manual?
sec02-card-r10.teaching_text: Studying this single handbook prepares applicants across all four teen or learner permits plus Class O operator knowledge screenings.

sec02-card-r11.question_text: What does the Nebraska drive test evaluate?
sec02-card-r11.teaching_text: Examiners watch how smoothly and safely you handle everyday traffic situations in a vehicle matching your requested license class.

sec02-card-r12.question_text: Can licensing staff require a drive test from any license applicant?
sec02-card-r12.teaching_text: Even when normal rules waive road testing, staff hold discretion to order a drive evaluation whenever safety questions arise.

sec02-card-r13.question_text: Who supplies the vehicle for the drive test, and what kind of vehicle must it be?
sec02-card-r13.teaching_text: Licensing offices never loan out cars, so you must bring a vehicle that represents the exact license class requested.

sec02-card-r14.question_text: What mechanical condition and lighting feature must your drive-test vehicle have?
sec02-card-r14.teaching_text: Burned-out brake lights or unsafe mechanical defects cancel your road appointment right in the parking lot before moving an inch.

sec02-card-r15.question_text: Which drive-test vehicles must provide a clean working passenger seat belt for licensing staff?
sec02-card-r15.teaching_text: Any test car from model year nineteen sixty-four or newer without a clean, latching passenger belt gets rejected immediately.

sec02-card-r16.question_text: Which drive-test vehicles must have clean working seat belts for both licensing staff and the driver?
sec02-card-r16.teaching_text: For vehicles from model year nineteen seventy-three onward, both front seats must have clean functioning belts before testing begins.

sec02-card-r17.question_text: Which dashboard instrument must work properly inside your drive-test vehicle?
sec02-card-r17.teaching_text: Examiners grade speed control across changing zones, so a broken speedometer disqualifies your vehicle from road testing.

sec02-card-r18.question_text: What interior condition is required for a Nebraska drive-test vehicle?
sec02-card-r18.teaching_text: Clearing trash, loose clutter, and grime out of the cabin keeps pedals unobstructed and ensures staff will ride inside.

sec02-card-r19.question_text: Which nine driving skills and maneuvers can the Nebraska drive test assess?
sec02-card-r19.teaching_text: Expect examiners to grade lane position, speed, parking, backing, right of way, traffic controls, turns, starts, and stops.

sec02-card-r20.question_text: What must you prove before reapplying after failing the Class O drive test three times in a row?
sec02-card-r20.teaching_text: Three straight Class O road failures pause retakes until you either complete DMV-approved driver training or hold a learner permit ninety days.

sec02-card-r21.question_text: What form do you receive explaining why a requested licensing document was denied?
sec02-card-r21.teaching_text: Instead of guessing what went wrong, check your Return for Services form for the exact missing document or failed requirement.

sec02-card-r22.question_text: What should you do with a Return for Services form when you come back to the licensing office?
sec02-card-r22.teaching_text: Handing staff your Return for Services sheet lets them pick up right where your previous application stalled.

sec02-card-r23.question_text: If you fail a licensing test, can you retake it later that same day?
sec02-card-r23.teaching_text: Mandatory overnight turnaround prevents rushed guesswork and gives applicants time to review weak spots before trying again.

sec02-card-r24.question_text: Within how many days and where must you present your issuance certificate for payment?
sec02-card-r24.teaching_text: Within ninety days, bring that certificate either to a rural county treasurer or to a Douglas, Lancaster, or Sarpy state office.

sec02-card-r25.question_text: What happens if you miss the ninety-day issuance-certificate payment deadline?
sec02-card-r25.teaching_text: Letting that certificate sit unpaid past ninety days voids it and sends you back to the licensing office to restart issuance.

sec02-card-r26.question_text: How long is the temporary receipt valid after you pay for your credential?
sec02-card-r26.teaching_text: Carry that thirty-day temporary receipt whenever driving until your permanent plastic card arrives in the mail.

sec02-card-r27.question_text: Does the TSA accept Nebraska's temporary paper receipt for boarding flights or entering federal buildings?
sec02-card-r27.teaching_text: Pack an unexpired passport if flying soon after licensing because airport security will not accept your temporary receipt.

sec02-card-r28.question_text: How is your permanent credential delivered, and will the postal service forward it?
sec02-card-r28.teaching_text: Give staff an accurate current mailing address because security mailings bounce back to the state instead of forwarding.

sec02-card-r29.question_text: When and whom should applicants contact if they need disability testing accommodations?
sec02-card-r29.teaching_text: Reaching out to your local licensing office or state DMV ahead of time ensures assistive testing tools are ready when you arrive.

sec02-card-r30.question_text: To whom may an applicant appeal a Nebraska license or State ID refusal?
sec02-card-r30.teaching_text: Applicants who believe a credential denial was mistaken have formal administrative recourse by appealing to the DMV Director.

sec02-card-r31.question_text: Whose safety report can prompt the DMV to recall a licensed driver for reexamination?
sec02-card-r31.teaching_text: Credible safety concerns reported by law enforcement, doctors, or concerned citizens can bring a driver back for fresh testing.

sec02-card-r32.question_text: What details appear in the letter sent to a driver recalled for reexamination?
sec02-card-r32.teaching_text: Read a recall notice closely because it schedules the specific office, date, and time for mandatory written and road evaluations.

sec02-card-r33.question_text: Which two professional statements must a recalled driver supply?
sec02-card-r33.teaching_text: Recalled drivers must bring both a licensed physician's driving medical report and an eye statement from an optometrist or ophthalmologist.

sec02-card-r34.question_text: What happens if a recalled driver skips reexamination, omits required statements, or fails required tests?
sec02-card-r34.teaching_text: Ignoring a recall appointment or failing to clear medical, vision, written, and road checks results in license cancellation.

sec02-card-r35.question_text: When does a Nebraska license expire for a U.S. citizen issued the card below age twenty-one?
sec02-card-r35.teaching_text: Expiring on birthday twenty-one lets young adult citizens transition from vertical underage formatting to a standard adult card.

sec02-card-r36.question_text: When does a Nebraska license expire for a U.S. citizen aged twenty-one or older at issuance?
sec02-card-r36.teaching_text: Adult citizen licenses run on a five-year cycle tied to your birthday in the fifth year after issuance.

sec02-card-r37.question_text: Within how many days must you report a changed name or address through a document change?
sec02-card-r37.teaching_text: Do not mix up the thirty-day new-resident rule with this sixty-day window for updating a name or Nebraska move.

sec02-card-r38.question_text: What happens to your previous license's validity once a replacement license is issued?
sec02-card-r38.teaching_text: Never try using a found old card as backup identification after ordering a replacement because issuance cancels the prior card.

sec02-card-r39.question_text: What does Restriction B mean on a Nebraska license?
sec02-card-r39.teaching_text: Restriction B is the most common code on state licenses, signaling that glasses or contacts are required whenever driving.

sec02-card-r40.question_text: What does Restriction C identify on a Nebraska driver license?
sec02-card-r40.teaching_text: Drivers using hand controls or adaptive steering equipment carry Restriction C to match their vehicle setup.

sec02-card-r41.question_text: How does Restriction E limit your driving privileges?
sec02-card-r41.teaching_text: Holders of Restriction E cannot legally operate manual stick-shift vehicles on public roadways.

sec02-card-r42.question_text: What vehicle equipment does Restriction F require?
sec02-card-r42.teaching_text: Drivers with limited neck mobility or hearing impairments often carry Restriction F to ensure full side-and-rear mirror visibility.

sec02-card-r43.question_text: What time-of-day limit does Restriction G place on a driver?
sec02-card-r43.teaching_text: Drivers whose night vision falls short of nighttime standards can still retain daytime mobility under Restriction G.

sec02-card-r44.question_text: Which roadways are off-limits under Restriction Q?
sec02-card-r44.teaching_text: Restriction Q keeps restricted drivers on local and state highways away from high-speed interstate freeway traffic.

sec02-card-r45.question_text: What signaling equipment does Restriction U require on the vehicle?
sec02-card-r45.teaching_text: When hand-and-arm signals are impractical or unsafe for a driver, Restriction U mandates working automatic turn indicators.

sec02-card-r46.question_text: How does Restriction V limit where a person may drive?
sec02-card-r46.teaching_text: Restriction V tailors driving privileges to familiar local routes or towns specified on the driver's record.

sec02-card-r47.question_text: Which type of road does Restriction W exclude?
sec02-card-r47.teaching_text: Keep Restriction W straight from Restriction Y because W specifically bars driving on one-way streets.

sec02-card-r48.question_text: What driving limit does Restriction X specify?
sec02-card-r48.teaching_text: Even if highway signs allow faster travel, a driver carrying Restriction X must stay at or below their personal speed cap.

sec02-card-r49.question_text: Which roads are allowed under Restriction Y?
sec02-card-r49.teaching_text: Restriction Y keeps drivers off multilane corridors by limiting travel strictly to two-lane roadways carrying traffic in both directions.

sec02-card-r50.question_text: What does Restriction Z stand for on a Nebraska license?
sec02-card-r50.teaching_text: Whenever an individualized safety requirement does not fit standard letter codes, the DMV assigns Restriction Z.

sec02-card-r51.question_text: Outside a renewal window, how can you remove a restriction placed from a medical or vision statement?
sec02-card-r51.teaching_text: Corrective eye surgery or medical recovery mid-cycle requires fresh doctor or vision documentation before licensing staff lift the code.

sec02-card-r52.question_text: How must an applicant qualify for a veteran designation on a Nebraska credential?
sec02-card-r52.teaching_text: Eligibility must be certified through the Nebraska Department of Veterans' Affairs before the veteran indicator prints on your card.

sec02-card-r53.question_text: When is voter registration offered through the Nebraska DMV?
sec02-card-r53.teaching_text: Eligible citizens can register to vote or update voter records right alongside their license or State ID application.

sec02-card-r54.question_text: At what minimum age may a permit, license, or State ID holder declare organ and tissue donation through the DMV?
sec02-card-r54.teaching_text: Starting at sixteen, teens getting a provisional permit or State ID can register their own organ-and-tissue donor choice.

sec02-card-r55.question_text: When does the heart donor symbol appear on a Nebraska credential?
sec02-card-r55.teaching_text: Donor registration is completely voluntary, so the heart emblem prints only when the cardholder affirmatively selects donation.

sec02-card-r56.question_text: For a donor between ages sixteen and eighteen, who may amend the minor's donation decision?
sec02-card-r56.teaching_text: Until a young donor reaches eighteen, available parents or legal adult guardians retain authority to modify that donation choice.

sec02-card-r57.question_text: What happens to your organ-donor status if your driving or identification card expires?
sec02-card-r57.teaching_text: Letting a plastic card expire does not erase your registered wish to donate organs or tissue.

sec02-card-r58.question_text: Can an organ donation declared on a credential, donor card, or registry be revoked after the donor's death?
sec02-card-r58.teaching_text: Legal first-person consent on a permit, license, ID, donor card, or registry cannot be canceled after the donor passes away.

sec02-card-r59.question_text: What role does a deceased registered donor's family play in the donation process?
sec02-card-r59.teaching_text: Transplant teams involve grieving families throughout the process, yet a registered adult donor's own legal consent already authorizes donation.

sec02-card-r60.question_text: When can you get a replacement Nebraska driving or identification document?
sec02-card-r60.teaching_text: Replacing a missing or damaged card promptly keeps valid identification in your wallet and cancels the lost plastic.

sec02-card-r61.question_text: Besides losing a card, which two life changes are reasons to obtain a replacement document?
sec02-card-r61.teaching_text: Changing your legal name or moving to a new residence calls for a replacement credential reflecting accurate current records.

sec10-card-f01.question_text: Where on the roadway should you travel when moving slower than normal traffic for current conditions?
sec10-card-f01.teaching_text: Camping in left or center lanes below prevailing flow forces faster drivers into risky right-side passes and sudden braking.

sec10-card-f02.question_text: Which two maneuvers allow a driver to leave the right lane under Nebraska's keep-right rule?
sec10-card-f02.teaching_text: Moving left early for a driveway, private road, or intersection turn prevents abrupt last-second cuts across faster lanes.

sec10-card-f03.question_text: Who yields when vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at roughly the same moment?
sec10-card-f03.teaching_text: Without signs or signals to assign priority, yielding to your right gives cross-street drivers one predictable tiebreaker.

sec10-card-f04.question_text: Why must you still drive defensively at an intersection when traffic rules give you priority?
sec10-card-f04.teaching_text: Legal entitlement cannot physically halt a speeding or inattentive motorist who blows past a sign or misjudges your approach.

sec10-card-f05.question_text: What should you scan for ahead of reaching an intersection controlled by a yield sign?
sec10-card-f05.teaching_text: Checking cross streets well before the yield line lets you match speed smoothly or brake cleanly if a vehicle appears.

sec10-card-f06.question_text: Which crossing vehicles must you let pass at a yield sign or when turning onto a roadway?
sec10-card-f06.teaching_text: Pulling out into a tight space forces oncoming drivers to slam their brakes or swerve across adjacent lanes.

sec10-card-f07.question_text: Once a safe opening appears at a yield point, how should you enter the roadway?
sec10-card-f07.teaching_text: Accelerating promptly after entering keeps fast-approaching drivers behind you from closing the space before you get up to flow.

sec10-card-f08.question_text: What must you do before entering a crossroad from the stop-sign side of a two-way stop?
sec10-card-f08.teaching_text: Rolling through a two-way stop is especially dangerous because cross-street drivers have no stop sign and carry full speed.

sec10-card-f09.question_text: After halting at a two-way stop, what must you check and wait for before pulling out?
sec10-card-f09.teaching_text: Checking both directions twice catches pedestrians in the crosswalk and fast vehicles hidden briefly behind parked cars or A-pillars.

sec10-card-f10.question_text: What two obligations apply to every driver crossing a four-way stop intersection?
sec10-card-f10.teaching_text: Even when all four approaches have octagon signs, watchful crossing catches impatient drivers who roll their turn early.

sec10-card-f11.question_text: How does Nebraska treat first-to-stop order at a four-way stop, and what resolves uncertainty?
sec10-card-f11.teaching_text: Test writers highlight that going in arrival order is courtesy, while yielding to the driver on your right settles doubts.

sec10-card-f12.question_text: What should you do whenever insisting on intersection priority could cause a collision?
sec10-card-f12.teaching_text: Giving up your turn costs two seconds, whereas forcing your way in front of an aggressive driver causes real wreckage.

sec10-card-f13.question_text: In which direction does all traffic circulate around a roundabout's central island?
sec10-card-f13.teaching_text: Turning right upon entry keeps every vehicle flowing smoothly around the center island without head-on left-turn conflicts.

sec10-card-f14.question_text: Why do roundabouts include a raised truck apron around the central island?
sec10-card-f14.teaching_text: Long tractor-trailers track tighter in the rear than in front, needing mountable pavement so back tires clear the curve.

sec10-card-f15.question_text: Which five road users are prohibited from riding or walking on a roundabout's truck apron?
sec10-card-f15.teaching_text: Cutting across the raised inner border puts smaller vehicles, riders, and walkers directly into the sweep zone of turning trailers.
sec10-card-f15.must_match_memory_hook: Passenger vehicles, bikes, walkers stay off

visual_sync.text_span: Passenger vehicles, bikes, walkers stay off

sec10-card-f16.question_text: How should you manage speed and the approach crosswalk as you near a roundabout?
sec10-card-f16.teaching_text: Slowing to the yellow advisory sign early gives you calm stopping margin for walkers and cyclists crossing ahead of the circle.

sec10-card-f17.question_text: Which vehicles have priority when you reach the yield line of a roundabout?
sec10-card-f17.teaching_text: Drivers already inside the ring never stop for entering cars, so look left and wait for a clean gap.

sec10-card-f18.question_text: What two actions must you take as you reach your roundabout exit?
sec10-card-f18.teaching_text: Blinking right tells waiting drivers they can enter while scanning the splitter crosswalk protects walkers stepping off the curb.

sec10-card-f19.question_text: How do you choose the right lane ahead of entering a two-lane roundabout?
sec10-card-f19.teaching_text: Picking your lane before the yield line avoids last-second weaving inside curved, tight circular lanes.

sec10-card-f20.question_text: In Nebraska's general two-lane roundabout layout, which approach lanes serve left turns versus right turns?
sec10-card-f20.teaching_text: Entering in the wrong shared lane traps you into cutting across an adjacent car's path when your exit arrives.
sec10-card-f20.must_match_memory_hook: Left uses left, right uses right

visual_sync.text_span: Left uses left, right uses right

sec10-card-f21.question_text: What three rules govern going straight through a two-lane roundabout?
sec10-card-f21.teaching_text: Drifting across the broken circle line mid-roundabout sideswipes drivers curving alongside you toward the next exit.
sec10-card-f21.must_match_memory_hook: Obey arrows, yield both, hold lane

visual_sync.text_span: Obey arrows, yield both, hold lane

sec10-card-f22.question_text: Why must you never drive alongside or overtake a large truck at a roundabout?
sec10-card-f22.teaching_text: Long trailers swing wide across lane markings and onto the inner apron, crushing any passenger car tucked beside them.

sec10-card-f23.question_text: How do you clear the way for an emergency vehicle before versus after entering a roundabout?
sec10-card-f23.teaching_text: Clearing past the splitter island before pulling right keeps narrow curved circle lanes open for wide fire trucks and ambulances.

sec10-card-f24.question_text: Where must you avoid stopping when yielding to an approaching emergency vehicle at a roundabout?
sec10-card-f24.teaching_text: Halting inside the curved ring corks the entire intersection so responders cannot steer around your bumper.

sec10-card-r01.question_text: What lane action is required on a multilane controlled-access highway near stopped emergency, roadside, utility, maintenance, or sanitation vehicles flashing lights?
sec10-card-r01.teaching_text: Putting an empty travel lane between high-speed traffic and roadside crews shields workers stepping beside open cab doors.

sec10-card-r02.question_text: What must you do under the Move Over law when heavy traffic or road conditions block changing lanes?
sec10-card-r02.teaching_text: Forcing an unsafe merge causes sideswipes, so shedding speed gives roadside personnel reaction space as you pass.

sec10-card-r03.question_text: Which four vehicle types make up the road-assistance group covered by Nebraska's Move Over rule?
sec10-card-r03.teaching_text: Test questions check whether you recognize amber-lit tow trucks, utility rigs, and motorist-aid vans alongside police cruisers.

sec10-card-r04.question_text: What maximum fine does the Nebraska handbook list for a first Move Over violation?
sec10-card-r04.teaching_text: Even a first failure to give roadside crews space carries an immediate wallet hit plus traffic-record consequences.

sec10-card-r05.question_text: What maximum penalties apply to a second or subsequent Move Over violation in Nebraska?
sec10-card-r05.teaching_text: Escalating repeat violations to potential jail time underscores how seriously state law protects vulnerable highway responders.

sec10-card-r06.question_text: What must you do after a minor freeway or interstate crash when nobody is hurt and vehicles still drive?
sec10-card-r06.teaching_text: Leaving drivable cars parked in live freeway lanes triggers high-speed secondary pileups far worse than the initial tap.

sec10-card-r07.question_text: How may a crashed vehicle be cleared to the shoulder if it cannot be driven under its own power?
sec10-card-r07.teaching_text: Restoring open freeway lanes quickly prevents miles-long backups and secondary collisions around immobilized wreckage.

sec10-card-r08.question_text: Where must you stop and whom must you yield to when pulling out of an alley, driveway, or parking lot?
sec10-card-r08.teaching_text: Creeping straight to the curb blocks walkers, joggers, and strollers before you ever start scanning street traffic.

sec10-card-r09.question_text: When does an authorized emergency vehicle gain priority over surrounding traffic?
sec10-card-r09.teaching_text: Scanning mirrors regularly and keeping cabin audio reasonable helps you spot silent strobes or distant sirens early.

sec10-card-r10.question_text: How must you position your car for a moving emergency vehicle, and when may opposing traffic keep moving?
sec10-card-r10.teaching_text: Stopping clear of intersections leaves turn paths open while a physical median barrier separates opposing traffic safely.

sec10-card-r11.question_text: How long must you remain stopped for an emergency vehicle, and what check comes before pulling back out?
sec10-card-r11.teaching_text: Police cruisers, fire engines, and ambulances routinely respond in pairs, catching drivers who pull out after the first rig.

sec13-card-f01.question_text: What kind of roadway does the Nebraska handbook mean when it uses the word interstate?
sec13-card-f01.teaching_text: Controlled ramps replace driveways and cross-street stop signs so multiple lanes carry continuous high-speed flow.

sec13-card-f02.question_text: What must you spot in the nearest traffic lane before pulling onto an interstate?
sec13-card-f02.teaching_text: Sizing up your target opening early lets you time your ramp speed instead of guessing at the merge tip.

sec13-card-f03.question_text: Which pavement-line transition on an entrance ramp marks where you adjust speed, signal, and merge?
sec13-card-f03.teaching_text: Crossing solid gore paint early cuts across ramp separation before lanes align safely.

sec13-card-f04.question_text: How should you manage your speed once cruising on the interstate?
sec13-card-f04.teaching_text: Blending smoothly with traffic flow without exceeding speed signs prevents constant overtaking conflicts.

sec13-card-f05.question_text: Which lane should you normally stay in on an interstate, and what lane habit should you avoid?
sec13-card-f05.teaching_text: Weaving unnecessarily and camping left blocks passing flow and multiplies blind-spot exposure.

sec13-card-f06.question_text: How can you help ramp drivers merge when you are cruising in the right interstate lane?
sec13-card-f06.teaching_text: Opening the right lane when the left lane is clear eliminates side-by-side merge pinches.

sec13-card-f07.question_text: What two steps are mandatory before changing lanes to pass on the interstate?
sec13-card-f07.teaching_text: At freeway speeds, an unseen car in your rear quarter closes gaps in a fraction of a second.

sec13-card-f08.question_text: What must you do if you overshoot your intended interstate exit?
sec13-card-f08.teaching_text: Backing on a freeway shoulder or cutting an emergency crossover puts you into seventy-five-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec13-card-f09.question_text: Is driving across an interstate median ever allowed?
sec13-card-f09.teaching_text: Cutting across grass or cable dividers launches slow tires straight into fast left-lane traffic.

sec13-card-f10.question_text: What minimum speed does the Nebraska manual list for interstate travel?
sec13-card-f10.teaching_text: Exam questions test forty miles per hour because slower vehicles create severe closing-speed rear-end hazards.

sec13-card-f11.question_text: At least how far ahead of an interstate exit should you signal and move into the proper exit lane?
sec13-card-f11.teaching_text: Lining up a full mile early prevents panicked last-second dives across multiple freeway lanes.

sec13-card-f12.question_text: When should you start slowing for an interstate exit, and what sign on the ramp must you check?
sec13-card-f12.teaching_text: Waiting until the deceleration lane keeps main lanes moving, while ramp speed signs prevent rollover entries on tight loops.

sec13-card-f13.question_text: What two roadway changes must you watch for right after leaving an interstate?
sec13-card-f13.teaching_text: After miles of divided one-way travel, drivers easily forget oncoming traffic and slower local speed limits.

sec13-card-f14.question_text: Between which daily landmarks must your headlights stay turned on?
sec13-card-f14.teaching_text: Every minute between sunset and sunrise demands full front and rear lighting on Nebraska roads.

sec13-card-f15.question_text: Which lights should you switch on as daylight fades, and what is the rule on driving with parking lamps alone?
sec13-card-f15.teaching_text: Parking bulbs are unlawful while moving because only real low beams make your approaching car visible at dusk.

sec13-card-f16.question_text: When must you switch off auxiliary driving lamps while meeting or following other vehicles?
sec13-card-f16.teaching_text: Extra driving lights blind oncoming eyes and mirrors just as badly as high beams if left burning.

sec13-card-f17.question_text: How do you know whether your nighttime cruising speed is safe for your headlights?
sec13-card-f17.teaching_text: Driving too fast to stop within your lit beam zone leaves zero chance to avoid dark road hazards.

sec13-card-f18.question_text: Where should you use high beams, and what two situations require dimming them?
sec13-card-f18.teaching_text: High beams help on open highways, while dimming for oncoming cars and within two hundred feet stops glare.

sec13-card-f19.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes if an oncoming vehicle's bright headlights start blinding you?
sec13-card-f19.teaching_text: Tracking the white fog line preserves your night vision while keeping your tires safely inside your lane.

sec13-card-f20.question_text: What glass-care step and eye habit prevent night-vision fatigue behind the wheel?
sec13-card-f20.teaching_text: Interior film scatters glare across the glass, and staring fixed into the beam pool hypnotizes tired eyes.

sec13-card-f21.question_text: How should you adjust speed in rain, and what happens physically during hydroplaning?
sec13-card-f21.teaching_text: Slowing matches reduced wet grip before water wedges beneath tread and lifts rubber off the road.

sec13-card-f22.question_text: What three adjustments help maintain control and visibility during rainy driving?
sec13-card-f22.teaching_text: Cruise control can spin wet tires on puddles, while low beams and longer gaps add stopping buffer.

sec13-card-f23.question_text: What must you do whenever water covers a roadway ahead?
sec13-card-f23.teaching_text: Gambling on crossing standing water strands drivers every storm when a quick detour takes minutes.

sec13-card-f24.question_text: Why is even shallow-looking floodwater across a road deceptive and dangerous?
sec13-card-f24.teaching_text: Opaque runoff masks collapsed culverts and deep pavement washouts beneath a flat surface.

sec13-card-f25.question_text: What shallow flood depth reaches underneath most passenger cars, stalling engines or spoiling steering?
sec13-card-f25.teaching_text: Half a foot of water floods low intakes and floats small tires enough to kill steering.

sec13-card-f26.question_text: What depth of moving floodwater can sweep away almost any vehicle, including pickups and SUVs?
sec13-card-f26.teaching_text: High clearance will not save a pickup or SUV once two feet of rushing current pushes broadside.

sec13-card-f27.question_text: What should you do if floodwater blocks every route, and when is flood caution extra critical?
sec13-card-f27.teaching_text: Waiting on high ground beats risking dark water at night when washed-out lanes are invisible.

sec13-card-f28.question_text: Which beam setting, speed adjustment, and mindset belong whenever driving in fog?
sec13-card-f28.teaching_text: High beams glare straight back off fog droplets while slower speed keeps hidden tailenders survivable.

sec13-card-f29.question_text: When visibility drops below a quarter mile, which roads does the Nebraska manual advise staying off?
sec13-card-f29.teaching_text: Highways posted at forty miles per hour or higher carry fast closing speeds that dense fog turns into pileups.

sec13-card-f30.question_text: Which vehicles feel strong wind hardest, and when should you brace for sudden steering corrections?
sec13-card-f30.teaching_text: Popping out of wind shelter or passing a semi hits light cars and tall vans with sudden side shoves.

sec13-card-f31.question_text: What weather alerts should you monitor when traveling across windy stretches?
sec13-card-f31.teaching_text: Checking prairie wind advisories early warns you before severe crosswinds threaten open-highway lane stability.

sec13-card-f32.question_text: Which four habits keep your vehicle controllable on snow- or ice-covered roads?
sec13-card-f32.teaching_text: Clean glass lets you spot hazards early so every gas, brake, and steering move stays feather-smooth.

sec13-card-f33.question_text: May you use cruise control on snowy or icy pavement?
sec13-card-f33.teaching_text: Automated throttle keeps feeding power when tires slip on black ice, whipping the car into a spin.

sec13-card-f34.question_text: How should a driver without antilock brakes slow on snow or ice, and why?
sec13-card-f34.teaching_text: Locked skidding tires slide straight ahead regardless of steering angle, whereas pumping keeps wheels rolling.

sec13-card-f35.question_text: How must you use antilock brakes on snowy or icy roads?
sec13-card-f35.teaching_text: Pumping defeats the computer's rapid pulsing that prevents wheel lockup while you steer.

sec13-card-f36.question_text: How much throttle should you apply when climbing a slippery hill?
sec13-card-f36.teaching_text: Too little gas stalls momentum mid-slope, while flooring it spins tires sideways.

sec13-card-f37.question_text: Which calendar dates bound Nebraska's printed studded-tire season?
sec13-card-f37.teaching_text: Permit questions love testing the exact November first to April first window protecting warm-season pavement.

sec13-card-f38.question_text: Why does the manual advise staying off the roads altogether during a blizzard?
sec13-card-f38.teaching_text: Combining near-zero sight, glare ice, and gale winds overwhelms even experienced winter drivers.

sec13-card-r01.question_text: What is the golden survival rule if a blizzard strands your vehicle?
sec13-card-r01.teaching_text: Walking out into blowing whiteout snow causes disorientation and frostbite yards from shelter.

sec13-card-r02.question_text: What ventilation and exhaust checks are mandatory before running the heater sparingly in a snowbound car?
sec13-card-r02.teaching_text: Plugged exhaust snow forces odorless, deadly carbon monoxide into an unventilated cabin within minutes.

sec13-card-r03.question_text: Which exterior and nighttime interior lights help plow and rescue crews spot a stranded vehicle?
sec13-card-r03.teaching_text: Hazard lamps warn snowplows while the tiny interior dome bulb glows after dark without draining the battery fast.

sec13-card-r04.question_text: How should multiple occupants manage rest if stranded together in a storm?
sec13-card-r04.teaching_text: Keeping one person awake watches for rescue lights, drifting exhaust snow, and hypothermia signs.

sec13-card-r05.question_text: What should you do first if your right wheels drop off the pavement onto a low shoulder?
sec13-card-r05.teaching_text: Jerking the wheel right back against a raised asphalt lip slingshots the car head-on into oncoming lanes.

sec13-card-r06.question_text: How should you bring your car back onto the road after stabilizing an edge drop?
sec13-card-r06.teaching_text: Bleeding off speed and checking mirrors lets the tires climb the pavement edge cleanly without whipping sideways.

sec13-card-r07.question_text: What does each category of driver distraction, visual, manual, and cognitive, pull away from driving?
sec13-card-r07.teaching_text: Losing sight, steering grip, or mental focus breaks the chain needed to spot and avoid sudden hazards.

sec13-card-r08.question_text: Which distraction categories can text messaging trigger at the exact same time?
sec13-card-r08.teaching_text: Reading, thumb-typing, and composing a reply pulls eyes, hands, and brain off the road simultaneously.

sec13-card-r09.question_text: What fine range does the Nebraska handbook list for texting and driving?
sec13-card-r09.teaching_text: Escalating repeat fines between two hundred and five hundred dollars back up Nebraska's texting ban.

sec13-card-r10.question_text: Does switching to a hands-free phone call eliminate driver distraction?
sec13-card-r10.teaching_text: Even with ten fingers on the wheel, an absorbing call narrows cognitive awareness and slows reaction time.

sec13-card-r11.question_text: Which common non-phone cabin habits does the handbook flag for distracting drivers?
sec13-card-r11.teaching_text: Reaching to the floorboard, unwrapping food, reading, handling jackets, or hunting playlists steals critical seconds of sight.

sec13-card-r12.question_text: Who else riding inside the vehicle can pull a driver's focus off the road?
sec13-card-r12.teaching_text: Backseat commotion or an unrestrained dog demands attention right when traffic ahead brakes hard.

sec13-card-r13.question_text: How should you prepare children before driving, and what must you do if they need attention en route?
sec13-card-r13.teaching_text: Twisting into the backseat while rolling turns two seconds of parenting into a lane-departure crash.

sec13-card-r14.question_text: How should you handle rowdy passengers, arguments, or upsetting conversations?
sec13-card-r14.teaching_text: Emotional arguments hijack mental focus and trigger unconsciously aggressive throttle and steering inputs.

sec13-card-r15.question_text: How should pets travel inside a vehicle, and where must a pet never sit?
sec13-card-r15.teaching_text: A dog on your lap blocks steering wheel spins and turns airbag deployment into a tragedy.

sec13-card-r16.question_text: Which three dashboard adjustments can pull your focus away from controlling the car?
sec13-card-r16.teaching_text: Tapping GPS addresses or hunting touch-screen menus takes eyes off lane lines just like texting.

sec13-card-r17.question_text: How does browsing mobile internet or checking email behind the wheel affect safety?
sec13-card-r17.teaching_text: Scrolling emails or web pages locks eyes onto tiny text while traffic closes ahead.

sec13-card-r18.question_text: When should you adjust your seat, mirrors, climate controls, and radio?
sec13-card-r18.teaching_text: Dialing in ergonomics and audio before shifting out of Park keeps both hands and eyes dedicated to traffic.

sec13-card-r19.question_text: When should you check messages, and how can passengers help with cabin controls underway?
sec13-card-r19.teaching_text: Handing GPS, radio, and heater tweaks to a front-seat passenger keeps the driver's eyes glued forward.

sec13-card-r20.question_text: When driving solo, what opportunity does the manual suggest using if vehicle controls need adjusting?
sec13-card-r20.teaching_text: Waiting for a routine stop keeps your car stationary while your hand reaches away from the wheel.

sec13-card-r21.question_text: What handheld wireless actions does Nebraska's printed noncommercial rule prohibit while operating a motor vehicle?
sec13-card-r21.teaching_text: Nebraska's statute covers reading a text just as strictly as typing or hitting send while operating.

sec13-card-r22.question_text: What rule governs television screens inside a vehicle on a public road?
sec13-card-r22.teaching_text: Moving video within the driver's sightline pulls involuntary eye glances away from live traffic.

sec13-card-r23.question_text: Which roadside sights commonly lure a driver's eyes away from the lane ahead?
sec13-card-r23.teaching_text: Rubbernecking at crash scenes, work zones, scenery, or house numbers causes classic rear-end chain collisions.

sec13-card-r24.question_text: Which frightening or rude behaviors illustrate aggressive driving in the handbook?
sec13-card-r24.teaching_text: Hostile moves shrink everyone's safety margins and escalate ordinary traffic delays into crashes.

sec13-card-r25.question_text: What emotional state should keep you from driving, and how should you treat other road users?
sec13-card-r25.teaching_text: Cooling off before turning the key prevents road rage and keeps traffic interactions predictable.

sec13-card-r26.question_text: How should you start every trip, and what must you do if drowsiness sets in?
sec13-card-r26.teaching_text: Willpower cannot stop microsleeps at highway speed once fatigue hits behind the wheel.

sec13-card-r27.question_text: How long is the short fatigue-rest nap option described in the Nebraska handbook?
sec13-card-r27.teaching_text: A brief ten-to-twenty-minute rest-area nap restores real mental alertness without leaving deep-sleep grogginess behind.

sec13-card-r28.question_text: What break timing and daily travel hours do the handbook's fatigue tips highlight?
sec13-card-r28.teaching_text: Human body clocks dip naturally midafternoon and overnight when drowsy single-car run-offs peak.

sec13-card-r29.question_text: Which physical and driving clues warn that dangerous fatigue has already set in?
sec13-card-r29.teaching_text: Yawning, missed exits, drifting lanes, or blanking on recent miles means microsleeps are seconds away.

sec13-card-r30.question_text: When traveling with another licensed person, what simple fatigue solution does the handbook mention?
sec13-card-r30.teaching_text: Handing the wheel to a rested companion keeps the trip safe without fighting heavy eyelids.

sec13-card-r31.question_text: What does the manual say about cold air, gum, loud music, caffeine, and energy drinks for fighting drowsiness?
sec13-card-r31.teaching_text: Blasting music or chugging energy drinks masks tiredness briefly before a sudden crash of microsleep.

sec13-card-r32.question_text: May you use phone calls or texting to keep yourself awake behind the wheel?
sec13-card-r32.teaching_text: Stacking phone distraction on top of sleepy reaction times doubles your crash odds instead of curing fatigue.

sec13-card-r33.question_text: In plain terms, what does defensive driving mean?
sec13-card-r33.teaching_text: Anticipating other road users' mistakes early keeps everyday traffic surprises from turning into collisions.

sec13-card-r34.question_text: What minimum look-ahead planning interval does the Nebraska handbook recommend?
sec13-card-r34.teaching_text: Looking ten to fifteen seconds up the road reveals slowing packs and merges while changes stay easy.

sec13-card-r35.question_text: Where should you scan to both sides, including right after an intersection signal turns green?
sec13-card-r35.teaching_text: Red-light runners and late walkers cross right after signal changes when unobservant drivers launch blind.

sec13-card-r36.question_text: At least how often should you check rear traffic, plus before which four situations?
sec13-card-r36.teaching_text: Ten-second mirror sweeps plus checks on lane shifts, backing, braking, and steep hills track tailgaters.

sec13-card-r37.question_text: What exact zone does an over-the-shoulder glance check that mirrors miss?
sec13-card-r37.teaching_text: Direct eye contact beside your rear pillar catches cars hidden outside mirror angles.

sec13-card-r38.question_text: At least how far ahead must you signal before turns, lane changes, freeway entries, or leaving a curb?
sec13-card-r38.teaching_text: One hundred feet gives surrounding drivers time to spot your blinker before your tires cross paint.

sec13-card-r39.question_text: Under what visibility condition and wiper condition must you switch on headlights?
sec13-card-r39.teaching_text: Any rain, mist, or snow needing wipers also shrouds unlit cars from oncoming and following eyes.

sec13-card-r40.question_text: How do a sharp horn blast and brief brake-pedal taps serve different warning jobs?
sec13-card-r40.teaching_text: A sharp horn warns ahead of immediate collision danger, while brake flashes alert drivers behind before slowing.

sec13-card-r41.question_text: Why must you maintain an open space cushion around your vehicle?
sec13-card-r41.teaching_text: Clear room on every side gives you space to brake, steer out, or pass safely when trouble erupts.

sec13-card-r42.question_text: How do you time your following gap with a roadside object, and what count proves you are too close?
sec13-card-r42.teaching_text: Passing the fixed landmark in fewer than three seconds leaves too little dry-road reaction space, and bad conditions need more.

sec13-card-r43.question_text: Starting from Nebraska's three-second minimum gap, how much following time should you add for adverse conditions?
sec13-card-r43.teaching_text: Adding one full second for rain plus another for heavy traffic scales your stopping buffer systematically.

sec13-card-r44.question_text: How do you protect your side cushions and your rear space cushion in traffic?
sec13-card-r44.teaching_text: Leaving room beside oncoming and parked cars while signaling slowdowns early keeps all four sides protected.

sec01-m01.narration_text: Quick check on Nebraska's foundational licensing requirement. Drive public roads, hold license. Keep that core rule sharp as you head into the module quiz.

sec01-m02.narration_text: Let's review the transfer timeline for new Nebraska residents. New resident, thirty days max. Take that thirty-day deadline straight into your module quiz.

sec01-m03.narration_text: Here is the core purpose behind Nebraska's graduated licensing stages. Staged privileges cut teen risk. Carry that staged-safety mindset into the module quiz.

sec01-m04.narration_text: Rapid recap on wireless devices under graduated restrictions. Moving vehicle, zero wireless use. Bring that zero-phone focus into the module quiz.

sec01-m05.narration_text: Quick check on seat-belt rules for permit vehicles. Permit driver, every occupant buckled. Step into the module quiz with every rider buckled.

sec01-m06.narration_text: Let's recap who may ride along on a school permit. School permit, household family only. Take that household-family rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m07.narration_text: Quick review of the early passenger cap on a provisional permit. First six months, one peer. Head into the module quiz with that six-month limit clear.

sec01-m08.narration_text: Here are the only exceptions to the provisional overnight curfew. Midnight curfew allows work, school. Bring those two travel exceptions into the module quiz.

sec01-m09.narration_text: Quick check on what happens if driving restrictions are broken. Break restrictions, risk losing license. Keep those license stakes in mind for the module quiz.

sec01-m10.narration_text: Let's review the under-twenty-one driver-improvement point trigger. Six points, course within three. Take that six-point timeline into the module quiz.

sec01-m11.narration_text: Quick recap on what the school learner permit prepares you for. School learner builds school permit. Jump into the module quiz with that permit path ready.

sec01-m12.narration_text: Let's check the minimum age rule for a school learner permit. Age fourteen minimum, zero early. Bring that birthday rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m13.narration_text: Here is the supervision standard for passenger-car school learners. Licensed supervisor twenty-one beside you. Carry that adjacent-supervisor rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m14.narration_text: Quick review of the required screenings for a school learner permit. School learner needs vision, written. Step into the module quiz with both screenings in mind.

sec01-m15.narration_text: Let's recap how long a school learner permit remains valid. School learner lasts six months. Take that six-month span into the module quiz.

sec01-m16.narration_text: Quick check on the geographic condition for school-permit eligibility. Live or attend outside five-thousand. Head into the module quiz with that population rule sharp.

sec01-m17.narration_text: Let's review where a school-permit holder may drive solo. Nearest direct route, school purposes. Bring that nearest-direct-route rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m18.narration_text: Here is when a school-permit driver may travel at any hour. Anytime alongside licensed adult twenty-one. Carry that adult-supervision rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m19.narration_text: Quick check on the exact minimum age for a school permit. Fourteen years, two months minimum. Take that age milestone straight into the module quiz.

sec01-m20.narration_text: Let's recap the prior-permit holding period before a school permit. Hold learner permit two months. Jump into the module quiz with that two-month rule set.

sec01-m21.narration_text: Quick review of the safety-course path to a school permit. Pass DMV-approved driver-safety course. Bring that approved-course option into the module quiz.

sec01-m22.narration_text: Here is the supervised-hour certification rule for a school permit. Fifty certified hours, adult signature. Take that fifty-hour requirement into the module quiz.

sec01-m23.narration_text: Let's check the nighttime share of school-permit practice hours. Ten hours sunset to sunrise. Step into the module quiz with those ten night hours clear.

sec01-m24.narration_text: Quick recap on how an approved safety course affects school-permit testing. Approved course waives written, drive. Head into the module quiz with those waivers ready.

sec01-m25.narration_text: Let's review which screenings remain on the school-permit practice path. Practice log needs vision, drive. Bring that vision-and-drive rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m26.narration_text: Quick check on waiving the written screening for school-permit practice applicants. Valid or year-expired learner waives. Take that one-year expiration window into the module quiz.

sec01-m27.narration_text: Here is the occupant-protection rule for school-permit vehicles. Every school-permit rider properly secured. Carry that every-rider restraint rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m28.narration_text: Let's recap the exact age when a school permit expires. Expires sixteen years, three months. Jump into the module quiz with that expiration age sharp.

sec01-m29.narration_text: Quick review of what a standard learner permit prepares you to earn. Practice toward provisional or operator. Step into the module quiz with both next-step credentials clear.

sec01-m30.narration_text: Let's check early-application and issuance timing for a learner permit. Apply sixty early, issued fifteen. Take that age-fifteen rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m31.narration_text: Here is the penalty for a first graduated wireless-device violation. Two-hundred-dollar fine plus license points. Bring those fine-and-point stakes into the module quiz.

sec01-m32.narration_text: Quick check on the graduated seat-belt violation fine. Unbuckled graduated rider, twenty-five dollars. Head into the module quiz with that dollar penalty set.

sec01-m33.narration_text: Let's review the point penalty for a graduated passenger violation. Extra teen rider, one point. Take that one-point consequence into the module quiz.

sec01-m34.narration_text: Quick recap on points added for a provisional nighttime violation. Provisional curfew violation, one point. Carry that curfew point rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m35.narration_text: Here is what happens on a first underage zero-tolerance offense. Court holds permit thirty days. Step into the module quiz with that thirty-day hold clear.

sec01-m36.narration_text: Let's check when adult drunk-driving laws hit drivers under twenty-one. Point zero eight triggers DWI. Bring that point-zero-eight threshold into the module quiz.

sec01-m37.narration_text: Quick review of eligibility standards for a school learner permit. Meet every school-permit requirement first. Jump into the module quiz with those criteria in mind.

sec01-m38.narration_text: Here is the paper-waiver rule for early safety-course completers. Too young then, paper waiver. Take that waiver requirement straight into the module quiz.

sec01-m39.narration_text: Let's recap adjacent-seat supervision for passenger-car learner drivers. Licensed twenty-one-plus in adjacent seat. Head into the module quiz with that adult-seat rule sharp.

sec01-m40.narration_text: Quick check on prior permits that waive learner written screening. Recent permit waives written test. Bring that one-year window into the module quiz.

sec01-m41.narration_text: Let's review how long a standard learner permit lasts. Standard learner expires one year. Step into the module quiz with that one-year span ready.

sec01-m42.narration_text: Here are the daily hours for unsupervised provisional driving. Solo driving six to midnight. Carry that six-to-midnight window into the module quiz.

sec01-m43.narration_text: Quick recap on allowed overnight trips for solo provisional drivers. Overnight solo, home-work or school. Take those work-and-school limits into the module quiz.

sec01-m44.narration_text: Let's check who unlocks round-the-clock driving on a provisional permit. Parent or twenty-one-plus unlocks anytime. Bring that adult-accompaniment rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m45.narration_text: Quick review of application and issuance timing for a provisional permit. Apply sixty early, issued sixteen. Jump into the module quiz with that age-sixteen rule clear.

sec01-m46.narration_text: Here is the six-month prior-permit rule before provisional licensing. Hold prior permit six months. Take that holding period straight into the module quiz.

sec01-m47.narration_text: Let's check the six-month point cap for provisional applicants. Under three points, six months. Step into the module quiz with that clean-record limit set.

sec01-m48.narration_text: Quick recap on certified hours for the provisional practice path. Fifty hours, ten night, signed. Head into the module quiz with fifty and ten sharp.

sec01-m49.narration_text: Let's review how an approved safety course helps provisional applicants. Safety course waives written, drive. Bring those written-and-drive waivers into the module quiz.

sec01-m50.narration_text: Here are the testing and waiver rules on the provisional practice path. Vision and drive, learner waives. Carry that learner-waiver rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m51.narration_text: Quick check on occupant protection inside a provisional driver's vehicle. Every provisional rider buckled up. Take that every-person restraint rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m52.narration_text: Let's recap which birthday ends a Nebraska provisional permit. Provisional expires on eighteenth birthday. Jump into the module quiz with age eighteen in mind.

sec01-m53.narration_text: Quick review of what vehicles a Class O license covers and excludes. Noncommercial vehicles, no motorcycles, commercial. Step into the module quiz with those vehicle boundaries clear.

sec01-m54.narration_text: Here is the autocycle rule for Class O road testing. Never test in an autocycle. Bring that vehicle restriction into the module quiz.

sec01-m55.narration_text: Let's check the minimum age for a full Nebraska operator license. Minimum operator age is seventeen. Take age seventeen straight into the module quiz.

sec01-m56.narration_text: Quick recap on qualifying for an operator license before age eighteen. Twelve provisional months, under three. Head into the module quiz with that twelve-month standard set.

sec01-m57.narration_text: Let's review the test waivers earned by clean under-eighteen provisional drivers. Clean provisional year waives tests. Carry those written-and-drive waivers into the module quiz.

sec01-m58.narration_text: Here is the waiver rule for provisional holders aged eighteen through twenty-one. Eighteen to twenty-one waives both. Step into the module quiz with that upgrade perk ready.

sec01-m59.narration_text: Quick check on testing for first-time adult operator applicants. Vision, written, drive unless learner. Bring those three required screenings into the module quiz.

sec01-m60.narration_text: Let's recap how a learner permit waives written testing for adults. Valid or year-expired learner waives. Jump into the module quiz with that one-year window sharp.

sec01-m61.narration_text: Quick review of out-of-state transfers for drivers below age eighteen. Under eighteen transfers into provisional. Take that provisional-requirement rule into the module quiz.

sec01-m62.narration_text: Here is what an adult new resident faces with a valid out-of-state card. Vision required, drive staff discretion. Head into the module quiz with vision and discretion clear.

sec01-m63.narration_text: Let's check when an adult new resident must take written screening. Missing or expired triggers written. Bring that missing-or-expired rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m01.narration_text: Quick check on holding a Nebraska driving credential and State ID together. One card only, never both. Bring that single-credential rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m02.narration_text: Let's review how long lawful-status licenses and IDs stay valid. Authorized stay or one year. Take authorized stay or one year into the module quiz.

sec03-m03.narration_text: Here is how out-of-state suspensions or revocations affect Nebraska licensing. Active suspension anywhere blocks licensing. Carry that nationwide sanction rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m04.narration_text: Quick recap on what suspension does to your driving privilege. Suspension temporarily removes driving privilege. Head into the module quiz with temporary removal clear.

sec03-m05.narration_text: Let's check how revocation differs by taking the card for a set period. Revocation takes license, removes privilege. Step into the module quiz with revocation sharp.

sec03-m06.narration_text: Quick review of what actually ends a suspension or revocation. Meet reinstatement rules, pay fees. Bring reinstatement steps and fees into the module quiz.

sec03-m07.narration_text: Here is what court impoundment means for your license. Court holds license, bans driving. Take that court-hold definition into the module quiz.

sec03-m08.narration_text: Let's recap when an officer confiscates a license roadside. Officer seizes license after test. Jump into the module quiz with confiscation clear.

sec03-m09.narration_text: Quick check on how long the temporary license lasts after confiscation. Temporary license lasts fifteen days. Head into the module quiz with fifteen days set.

sec03-m10.narration_text: Here is what happens when that fifteen-day temporary card expires. Revoked unless departmental hearing dismisses. Carry revocation unless dismissed into the module quiz.

sec03-m11.narration_text: Let's review the license consequence of motor-vehicle homicide. Motor-vehicle homicide triggers license loss. Step into the module quiz with those high stakes clear.

sec03-m12.narration_text: Quick recap on repeated traffic tickets across any state. Repeat violations anywhere lose privileges. Bring that interstate violation rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m13.narration_text: Here is how using a vehicle in a crime threatens your license. Vehicle crime brings license loss. Take that license-loss rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m14.narration_text: Let's check how impaired-driving arrests or convictions impact licensing. Impaired arrest, conviction loses license. Jump into the module quiz with zero impaired driving.

sec03-m15.narration_text: Quick review of falsifying or hiding application details. Falsifying application brings license loss. Head into the module quiz with honest paperwork sharp.

sec03-m16.narration_text: Here is the license risk of leaving a crash without giving contact info. Leave crash unrecorded, lose license. Carry that post-crash duty into the module quiz.

sec03-m17.narration_text: Let's recap what happens when citations or court judgments are ignored. Ignore citations anywhere, lose license. Step into the module quiz handling every citation promptly.

sec03-m18.narration_text: Quick check on how alcoholism or drug addiction affects driving privileges. Addiction can remove driving privileges. Bring that fitness-to-drive rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m19.narration_text: Here is the license consequence of fleeing an officer. Fleeing police risks license loss. Take that immediate-stop habit into the module quiz.

sec03-m20.narration_text: Let's review what refusing a chemical test can do to your license. Refuse chemical test, lose license. Jump into the module quiz with implied consent clear.

sec03-m21.narration_text: Quick recap on reckless driving and license loss. Reckless driving risks license loss. Head into the module quiz with controlled driving sharp.

sec03-m22.narration_text: Here is why you should never lend your driver license out. Lend your license, risk loss. Carry that personal-card rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m23.narration_text: Let's check the penalty for sending someone else to take your exam. Proxy test-taker triggers license loss. Step into the module quiz earning your own score.

sec03-m24.narration_text: Quick review of convictions for failing to show insurance proof. No insurance proof risks license. Bring active insurance proof into the module quiz.

sec03-m25.narration_text: Here is how child-support or alimony noncompliance affects licensing. Unpaid support orders risk license. Take that court-order rule into the module quiz.

sec03-m26.narration_text: Let's recap what happens when young drivers skip six-point training. Skip six-point training, lose privileges. Jump into the module quiz with that under-twenty-one rule set.

sec03-m27.narration_text: Quick check on transporting a child while intoxicated. Intoxicated with child loses license. Head into the module quiz with child safety paramount.

sec03-m28.narration_text: Here is the age-sixteen lockout for violating early permit rules. Break permit terms, locked sixteen. Carry that permit-eligibility bar into the module quiz.

sec03-m29.narration_text: Let's review the automatic twelve-point revocation rule. Twelve points revokes six months. Step into the module quiz with twelve points in two years.

sec03-m30.narration_text: Quick recap on what the DMV's point-revocation letter directs. Point letter orders license surrender. Bring mandatory license surrender into the module quiz.

sec03-m31.narration_text: Here are the fine and jail penalties for keeping a revoked card. Five hundred dollars, thirty jail. Take five hundred dollars and thirty days into the module quiz.

sec03-m32.narration_text: Let's check the four-hour training course needed for point reinstatement. Four-hour DMV course, driver pays. Jump into the module quiz with driver-paid training clear.

sec03-m33.narration_text: Quick review of the three-year financial-responsibility tail after point revocation. Maintain proof three post-revocation years. Head into the module quiz with three post-revocation years sharp.

sec03-m34.narration_text: Here is the harsher penalty for a repeat point revocation within five years. Repeat five-year revocation, three years. Carry that three-year revocation into the module quiz.

sec03-m35.narration_text: Let's recap the twelve-point hit from motor-vehicle homicide. Motor-vehicle homicide adds twelve points. Step into the module quiz with that maximum point count.

sec03-m36.narration_text: Quick check on points assigned to a third drunk-driving offense. Third drunk-driving adds twelve points. Bring twelve points straight into the module quiz.

sec03-m37.narration_text: Here is the point penalty for failing to report a crash. Unreported crash adds six points. Take six points into the module quiz.

sec03-m38.narration_text: Let's review points added for failing to help after a crash. Refusing crash aid, six points. Jump into the module quiz with six points clear.

sec03-m39.narration_text: Quick recap on points carried by driving under the influence. Driving under influence, six points. Head into the module quiz with six impaired-driving points set.

sec03-m40.narration_text: Here is the point count for willful reckless driving. Willful reckless carries six points. Carry six points for willful recklessness into the module quiz.

sec03-m41.narration_text: Let's check the points assessed for leaving a crash scene. Leaving crash scene, six points. Step into the module quiz with six hit-and-run points.

sec03-m42.narration_text: Quick review of standard reckless driving on the point scale. Reckless driving carries five points. Bring five points into the module quiz.

sec03-m43.narration_text: Here is the point penalty for careless driving. Careless driving carries four points. Take four careless-driving points into the module quiz.

sec03-m44.narration_text: Let's recap the point hit when failing to yield injures a pedestrian. Pedestrian injury failure, four points. Jump into the module quiz with four points sharp.

sec03-m45.narration_text: Quick check on points for handheld texting while driving. Handheld texting carries three points. Head into the module quiz with three texting points clear.

sec03-m46.narration_text: Here is the point value assigned to negligent driving. Negligent driving carries three points. Carry three negligent-driving points into the module quiz.

sec03-m47.narration_text: Let's review the points for illegally passing a stopped school bus. Illegal bus pass, three points. Step into the module quiz with three bus-safety points.

sec03-m48.narration_text: Quick recap on failing to yield to an uninjured pedestrian. Non-injury pedestrian yield, two points. Bring two crosswalk points into the module quiz.

sec03-m49.narration_text: Here is the point penalty for unlawfully blocking your view. Blocked driver view, one point. Take one clear-sightline point into the module quiz.

sec03-m50.narration_text: Let's check the point-schedule count for refusing an alcohol test. Alcohol-test refusal carries one point. Jump into the module quiz with that one-point rule set.

sec03-m51.narration_text: Quick review of the point hit for a child-restraint violation. Child-restraint violation adds one point. Head into the module quiz with one child-restraint point.

sec03-m52.narration_text: Here is the insurer certification form used after point revocation. Insurer files Form SR-twenty-two. Carry Form SR-twenty-two into the module quiz.

sec03-m53.narration_text: Let's recap financial-responsibility proof after court-ordered revocation. Court revocation uses Form SR-twenty-two. Step into the module quiz with Form SR-twenty-two sharp.

sec03-m54.narration_text: Quick check on the three citations that carry zero points. Parking, muffler, forgot wallet license. Bring parking, muffler, and forgotten cards into the module quiz.

sec03-m55.narration_text: Here is how long a post-holdoff sobriety permit stays valid. Remaining portion of one-year revocation. Take the remaining one-year balance into the module quiz.

sec03-m56.narration_text: Let's review the span of a later-offense interlock permit. Lasts remaining one-year revocation balance. Jump into the module quiz with that remaining revocation balance.

sec03-m57.narration_text: Quick recap on interlock permit length after chemical-test refusal. Covers remaining one-year revocation. Head into the module quiz with the remaining year clear.

sec03-m58.narration_text: Here is the criminal class for fleeing over moving traffic violations. Class I misdemeanor, possible revocation. Carry Class I misdemeanor and revocation into the module quiz.

sec03-m59.narration_text: Let's check the thirty-day lockout for unlicensed juveniles. Unlicensed youth barred thirty days. Step into the module quiz with that juvenile rule ready.

sec03-m60.narration_text: Quick review of one-to-five-over speeding on modern citations. One through five adds zero. Bring zero points into the module quiz.

sec03-m61.narration_text: Here is the city speeding bracket for six through ten over. City six-to-ten over, two points. Take two city points into the module quiz.

sec03-m62.narration_text: Let's recap city speeding from more than ten through thirty-five over. City over-ten through thirty-five, three. Jump into the module quiz with three city points sharp.

sec03-m63.narration_text: Quick check on speeding past thirty-five over anywhere in Nebraska. Over thirty-five adds four points. Head into the module quiz with four points set.

sec03-m64.narration_text: Here is the rural speeding bracket for six through ten over. Outside city six-to-ten, one point. Carry one rural point into the module quiz.
